facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: aaPanel includes no CPU, RAM, server disk, or persistent volume; these come from the user's server provider.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: The quick-start guide lists a minimum of 1 CPU core, 512 MB RAM, and 1 GB storage for aaPanel itself.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: aaPanel has no vendor CPU-hour, RAM-hour, request, egress, or disk meters for self-hosted software.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: The Free edition is a permanent $0 software edition, not a temporary hosted trial.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free includes unlimited website creation and unlimited SSL certificates, plus website, database, FTP, Docker, and file management.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free includes 100+ apps and extensions, but the pricing page does not give a complete item list or a numeric limit on which can be installed.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: No free-software inactivity timer, automatic suspension, or free-account resource reset is published; the server remains user managed.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: aaPanel itself includes no vendor outbound-data allowance or per-GB transfer rate.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Cloudflare integration is listed as included in Free, but Cloudflare service limits and charges remain governed by Cloudflare's own terms and plan.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: aaPanel does not sell build minutes or hosted build agents; the customer builds on their server or another CI provider.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Git deployment can pull a chosen branch and run a webhook-triggered deployment script, but no build-minute cap or deployment count is published.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: The Go project tool expects a compiled binary; it does not deploy Go source code.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Server, public IP, storage, bandwidth, domain, and optional CDN charges are outside aaPanel's software fee.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Remote backup destinations such as S3, Google Cloud Storage, Google Drive, FTP, and Cloudflare R2 need separate provider accounts and may have their own charges.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: aaPanel publishes no account-wide spending cap or automatic pause because it does not bill the server's infrastructure.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: The panel can show resource use and send configured alarms, but no vendor bill threshold or guaranteed alert delay is published.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: aaPanel does not sleep or scale a hosted service; server uptime and scaling are controlled by the operator and infrastructure provider.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Pro markets multi-server management and file sync/database replication, but no automatic request-driven autoscaling policy is published.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: There is no aaPanel request-count or app execution-time allowance; user server capacity and configured web server/app limits apply.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Node project settings include a configurable process memory limit; the example uses 1024 MB, not a universal plan cap.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Pro has a 14-day trial with no credit card and no charge during the trial, according to the download page.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The Free edition download requires a new Linux server and root SSH access; the page does not require a sales account to install the free panel.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Buyer-country eligibility, identity checks, and accepted payment methods are not specified on the public pricing page.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The public plan card states USD prices, while the dynamic order page shows a local-currency payment option; exact supported currencies and country rules are not readable there.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: The custom license permits use of aaPanel for-profit or non-profit projects.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: The same license bars using the source to operate a service of the same type and says modified source code may not be publicly released under its personal-use clause.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: aaPanel is installed on a Linux server that the user supplies; aaPanel does not rent the VM or host the app for the user.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: The panel provides browser, terminal, and API-based server administration for websites, databases, files, Docker, monitoring, and system security.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: aaPanel can be run in an official Docker image, but the host server and container storage remain customer supplied.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: The free panel can manage static and PHP sites, WordPress, domains, FTP, databases, and SSL certificates.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: The panel has separate project tools for Node.js, Python, Go binaries, reverse-proxy apps, and Docker workloads.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: aaPanel also includes mail and DNS administration; those features overlap with separate mail, DNS, database, and VPS directory categories.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: aaPanel publishes no vendor compute region or delivery edge; the user chooses a server provider and its location.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Official requirements document Linux distributions, not a list of countries or server regions where aaPanel's software is available.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: The download page lists Nginx, Apache, OpenLiteSpeed, PHP, MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis/Memcached, Node.js, Python, Go, and Docker options.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: PHP versions shown by the download page span 5.3–8.5; the page does not explain support lifecycle for each version.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: The Node project guide offers a Node version manager and PM2 or default projects; the Python guide supports virtual environments and Django, Flask, and FastAPI examples.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Go projects must be supplied as compiled binaries; Docker projects use user-supplied or catalogued images and host resources.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: The current quick-start guide lists supported OS families but does not identify supported CPU architectures; the repository README lists an older subset and also does not settle architecture.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Python projects are documented for Django, Flask, and FastAPI, with uWSGI, Gunicorn, and custom start commands.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Node projects can run a package script or custom command; domains are mapped through Nginx or Apache reverse proxy.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: The PHP project manager lists one-click deployment for apps such as Drupal, Joomla, Laravel, OpenCart, and PrestaShop; no exhaustive version or framework compatibility matrix is published.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: aaPanel accepts website files through its file manager/editor, local upload, FTP/SFTP, Git, and Docker workflows.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Git website deployment supports GitHub/GitLab repository URLs, branch selection, webhooks, deployment scripts, and one-click rollback in the product page.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: The panel's Node project manager can pull Git projects; its Go project expects a binary; Python projects are created from server files and selected virtual environments.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: The official API can manage panel functions after API access is enabled and the caller IP is added to an allowlist.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Node projects run as processes under PM2 or the default project manager and can be started, stopped, and restarted from the panel.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Python, Go, proxy, and Docker apps can run as server processes or containers configured by the operator; no managed worker service is included.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: The Cron tool can run shell commands and scheduled backups on daily, weekly, monthly, hourly, minute, or second-based cycles.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: aaPanel manages web-server ports and supports mapping project domains through Nginx or Apache to application ports.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: The system firewall UI documents TCP, UDP, inbound/outbound directions, port ranges, allow/deny rules, and source-IP filters.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: WebSocket, streaming, long-lived connection timeouts, fixed outbound IP, and private-network features are not stated as aaPanel service guarantees.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Websites, databases, Docker volumes, and panel state are stored on the user's server or mounted storage.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: aaPanel provides a file manager and site directory controls, but does not sell persistent disk capacity.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Whether app data survives a redeploy or container replacement depends on the user's Docker volumes and deployment configuration.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: aaPanel can install/manage MySQL and MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Redis on the user's server; these are not aaPanel-managed cloud databases.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: The docs also expose a SQL Server management page, but do not establish that it is bundled as a managed service or included in every edition.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Built-in database backup, import, restore, download, and per-database access permissions are documented.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: aaPanel does not include a vendor-managed queue, object store, or authentication service in the Free or Pro panel price.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: The user connects their own domain to the server; aaPanel does not register or include a domain name.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Free includes unlimited SSL certificates; the website guide documents Let's Encrypt issue, renewal, force HTTPS, and manual certificate upload.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Wildcard certificates require DNS validation; the guide says manually adding TXT records does not automatically renew the certificate.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: The panel itself uses a self-signed certificate by default and can be configured with a trusted certificate or Let's Encrypt.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Git deployment supports branch pull, webhook deployment, logs, and a one-click rollback claim on the official product page.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Pro WordPress tools advertise staging, cloning, and bulk site operations; no universal preview-deployment environment for arbitrary app types is documented.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: The panel can create server snapshots only through an external cloud provider; the restore guide recommends a provider snapshot before risky restores.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: A documented aaPanel migration can install the panel on a target server and restore backups; the guide warns to verify restored files, extensions, and data.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: The free panel shows CPU, memory, disk, network and service status and exposes website access/error logs.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: The Node, Go, Git, and backup tools expose project, deployment, or task logs for troubleshooting.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Pro adds website analytics and historical traffic reports; no plan-wide data-retention period was published.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: The panel supports password strength rules, Google Authenticator, BasicAuth, authorized IPs, a hidden security path, domain binding, and panel-port changes.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: The API can be enabled with a caller-IP allowlist; the docs warn access is denied when the IP is not on the list.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Pro advertises unlimited team members; the Free page does not publish a team-user count.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: A July 31, 2026 forum report says the built-in terminal displayed/stored SSH private keys and passwords in plain text; aaPanel staff replied that it was safe and recommended BasicAuth.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: On December 5, 2025 a forum user reported a compromised server after an alleged WordPress-plugin breach and attributed kernel panics to a buffer overflow in Pro's tampercore module; aaPanel staff replied that it had contacted the user privately.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: The current quick-start guide lists Ubuntu 22, 24, 26; Debian 11–13; CentOS 9/10; AlmaLinux 8–10; and Rocky Linux 8–10, with Ubuntu 22 recommended.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: The download page gives a broader OS range in its compatibility list, including Ubuntu 18.04–26.04 and Debian 9–13, while the quick-start guide starts Ubuntu at 22 and Debian at 11.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: The minimum panel hardware is 1 CPU core, 512 MB RAM, and 1 GB disk; the download page recommends 1 CPU core and 1 GB RAM.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Install requires SSH access and root privileges on a fresh supported Linux server; the README warns against preinstalled Apache, Nginx, PHP, or MySQL stacks.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: The operator maintains OS and app updates, firewall/security-group rules, domain/DNS, mail delivery, storage, database recovery, and remote backup credentials.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: aaPanel includes system firewall, brute-force protection, panel login controls, website WAF and anti-tamper options; WAF Pro and several advanced tools are paid features.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: If the panel UI is unavailable, the web/database services can continue running; the Settings guide says closing only the panel does not stop those services.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: aaPanel's privacy policy identifies the Website as the service and covers account/email and website usage data; it does not give a product-specific data-processing agreement for self-hosted panel data.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The privacy policy says personal data may be processed at company offices or other processor locations, including outside the user's jurisdiction; no fixed storage country or subprocessor list is given.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The license says aaPanel must not collect user data or remotely control a user panel without permission, but the pages do not provide a complete current inventory of product telemetry or plugin data flows.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: An August–September 2026 aaPanel forum thread reports that malware scanning uploaded file contents to a remote endpoint. aaPanel staff said it was being checked/optimized; the user later reported automatic scanning no longer used the upload after panel repair, but manually triggered file checks still sent file contents.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: aaPanel provides site, database, directory, and panel backup/restore controls, with configurable retention counts.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Scheduled backups can target local disk, FTP, Google Drive, Google Cloud Storage, or AWS S3; the storage plugin must be installed/configured.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: The documentation includes Cloudflare R2 integration as a remote backup destination.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: A restore can overwrite existing data; aaPanel advises taking a server snapshot first and checking data integrity after restore.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Site and database backups can be downloaded or restored on a different aaPanel server; migration docs describe installing the panel on the target and restoring.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Git-based sites retain their source in the user's repository; aaPanel is not the only copy of the source if the user maintains that repository.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: The listed product is aaPanel, the international web-based Linux server control panel at aapanel.com.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: The About and Privacy pages name AAPANEL LIMITED as the company and give a Hong Kong address.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: The repository license names Dongguan Baita Network Technology Co., Ltd. as the body behind aaPanel; the public pages checked do not explain how that entity relates to AAPANEL LIMITED.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: The international website calls the software aaPanel, while its source tree includes BTPanel/BT-Panel and the installer identifies BT-SOFT; the official pages checked do not define the international aaPanel/BT Panel relationship.

facts.label: Operating and signup status

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: GitHub's latest tagged release page shows aaPanel v7.65.0, labeled January 22 without a year, and 11 commits to master since the release.

facts.label: Operating and signup status

facts.value: aaPanel does not promise uptime for the user's server or application; the custom license disclaims warranties.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: No aaPanel status page was linked from the product, pricing, or documentation pages checked; the candidate status.aapanel.com page did not open.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: The October 2026 PHP security notice is an upstream runtime issue; aaPanel published update instructions, but no aaPanel software SLA or service-credit terms accompany it.

facts.value: Free support channels include documentation, community forum, email, Telegram/Discord, and GitHub issues.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Pro pricing includes priority support, but the public plan page does not give a response-time or availability target.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: No linked general product Terms of Service page was found on the pricing or About page; candidate terms-of-service URLs failed to open, while the repository license is readable.

facts.value: The repository license title is exactly “AAPANEL Open Source License Agreement”; it is a custom agreement, not a standard SPDX license identifier.

facts.value: The agreement permits profitable and non-profit use of aaPanel for the user's own projects.

facts.value: The agreement says code must remain readable except paid plugins, restricts public release of modified source under its personal-use clause, prohibits undermining the commercial authorization mechanism, and allows publishing or integrating aaPanel only without changing its source.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: The license disclaims express and implied warranties and selects PRC law and courts in Dongguan for disputes.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: The official About/Privacy pages name AAPANEL LIMITED, while the license names Dongguan Baita Network Technology Co., Ltd.; the relationship is not explained.

facts.value: Rented Linux virtual machines on Akamai Cloud. Akamai runs the underlying infrastructure; the customer chooses and maintains the guest OS, software stack, app configuration, patches, and release process. Manage through Cloud Manager, Linode CLI, or API.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs

facts.label: Network and connection support

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow

facts.label: Access and secret handling

facts.value: Not applicable: Akamai operates the Cloud Compute infrastructure; customers maintain the guest OS and apps on the rented VM.

facts.value: New billing docs describe a first-use three-month CU trial, not an indefinite repeating FC compute allowance; the public pricing page still advertises 1 million requests and 400000 GB-s free monthly.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Function Compute Internet outbound traffic is billed separately through Cloud Data Transfer (CDT), including responses, function Internet requests and CDN origin traffic.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: CDT: account-level 220 GB/month free BGP transfer, split 20 GB mainland China and 200 GB outside mainland China; no rollover.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: CDT Singapore, USD/GB, after applicable free quota: 0–10 TB 0.100; 10–50 TB 0.070; 50–150 TB 0.065; over 150 TB 0.055.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: The FC transfer-change notice still states 10 GB monthly free traffic, while the newer CDT tariff states 220 GB split by geography.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: ZIP/folder upload, OSS package input and custom runtime startup commands supported; build/dependencies can run locally with Serverless Devs.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Custom container deployments require Alibaba Cloud Container Registry images in the same account and region; linux/amd64 builds required.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: ZIP/JAR upload quota: Singapore and listed larger-quota regions 500 MB; other regions 100 MB. Default compressed CPU image quota 10 GB.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: A general FC-hosted build-minute allowance, price, build-machine size or build-concurrency limit was not established.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: OSS, NAS and Simple Log Service are separate products with separate billing.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Custom-domain HTTPS uses a selected Alibaba certificate or manually uploaded certificate/key; certificate purchase and renewal may add separate work/cost.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: SLS logs are enabled by default for newly created functions; turning them off prevents persisted function logs.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Separate SLS pay-by-feature, Singapore/USD: read/write USD 0.045/GB, log indexing USD 0.0875/GB, log storage USD 0.002875/GB-day; table lists 500 MB/month free for each.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Budgets provide actual/forecast alerts; alerts do not restrict resource usage.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Function quotas can limit elastic instances or be set to zero to block invocations; default account limit 300 instances/region, function-level allocations share up to 90%.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Low balance alerts notify only; billing can continue during a grace period, and separate resources must be released to stop their charges.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Elastic minimum 0 scales from zero and avoids idle instance charges when not invoked; minimum at least 1 keeps billable warm capacity.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Scheduled, metric-based and dynamic elastic policies supported; regional speed/count limits can return HTTP 429 throttling.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Instance concurrency configurable 1–200; default maximum 300 instances/account/region, subject to actual Quota Center value.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: CPU timeout ceiling 86400 s; initializer 300 s; PreStop 90 s; synchronous payload 32 MB; asynchronous payload 128 KB, adjustable up to 256 KB.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Web HTTP headers 8 KB, path/query 4 KB, synchronous body 32 MB; response headers 8 KB. Shared-responsibility page instead lists 4 KB headers and 16 MB body.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Singapore regional compute-node default 300 vCPU/600 GB; scale-out 180 vCPU and 360 GB per minute after burst capacity.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: First-use trial: 150000 CU per period, three consecutive monthly periods; primary account and RAM users share it; excess automatically billed.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Paid service ordering and most paid-product trials require security authentication and payment information; individual/enterprise accounts available. Mainland-China servers also require photo ID or corporate registration verification.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Bank cards, Alipay CN/PayPal wallets and eligible bank transfers are described; available methods depend on the contracting entity.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Registration country cannot be changed and determines billing currency/tax; verification phone number must match that country.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: International/country sanctions, import/export, re-export and strategic-goods controls must be followed; access may be restricted or suspended for violations.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Commercial/end-user application use is contemplated; no CPU pay-as-you-go non-commercial-only restriction found.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Prohibitions include unlawful or fraudulent use, infringement, virtual-currency mining, pornography, discriminatory content, malware and unauthorized network access.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Fully managed, event-driven function execution; provider supplies infrastructure, customer uploads application code and configuration.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Event functions, HTTP web applications, scheduled/processing tasks and GPU workloads; arbitrary application code through supported runtimes or custom containers.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Outside mainland China: Hong Kong, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta, Bangkok, Tokyo, Seoul, Frankfurt, London, Virginia, Silicon Valley and Riyadh partner region.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Mainland public regions include Hangzhou, Shanghai, Qingdao, Beijing, Zhangjiakou, Hohhot, Ulanqab, Shenzhen and Chengdu.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Built-in Node.js, Python, PHP, Java, .NET and Go runtimes; Linux/x86_64 entries and Debian 9/10/11/12 custom runtime choices are documented.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Deprecation phase 1 blocks new functions; phase 2 blocks create/update; runtime guide says deprecated-runtime invocations remain possible, without security patches/support.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Shared-responsibility guide says community-EOL runtimes stop executing; runtime lifecycle guide says deprecated invocations are not blocked.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Web functions run an HTTP server; official Flask example listens on 0.0.0.0:9000 and forwards requests/responses.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Console ZIP/folder upload, OSS package and custom container deployment; Serverless Devs supports local build/debug/deploy and API-oriented automation.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Time triggers support intervals, selected schedules and cron; cron defaults to UTC and supports explicit CRON_TZ time zones.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Execution may last up to 86400 seconds; asynchronous processing is supported, but execution after the handler returns is not guaranteed.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: HTTP web functions and WebSocket triggers supported; WebSocket connection closes when the execution timeout is reached.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Public Internet egress enabled by default; VPC access must be configured. Private database/NAS access needs network and execution-role permissions.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Temporary disk is instance-local and not durable/shared; NAS and OSS support persistent files; layers are read-only dependency archives.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Active/light-sleep temporary disk up to 10 GB is described as free; deep-sleep/snapshot storage has separate billing.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Managed RDS PostgreSQL can be reached from FC through a same-region VPC and a database whitelist.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Separate RDS PostgreSQL Serverless, Singapore/USD: USD 0.0796/RCU-hour and USD 0.0004/provisioned-GB-hour.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: RDS PostgreSQL Serverless: 1 RCU = 1 vCPU + 2 GB memory; supported storage starts at 20 GB; automatic storage growth cannot be disabled.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Custom standard/wildcard domains supported; Chinese domain names unsupported. Mainland hosting requires ICP filing; Hong Kong/overseas functions do not.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: HTTPS can use a selected cloud certificate or manually uploaded PEM certificate/key; HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect configurable.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Default aliyuncs.com function URL forces Content-Disposition: attachment; use a custom domain for ordinary browser-rendered pages.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Publish immutable versions and point aliases at versions; aliases support rollback and weighted canary traffic.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Versions snapshot function code/configuration; LATEST remains the editable version.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Web/GPU functions support periodic instance health checks; unhealthy instances stop receiving requests.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: No automatic pull-request preview environment guarantee established.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: SLS persists function execution logs and request/instance metrics; default-enabled log configuration can be disabled.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: SLS LogStore retention defaults to 30 days when created through its documented workflow; billing mode and retention can be configured.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: CloudMonitor FC metrics query window/retention 31 days, aggregation 60 seconds; metrics include requests, errors, latency, memory and concurrency.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Per-function environment variables encrypted at rest with AES-256 and decrypted into the runtime; total variable size 4 KB.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: RAM users and short-lived STS credentials supported; temporary code-package/layer download URLs must be protected.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: No self-host hardware/OS requirements for the managed FC service.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: Resource region is chosen at creation and cannot be changed in place.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: DPA: customer selects the storage region; any processing transfer outside it must comply with applicable data-protection law, including restricted-transfer safeguards.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: Provider privacy policy permits data sharing for contracting/support and processing across jurisdictions; country-specific addenda apply.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: FC temporary instance files are not a durable backup. Version recovery does not protect separate NAS/OSS/database state.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Separate RDS PostgreSQL cloud-disk snapshots: choose backup days and 7–730-day retention, default 7; Basic Edition lacks log-backup/PITR support.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: RDS cloud-disk backup free quota 200% of instance storage; excess snapshot storage USD 0.00004/GB per hour in the generic international table.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Retain/download function packages and use Serverless Devs to synchronize cloud resources locally; custom images/code can be redeployed elsewhere with adaptations.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: RDS backups can restore to another instance and backup downloads are separately billed; database export/recovery is distinct from function rollback.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Alibaba Cloud Function Compute (FC), on the Alibaba Cloud international website; contracting entity varies with the customer's registered billing jurisdiction.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Active public offer; FC 3.0 is recommended for new projects, while FC 2.0 has separate existing-user documentation.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Funcraft is no longer maintained; Serverless Devs is its documented successor.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: International paid FC SLA 99.95% monthly; five-minute error-rate intervals; free/trial services excluded.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Credits: 10% for 99.00%–<99.95%, 25% for 95.00%–<99.00%, 100% below 95.00%; claim within 30 days after billing month.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Public Alibaba Cloud Health Status dashboard offers region/product status and historical events.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Basic support includes free self-help and limited trial technical/ticket services; Developer, Business and Enterprise are separate support tiers.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Technical support tickets, sales contact and documentation channels are public; a plan-specific response promise was not established.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Optional Developer support: USD 19.99, charged immediately upon purchase; automatic renewal can be selected.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Optional Business support: starting from USD 100, with charges based on cloud-product usage.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Optional Enterprise support: starting from USD 8000; consult the business manager for details.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: Proprietary hosted service under international Membership Agreement, Product Terms, Terms of Use, DPA and Payment/Tax Terms.

facts.value: €6/month on monthly payment; €5/month equivalent on annual payment. 50 GB disk, 1 GB RAM, CPU 1, 7 rolling backup days; VAT excluded.

facts.label: Medium paid plan
facts.value: €22/month on monthly payment; €20/month equivalent on annual payment. 100 GB disk, 2 GB RAM, CPU 2, 20 rolling backup days; VAT excluded.

facts.label: Large paid plan
facts.value: €55/month on monthly payment; €50/month equivalent on annual payment. 200 GB disk, 4 GB RAM, CPU 4, 20 rolling backup days; VAT excluded.

facts.label: X-Large paid plan
facts.value: €165/month on monthly payment; €150/month equivalent on annual payment. 500 GB disk, 8 GB RAM, CPU 8, 30 rolling backup days; VAT excluded.

facts.label: Cheapest commercial entry / renewal price
facts.value: Small monthly is €6 excluding VAT; no compulsory per-seat/base licence fee is stated in its published account tariff. Listed pricing is ordinary subscription pricing, separate from the 30-day trial.

facts.label: Annual upfront equivalents — our calculation
facts.value: Small €60/year; Medium €240/year; Large €600/year; X-Large €1,800/year, excluding VAT, calculated as 12 × displayed annual-payment monthly equivalent.

facts.label: Private Cloud entry / upfront
facts.value: Documented Max example: €409/month monthly payment or €369/month equivalent annual payment; first monthly invoice covers three months. No setup fee; avoiding the three-month commitment adds 20% for the first three months.

facts.label: Contract term / cancellation
facts.value: Shared special terms set one month or one year plus initialization, automatic same-period renewal, and registered notice at least one month before anniversary. Dedicated terms set three months or one year plus installation.

facts.label: Plan changes / refunds
facts.value: Upgrade/downgrade can generate pro-rata credit to the prepaid account; credit pays future invoices. Early account deletion/server decommission does not receive a refund; free-pack downgrade requires support review.

facts.label: Free resources
facts.value: 1 GB total disk, 256 MB RAM, CPU 1/4; three rolling backup days.

facts.label: Public compute tenancy / resource scope
facts.value: Public accounts share servers with hundreds of users. Accounts use cgroup isolation; spare resources can be temporarily redistributed for peaks. Sites within an account share resources.

facts.label: Max example hardware
facts.value: 8 AMD EPYC cores, 16 GB RAM, SSD 1 TB NVMe with RAID1; 10 TB/month traffic on a 1 Gbps link.

facts.label: OS / architecture
facts.value: Provider servers run Debian Linux x64; shared account isolation uses cgroups. User programs may install dependencies within the account, without root/sudo.

facts.label: Billing model
facts.value: Recurring account/server subscription; ordinary public pricing lists monthly or annual plans, rather than per-request, function-duration or build-minute meters.

facts.label: Missing usage tariff details
facts.value: No public numeric request, CPU-second, build-minute, storage-overage or Public Cloud per-GB transfer tariff found in checked plan/pricing and terms.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: €0 repeating plan without stated time expiry, restricted to personal/non-profit use; website address limited to the account's alwaysdata.net address. Services and database-only hosting are prohibited.

facts.label: Free inactivity / deletion
facts.value: Admin login required every 120 days for profiles younger than one year, every six months for profiles aged 1–4 years, and annually thereafter. Inactivity suspends; profile deletion follows 30 days after suspension unless corrected.

facts.label: Free marketing scope disagreement
facts.value: Homepage says Free has all Plus features, while tariff, suspension and Services docs explicitly exclude profitable use, custom website domains and background Services.

facts.label: Public transfer allowance
facts.value: Public Cloud plan's numeric monthly traffic allowance and internal app/database transfer classification were not established from public pricing/docs.

facts.label: Contractual traffic overage
facts.value: Shared and dedicated terms provide Order-Form traffic volume, separate invoicing when exceeded, no carry-forward of unused volume, and potential suspension if extra traffic is refused/unpaid.

facts.label: Max transfer inclusion
facts.value: Published single-server Max example includes 10 TB/month at 1 Gbps; additional traffic is offered in 1-TB slots, with no slot price on the page.

facts.label: Build/deploy method
facts.value: Documented React workflow builds locally with npm run build and uploads artifacts by rsync/SSH. Native Node apps install dependencies/run commands through account tools.

facts.label: Build limits / fee schedule
facts.value: No managed build-minute allocation, build-machine size, matrix/concurrency cap or deployment-count/preview-build tariff published in checked workflow/pricing docs.

facts.label: Included platform components
facts.value: Paid plans include unlimited site/database/mailbox counts within resources, SSH, automatic HTTPS and daily retained backups; backup files do not consume account disk quota.

facts.label: Private intervention charges
facts.value: CPU upgrade €400, disk upgrade €400, RAM change €200, GPU addition €200, disk addition €200 excluding VAT; simultaneous changes capped at €600; Gold doubles rates/cap to €1,200.

facts.label: Monitoring / urgency extras
facts.value: Private Cloud probe €10/month; application-caused probe work and out-of-guarantee urgent tickets €100 excluding VAT. An urgent request itself accepts the latter charge without prior quote.

facts.label: Other contractual costs
facts.value: Dedicated HTTP/SMTP IPs are subscription items; amount not found in checked pages. Standard terms section 7.5 requires risk insurance related to website/service operation; no premium is published.

facts.label: Invoice alerts / prepaid balance
facts.value: Negative prepaid balance triggers email alerts and reminders, with suspension if unresolved. Automatic debit can settle amounts due.

facts.label: Resource controls / upgrade risk
facts.value: Private Cloud can set account/server disk, CPU and RAM limits plus a RAM-threshold command. Shared terms authorize resource upgrades at applicable prices when actual needs exceed the chosen configuration.

facts.label: Hard monthly cap / idle residual
facts.value: No enforceable user-set monthly spending cap, quantified usage-alert thresholds or zero-balance cutoff timing found. Sleep/maintenance affects programs, while recurring account subscriptions remain.

facts.label: Sleeping / wake-up
facts.value: Website Idle time stops an inactive app and starts it on the next HTTP request. Value 0 disables that timer, but docs explicitly do not guarantee the app can never be stopped.

facts.label: Capacity changes / billing while idle
facts.value: Public plan changes are immediate through subscriptions; Private Cloud changes require support. Monthly/yearly account subscription continues independently of process idle time.

facts.label: Published quotas
facts.value: Public Postgres maximum 50 simultaneous connections per user; FTP maximum 10 per user. Private Cloud can request changes. Websites/databases/mail counts are unbounded subject to aggregate resources.

facts.label: Control API rate limits
facts.value: REST control API documents 10 actions/minute, 50/minute for authenticated requests and 250/minute for safe methods such as GET.

facts.label: HTTP/resource ceilings not published
facts.value: No universal numeric HTTP request timeout, body-size cap, app-concurrency quota, burst CPU entitlement or exact Public Cloud OOM/throttling algorithm found.

facts.label: Trial / card
facts.value: Plus offer advertises 30 days free on all its plans; Free signup is advertised without credit card. Public registration offers email/password, Google and Apple.

facts.label: Restricted profile validation
facts.value: Without a saved credit card or any completed payment, profile remains technically restricted; stricter HTTP filtering and SMTP limits can apply. A bank account alone does not lift restrictions.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Prepaid balance accepts credit card, PayPal or bank transfer; accepted card brands Visa/MasterCard. Automatic card/bank debit is available. Checks are not accepted.

facts.label: Eligibility / identification
facts.value: General terms accept private individuals and legal entities with contractual capacity; accurate registration/contact details are required and identity documents may be requested.

facts.label: Paid trial end / countries
facts.value: Exact paid-trial card requirement, end-of-trial conversion/deletion behavior, number of eligible trials and exhaustive supported/banned-country list not found.

facts.label: Commercial / revenue rules
facts.value: Paid Plus/Max marketed for business applications. Free explicitly forbids company websites/email, revenue-generating ads, selling products and other profit-making goals.

facts.label: Acceptable use
facts.value: French law and third-party rights apply; spam, phishing, hacking and harmful infrastructure/network use can cause suspension. Free additionally excludes excessive scraping, multiple free accounts and resource-heavy apps.

facts.label: Public Cloud management
facts.value: Free/Plus are managed shared hosting spread over multiple servers. alwaysdata manages infrastructure, OS, language stack and native databases; customer deploys, secures and updates applications.

facts.label: Private Cloud / Gold
facts.value: Max is provider-managed dedicated bare-metal infrastructure; Gold adds another server/datacenter with real-time redundancy. Customers can create isolated accounts on their dedicated environment.

facts.label: Suitable apps / overlap
facts.value: Static websites, PHP apps, Node/Python/Ruby/.NET/Java and custom HTTP servers, APIs, long-running services and scheduled commands; paid plans support commercial use.

facts.label: Container boundary
facts.value: Public Cloud does not offer Docker. Private Cloud supports rootless Docker after support installs it; the customer then configures its daemon service and images.

facts.label: Compute / primary storage location
facts.value: Servers are in France, Paris region; provider-owned equipment uses Equinix production datacenters. No standard selectable global region list published.

facts.label: Delivery / CDN distinction
facts.value: Built-in reverse-proxy HTTP cache is available; Max advertises CDN among custom options. No included global CDN with POP list or location controls established for Plus.

facts.label: Languages / architecture
facts.value: Debian x64 supports .NET, Deno, Elixir, Go, Java, Lua, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby and Rust; other account-level binaries can use User Program.

facts.label: Version selection / updates
facts.value: Choose a language major or specific minor; selecting a major receives new minor/security fixes automatically. Node currently lists LTS versions 6–24 and uses NODEJS_VERSION for overrides.

facts.label: Docker support / responsibility
facts.value: Rootless Docker is restricted to Private Cloud after support setup; images can power sites, services or tasks, with an HTTP site mapped through the supplied port.

facts.label: Node frameworks
facts.value: Node docs advertise marketplace installation for Express.js, Svelte and Next.js, and compatibility with applications such as Meteor/Nuxt/WebSocket.

facts.label: React static deployment
facts.value: Documented workflow builds static production assets locally, uploads them using rsync/SSH and points a Static files site at the build directory.

facts.label: Framework feature detail
facts.value: No current version/adapter matrix or precise Next.js Server Actions, streaming, image optimization, ISR/cache-durability guarantees found.

facts.label: Code / artifact inputs
facts.value: Upload using SSH/rsync, SFTP/FTP or WebDAV; marketplace can install selected apps. Configure site paths/start commands and environment through dashboard or REST API.

facts.label: Private-source workflow / automation
facts.value: Private source can remain on the builder's machine/repository while locally built artifacts are uploaded over SSH; automatic Git-triggered releases are customer automation rather than a documented included pipeline.

facts.label: Long-running workers
facts.value: Paid plans from Small provide Services: foreground programs are supervised/restarted automatically, with optional monitoring command and repeated-failure disabling.

facts.label: Scheduled jobs
facts.value: Dashboard scheduled commands/URLs use cron on Debian; scheduling is minute-based. If a previous execution still runs, the next is skipped; optional error email and job logs are supported.

facts.label: Job duration / retries
facts.value: No universal maximum task duration, numeric retry guarantee or missed-run catch-up policy found beyond the documented skip-overlap behavior.

facts.label: HTTP / WebSocket
facts.value: Native HTTP reverse proxy routes custom runtimes; first-party Node/Python WebSocket tutorial documents real-time bidirectional sites and idle-time considerations.

facts.label: Public custom service ports
facts.value: Paid Public Cloud Services use services-[account].alwaysdata.net ports 8300–8499 and external IPv6 only. Private Cloud needs a firewall rule for external access and can use other ports.

facts.label: Outbound / addresses / isolation
facts.value: Outbound ports are open without filtering, but connections are logged and abuse can trigger temporary blocking. IPv6 is native; published IP ranges support allowlisting.

facts.label: Private network / raw UDP detail
facts.value: No documented customer VPC/cross-account private-network contract, guaranteed static-egress option or explicit universal UDP service policy found.

facts.label: Persistent files / quota
facts.value: App code/uploads live in account directories accessed over normal file protocols; aggregate disk quota covers files, mail and databases. Backup NFS mount is external and excluded from quota.

facts.label: Shared storage restrictions
facts.value: No independently attachable managed-volume tariff, object-store durability tier or multi-node volume attachment contract found for standard Plus.

facts.label: Managed database / cache / queue catalog
facts.value: Native managed MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ available; Private Cloud adds managed Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Memcached and Redis/Valkey on request.

facts.label: Postgres versions / operational limits
facts.value: Postgres 16, 17 and 18 listed; pgBouncer on 5433; per-user permissions and extensions are configured in dashboard/API. Public connection maximum 50/user.

facts.label: Database memory / extra service prices
facts.value: No native PostgreSQL per-database RAM guarantee, separately priced 1-GiB DB tier, managed auth product or dedicated object-storage tariff established in checked catalog/pricing.

facts.label: Custom domains / HTTPS
facts.value: Paid plans accept own domains and unlimited site/domain counts within resources; automatic Let's Encrypt issue/renewal covers configured addresses pointing at alwaysdata. *.alwaysdata.net is covered by the platform wildcard.

facts.label: Wildcards / certificate constraints
facts.value: Wildcard site addresses are supported; automatic-renewed Let's Encrypt wildcard certificates can be created when the domain uses alwaysdata DNS. Full certificate address length limit is 64 characters.

facts.label: Previews / releases
facts.value: Customer can use multiple sites/accounts and preproduction addresses, then update paths/config/DNS; API can configure/restart sites. No managed automatic pull-request preview lifecycle published.

facts.label: Restart / rollout safety
facts.value: Default restart sends SIGTERM and can lose requests. Apache/uWSGI warm signals are handled; other programs can configure a Hot restart signal. Restarting an Apache site restarts all Apache sites in that account.

facts.label: Code / data recovery
facts.value: Return to earlier files/releases using customer source/artifact copies; dated native backup restore can restore selected directories and databases separately.

facts.label: Logs / retention / export
facts.value: Files contain HTTP access, upstream lifecycle, jobs, services, Apache, PHP and uWSGI logs; excerpts appear in admin. Per-account retention is configurable; Private Cloud also has server-level settings.

facts.label: Monitoring / metrics scope
facts.value: Server Status and resource/disk usage are exposed through account/server permissions. Private Cloud supports paid probes and CPU/RAM/disk limit controls; probes can alert the provider.

facts.label: Connection logging policy conflict
facts.value: Shared terms section 4.7 says server-connection data including connecting IPs is not retained; network docs say every connection is logged, and current HTTP-log formats include client IP.

facts.label: Numeric retention / observability limits
facts.value: No standard default log-retention day count, metrics retention interval, external log-drain contract or included application-error-alert guarantee found.

facts.label: MFA / delegated access
facts.value: Admin supports TOTP two-factor auth; delegated permissions can require 2FA. Roles split billing/account management, account/server technical scope and individual services.

facts.label: SSH access limitation
facts.value: SSH is available in all environments, with passwords/keys and no root/sudo. SSH users are not chrooted and can access the whole account even if their initial directory is restricted.

facts.label: Secrets / runtime settings
facts.value: Site/service/task environment variables and separate database credentials are configured through admin; control API uses profile tokens and account/customer scope.

facts.label: Platform security responsibility
facts.value: Provider applies security upgrades, has cgroup account isolation, network anti-DDoS and an annual Synacktiv audit; apps and Docker contents remain customer security duties.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the offered fully managed Free/Plus/Max platform; the provider installs/maintains its infrastructure and users have no root/sudo.

facts.label: Privacy / processing terms
facts.value: Public privacy policy covers data minimization, retention, rights and security. General terms section 17.2 includes controller/processor clauses, instructions, audit assistance and subprocessors, with Annexes II–V.

facts.label: Location exceptions / subprocessors
facts.value: Privacy generally excludes outside-EU transfer but allows necessary GDPR-compliant exceptions; processing terms permit instructed/law-required international transfer with safeguards.

facts.label: Referenced schedules / detailed residency
facts.value: Current separate subprocessor register and technical-organizational schedule referenced in Annexes IV/V, plus a data-type-by-data-type location promise, were not found in checked public sources.

facts.label: Daily backups / included scope

facts.label: Data retention after relationship
facts.value: Privacy retains customer relationship data up to 5 years after end and prospects up to 3 years after last contact; hosting termination deletes data after repeated deadline notices. Docs delete suspended profiles after 30 days.

facts.label: Identity and legal operator
facts.value: alwaysdata; ALWAYSDATA SARL, Paris company register 492 893 490, share capital €200,000; registered office 91 rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, 75008 Paris, France.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Linux/Unix shared-tenancy On-Demand rates on the AWS T3 page are USD $0.0104/hour for t3.micro, $0.0209/hour for t3.small, and $0.0418/hour for t3.medium; that page identifies US East (N. Virginia), us-east-1.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: A separate AWS Prescriptive Guidance table gives $0.0208/hour for t3.small and $0.0416/hour for t3.medium in us-east-1, versus $0.0209 and $0.0418 on the T3 product page.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: On-Demand instances have no long-term commitment; EC2 bills running instances by the second after a 60-second minimum, with OS-specific exceptions such as SLES hourly billing.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: AWS list-price pages say listed rates exclude applicable taxes and duties, including VAT and sales tax, except where noted.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: The EC2 price examples are in USD. AWS uses the account's billing country and contracting party for invoice and tax handling; the reviewed pricing page does not enumerate every possible invoice currency.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: t3.micro has 2 vCPUs, 1 GiB RAM, and 10% baseline CPU performance per vCPU; t3.small has 2 vCPUs, 2 GiB and 20%; t3.medium has 2 vCPUs, 4 GiB and 20%.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: T3's listed processor is Intel Xeon x86-64; the T4g family is Arm64 on AWS Graviton and needs compatible app images and dependencies.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: The three T3 examples are EBS-only; block storage is a separately billed EBS volume rather than included local SSD capacity.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: EC2 On-Demand charges accrue while the instance is running, even if it is idle; Linux and Windows partial hours are billed by the second after the first minute.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
