facts.value: Cluster Mode: customer-account EKS Auto Mode foundation, shared nodes and container replicas; AWS manages node provisioning, scaling, patching and platform add-ons.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Web applications, APIs and long-running processes; Standard also has a queue-driven worker tier. Static assets can be served by an application but this is not static-only edge hosting.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Cluster applications must tolerate interchangeable stateless replicas; persistent state belongs in an external service.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Standard compute is regional; consult the Beanstalk endpoint/availability table, including US East (N. Virginia), European and Asia-Pacific Regions.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Cluster placement uses supplied subnets in one Region/account; shared-cluster selection depends on matching subnet set. Source builds additionally need CodeBuild availability.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Standard supported families include Docker, Go, Java SE, Tomcat, .NET on Linux/Windows, Node.js, PHP, Python and Ruby; use current solution-stack versions.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Standard supports compatible x86/Graviton instance selections. Cluster supports amd64/arm64 container images; image and environment architectures must match.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Documented Standard Node.js/Express deployment runs an ordinary application server; Docker permits applications packaged with their dependencies.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: A provider-wide current matrix guaranteeing every framework's SSR, streaming and incremental cache-refresh behavior was not found.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Standard: console upload, EB CLI, AWS CLI/API and versioned application source bundles; deploy a previously uploaded application version.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Cluster reuses application/environment/version concepts and CLI/API workflows, with new EKS options; prebuilt image or source-build configuration is required.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Standard worker tier: SQS daemon pulls messages and delivers them to a local HTTP application; worker EC2/Auto Scaling resources are separate from the web tier.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Standard periodic tasks use cron.yaml and queue-based worker scheduling. Cluster can run container workers, including without an ALB.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Standard networking follows selected EC2 security groups/VPC and load-balancer type; ALB supports HTTP(S) and WebSockets, NLB supports lower-level connection forwarding.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Cluster requires one VPC, at least two AZs, consistent public/private subnets, VPC DNS and at least 32 free IPs per subnet; environment network isolation is default.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Standard root EBS is instance storage, not a durable shared-upload contract; application instances may be replaced. Persist durable objects in separately managed S3/storage.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Cluster local container files are lost on restart; stateless replicas should externalize persistent data.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Standard can create a coupled RDS database or connect an independently managed database. RDS, S3, SQS and other AWS services are separate products with separate bills.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: External RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1: Single-AZ db.t4g.micro 2 burstable vCPU/1 GiB US$0.016/hour; gp3 US$0.115/GB-month with 20 GiB minimum.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Standard generated environment domain and custom DNS mapping are supported; ALB HTTPS needs a certificate/listener, and single-instance HTTPS requires instance web-server configuration.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Cluster default ALB listens on HTTPS 443; Beanstalk manages ACM certificate issue/renewal/deletion for its environment domain. No default port-80 redirect is implied.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: ACM non-exportable public certificates used with supported integrated AWS services have no additional certificate charge.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Standard deployment policies include all-at-once, rolling, rolling with additional batch, immutable and traffic splitting; ordinary default all-at-once, EB CLI load-balanced default rolling.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Separate environments and CNAME swapping support blue/green; deploy an earlier saved application version for code rollback.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Cluster defaults to RollingUpdate; Recreate is an alternative. It uses Cluster options rather than the classic deployment-policy namespace.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Standard provides instance log tail/bundle retrieval; temporary download bundles in S3 are removed after 15 minutes. Hourly rotated-log upload and CloudWatch streaming are configurable.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Standard basic infrastructure metrics are available without additional metric charge; detailed/custom metrics, alarms and logs can bill separately.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cluster supports OpenTelemetry output to CloudWatch/X-Ray or external backends; supported language auto-instrumentation includes Java, Node.js, Python and .NET.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: AWS IAM controls service permissions; root MFA is enforced for traditional AWS accounts, and IAM identities have their own MFA/policy setup. Standard EC2 SSH requires keys/security-group access.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Standard platforms released from March 26, 2025 support Secrets Manager/SSM values as environment variables, with appropriate IAM permissions.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Self-hosted control-plane installation requirements: not applicable. AWS operates Beanstalk; customer-account EC2/EKS resources and application maintenance duties still apply.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: AWS Customer Agreement gives customer control of selected content Regions, with disclosed legal/service exceptions; AWS Privacy Notice separately covers personal/account data.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: RDS automatic backups support configurable retention up to 35 days; choose 7 explicitly for C. Daily backup windows and transaction logs support point-in-time recovery.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: RDS us-east-1 excess automated/snapshot backup storage: US$0.095/GB-month beyond eligible free backup allocation of 100% provisioned database storage.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Coupled RDS supports Delete, Snapshot or Retain lifecycle choices. Set Retain in a separate update before decoupling if the current policy could delete/snapshot it.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Keep/export source bundles and environment configuration, copy persistent objects, back up/export databases and repoint owned DNS. Standard application versions can be redeployed; Cluster uses portable container images.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Environment termination can delete owned resources; retained S3 versions/logs or independent RDS may remain. Cluster shared-cluster cleanup is delayed three hours after its last environment.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: AWS Elastic Beanstalk; Amazon Web Services product; Standard and Cluster deployment modes.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Active public offer. No whole-service shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the current offer, FAQ, release notes and lifecycle documentation.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Cluster Mode launched September 17, 2026. Amazon Linux 2 platform branches retired August 6, 2026.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: AL2 retirement dates disagree: the schedule introduction says no later than June 30, 2026, while its actual retirement table and retiring-platform notice say August 6, 2026.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: No Beanstalk-specific written uptime percentage/service-credit SLA found.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Underlying EC2 SLA: 99.5% single-instance and 99.99% qualifying multi-AZ regional deployment; credit bands 10%, 30%, 100%. EKS standard control plane SLA 99.95%, credit bands 10%, 25%, 100%.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Public AWS Health status URL exists, but incident/history contents could not be retrieved in the public fetch.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Basic account/billing support and public documentation/community are available; technical engineer support requires a qualifying paid AWS Support plan.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Business Support+ lists a US$29/month minimum per account, with 24/7 access to AWS experts.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: Hosted service software license: not applicable; AWS Customer Agreement, Service Terms and AUP govern this service.

facts.label: Lifecycle / AWS account Free Tier change
facts.value: AWS ended the legacy 12-month Free Tier for accounts created from July 15, 2025. New accounts instead receive up to USD $200 in credits and a Free account plan that ends after six months or credit exhaustion; earlier accounts keep legacy eligibility.

apps.name: AWS Lambda
apps.line: Run event functions or HTTP applications on managed AWS compute.

free.text: Event functions: 1 million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds monthly

cells.regions: AWS regions; Web Functions in five regions

work.math: Lambda storage is limited to code and execution files. A separate S3 + CloudFront example is not a price for hosting on Lambda.
1 million requests and 62,500 GB-seconds fit within the unused monthly allowances of 1 million and 400,000 GB-seconds. Assumes logs and request transfer stay free.
The small app API cost, plus $13.98 a month for RDS compute and 20 GB of storage. Backup excess, CPU credits, network path and logs vary.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: On-demand Event Functions: pay for requests and configured-memory duration; no mandatory Lambda base or seat fee, and no upfront commitment for on-demand usage.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: AWS normally calculates/bills fees monthly; invoice due date governs payment; prices exclude indirect taxes unless local law requires otherwise.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Optional Compute Savings Plans and capacity commitments have separate terms; Managed Instances may additionally use EC2 purchasing options. They are not used in our on-demand examples.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Event Functions: memory 128–10,240 MB in 1-MB steps; Lambda's MB means 1,024 KB. CPU is proportional to memory; 1,769 MB corresponds to approximately one vCPU.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Event Functions: 512–10,240 MB /tmp; first 512 MB at no extra storage charge. Default ephemeral space is not persistent app disk.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Web Functions: Arm64, two vCPUs and 2 GB per execution environment; 512 MB /tmp; default 64 concurrent requests/environment, configurable 1–128.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: MicroVMs: Arm64; configure baseline memory and proportional CPU, with burst scaling up to four times baseline. Current launch materials describe up to 16 vCPUs/32 GB memory/disk.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: US East (N. Virginia), us-east-1: Event Function requests US$0.20/million; x86 first-tier duration US$0.0000166667/GB-second; Arm US$0.0000133334/GB-second.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Asia Pacific (Mumbai), ap-south-1: Event Function requests US$0.20/million; x86 first-tier US$0.0000166667/GB-second; Arm US$0.0000133334/GB-second.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: us-east-1 and ap-south-1 Event duration tiers: x86 0–6 billion GB-s US$0.0000166667, 6–15 billion US$0.000015, above 15 billion US$0.0000133334; Arm 0–7.5 billion US$0.0000133334, 7.5–18.75 billion US$0.0000120001, above 18.75 billion US$0.0000106667.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Event Function duration rounds to 1 ms and includes initialization; INIT billing was standardized across runtime/package configurations on August 1, 2025. Extensions can add billed execution time.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: us-east-1 extra /tmp: US$0.0000000309/GB-second above 512 MB, both x86 and Arm.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: ap-south-1 extra /tmp: US$0.0000000352/GB-second above 512 MB, both x86 and Arm.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: us-east-1 Web Functions Arm: US$0.30/million requests; US$0.0000276944/active vCPU-second; US$0.0000036667/consumed GB-second.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: us-east-1 Provisioned Concurrency: x86 US$0.0000041667/GB-second provisioned plus US$0.0000097222/GB-second execution; Arm US$0.0000033334 plus US$0.0000077778; requests additional.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Managed Instances: US$0.20/million requests plus a 15% management premium based on EC2 on-demand price and the actual EC2-instance charges; no separate per-request execution-duration bill.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: us-east-1 Durable Functions: US$8/million durable operations; US$0.25/GB written; US$0.15/GB-month retained, in addition to ordinary invocation/compute charges.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: ap-south-1 Durable Functions: US$8.60/million operations; US$0.27/GB written; US$0.16/GB-month retained.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: us-east-1 MicroVM Arm: US$0.0000276944/vCPU-second and US$0.0000036667/GB-second; snapshot reads US$0.0015467699/GB, writes US$0.0037977138/GB, storage US$0.0001111111/GB-hour.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: us-east-1 SnapStart cache US$0.0000015046/GB-second and restore US$0.0001397998/GB where applicable; runtime-specific SnapStart exemptions/eligibility remain separate.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Event Functions recurring monthly free allowance: one million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds of compute.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Current Free AWS account plan is temporary: up to six months or credit exhaustion; an ordinary Paid plan can still use always-free service allowances and pays usage beyond them.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free account expiry suspends projects/resources; AWS describes 90 days to upgrade/recover data before permanent deletion. Paid plans normally continue charging rather than pausing at Lambda's free quota.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Service terms permit deletion of Lambda content after more than three months without running, on 30 days' notice.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: A current mode-specific repeating free CPU/memory allowance for Web Functions or MicroVMs was not established from their sections and the checked regional catalog.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Event Functions' inter-Region/internet transfer uses standard EC2 data-transfer rates; pricing explicitly lists free same-Region transfers with S3, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, EFS and certain other named services.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Standard AWS internet egress has a 100 GB/month free allowance aggregated across services/Regions, excluding China/GovCloud; not 100 GB for each Lambda function.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Web Functions/MicroVMs use standard AWS transfer rates and can incur separate transfer charges between managed compute and a customer's VPC.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Separate CloudFront pay-as-you-go delivery has an always-free allowance of 1 TB internet egress and 10 million HTTP(S) requests/month; AWS-origin fetch transfer is free under its pricing rules.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: us-east-1 direct internet transfer beyond the shared global free tier: first 10 TB/month US$0.09/GB; next 40 TB US$0.085/GB; next 100 TB US$0.07/GB; above 150 TB US$0.05/GB.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: ap-south-1 direct internet transfer beyond the shared global free tier: first 10 TB/month US$0.1093/GB; next 40 TB US$0.085/GB; next 100 TB US$0.082/GB; above 150 TB US$0.08/GB.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Lambda does not sell a native source-build minute pool for ordinary Event deployment. Build locally/external CI, then upload ZIP or ECR container; CodeBuild/CodePipeline/SAM build resources are separate.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Event package limits: 50 MB ZIP for direct API/SDK/console upload, 250 MB total unzipped including layers/custom runtime; container image ≤10 GB uncompressed in ECR.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Web Functions deploy ZIP packages from S3, with 512 MB unzipped package limit; MicroVM image creation consumes running MicroVM resources and uses S3/Dockerfile inputs.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Potential separate costs: CloudWatch logs/custom metrics, S3/ECR artifacts/files, CloudFront/custom-domain front door, API Gateway if selected, VPC NAT/private networking, EFS/S3 Files, SQL, secrets/KMS and optional support.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Optional Lambda-specific extras include provisioned concurrency, SnapStart, durable operations, tenant isolation, provisioned event pollers and response streaming above its included thresholds.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Lambda@Edge is another separately priced path tied to CloudFront: US$0.60/million requests and US$0.00000625125 per 128-MB-second in the published global edge pricing example.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Event reserved concurrency caps concurrent execution and reserves that capacity for a function; setting it to zero throttles the function. Reservation itself is not provisioned/billed warm capacity.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Web endpoints support opt-in maxEnvironments (2–10,000) and rate limits; rateLimit=0 blocks endpoint traffic. Controls apply separately per Region.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: New AWS-experience paid projects can opt into an enforced pre-tax spend limit: minimum greater of US$20 or a conservative estimate; AWS pauses resources at the limit.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Spend-limited paused project data is preserved, but docs say permanent deletion after 90 days without action; increasing the limit reactivates the project and some resources need manual restart.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Ordinary AWS Budgets notifications/actions are separate: actions can apply IAM/SCP policies or target EC2/RDS instances, but do not establish an immediate universal account-wide Lambda dollar stop.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: On-demand Event execution environments are created/reused with traffic; no reserved idle instance bill by default. Provisioned Concurrency and Managed Instances have different capacity charges.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Event standard regional concurrency default 1,000, with lower new-account quotas possible; per-function scaling up to 1,000 new environments every 10 seconds.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Web scales to zero; memory remains billable for the full environment lifetime including idle time between requests, while CPU bills active consumption.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: MicroVM suspend preserves memory/disk and stops running compute charges; snapshot storage/read/write still bill, and total session lifespan remains eight hours.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Event limits: 6 MB synchronous request/response, 1 MB async event, 200 MB streamed response; streams beyond 6 MB limited to 2 MB/s; 4 KB aggregate environment variables; five layers.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Event process/file limits: 1,024 threads/processes and file descriptors, except Managed Instances has higher/different limits; direct code-size and regional storage quotas also apply.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Web: 30-second request timeout configurable 3–900 seconds; 10-second startup; 128 KiB headers; 512 MB unzipped package; 32 KB environment variables; 10 endpoints and automatic 50-revision cleanup target.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Web account default quotas: 100,000 requests/second and 2,000 Arm64 vCPUs per Region; endpoint default 10,000 requests/second absent a lower configured limit; new accounts can be lower.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: MicroVM limits include eight-hour session, account/Region memory quotas and finite connection/rate limits; current connection cap scales from eight at one vCPU to 128 at sixteen vCPUs.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Current new AWS signup: most new customers do not need a payment method initially; AWS may request one or other information for identity verification.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Current account promotion: US$100 at signup and up to US$100 additional credits for eligible activities; prior/current AWS customers are not eligible for a second new-customer offer.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Credit-expiry guidance conflicts within the current AWS Free Tier FAQ: general/advanced sections say six months; paid-upgrade/activity sections say 12 months.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: AWS (new) signup uses preconfigured projects/designated Region; AWS (advanced) permits selecting Regions and granular IAM/networking. Account experience determines available controls.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Trade/sanctions compliance is required for users, controlling parties and financial institutions under the AWS Customer Agreement.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: A complete Lambda-specific accepted-country and supported-payment-method list was not found in the checked public pricing, signup and account FAQ pages.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Commercial apps and end-user services are within the hosted AWS agreement; Lambda's service-price free allowance is not described as a personal-only license.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: AUP forbids illegal/fraudulent use, rights violations, serious-harm/terrorism promotion, child exploitation, security/integrity attacks and unsolicited bulk messaging.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Lambda storage is limited to function code, dependencies and related configuration/metadata necessary to execute code; general downloadable-content/storage use is prohibited by service terms.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Managed compute: Event Functions use handlers/events; Web Functions run an HTTP server; MicroVMs provide customer-controlled isolated session environments.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Lambda Managed Instances run Event Functions on AWS-managed EC2 capacity in the customer's VPC, with multi-concurrent invocation and EC2 plus Lambda charges.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Event Functions: HTTP handlers/APIs, queue/stream processing, scheduled automation, file processing and other event-driven jobs. Web Functions: Node.js web servers, SSR, REST/GraphQL and response streaming.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: MicroVMs target per-user/job sandboxes, interactive coding, AI-generated code, CI jobs and other isolated sessions with OS capabilities.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Event Functions are regional. Examples of listed endpoints: us-east-1/us-east-2/us-west-2, Mumbai ap-south-1, Hyderabad ap-south-2, Singapore, Tokyo, Sydney, Frankfurt, Ireland, London and São Paulo.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Web Functions launch availability: us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo), eu-west-1 (Ireland); endpoint types HomeRegion, MultiRegion and PerRegion.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: MicroVMs: October 22 announcement reports 14 Regions and adds Hong Kong, Malaysia, Thailand and Spain.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Event managed runtimes include Node.js 22/24, Python 3.11–3.14, Java 8/11/17/21/25 variants, .NET 8/9-container/10, Ruby 3.3/3.4/4.0 and provided.al2023; supported runtimes generally support x86_64 and arm64.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Event Functions accept Linux container-image packages with the Lambda Runtime API/runtime interface client; ZIP and image package types cannot be switched in place for an existing function.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Web Functions: managed Node.js 24 on Arm64; latest patch applied automatically, with no patch-version pin/disable control. Server listens at AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: MicroVMs use customer image content built from the service's Amazon Linux 2023 base; include a Dockerfile; image/base versions have a lifecycle and need customer-triggered rebuilds for updates.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Web Functions run Express, Hono, Fastify, Next.js/other standard Node HTTP production servers without Event-handler adapters; SSR, API routes and streaming are promoted.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Framework-specific ISR cache persistence, exact Next.js version matrix, image-processing behavior and cross-Region application-state semantics are not completely specified by the checked Web runtime/sample descriptions.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Console/API/CLI ZIP upload, ECR images and infrastructure as code such as SAM/CloudFormation; Git source can stay private and be compiled/uploaded by an authorized local or CI workflow.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Web Functions use immutable S3-backed code revisions and endpoints; MicroVMs use versioned images with S3 inputs/Dockerfiles.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Event-driven background work is supported within invocation limits; schedules use separate EventBridge/Scheduler triggers, and queue delivery can use SQS or other sources.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Default Event invocation maximum 900 seconds; Managed Instances asynchronous/eligible event-source invocations up to 5,400 seconds; synchronous remains 900 seconds.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Durable workflows can last up to one year using checkpoint/replay/wait operations; current quota 30,000 durable operations/execution and 1 MB/operation payload.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Web environments can be shut down when no longer needed, and process state is lost; MicroVM running/suspended lifespan is at most eight hours.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Event Function URLs provide a public dual-stack HTTP(S) invocation endpoint; IAM or NONE auth, CORS and streaming supported; the endpoint itself has no extra fee.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Web endpoints accept HTTP/1.1, support streaming/SSE, remove Upgrade headers and explicitly do not support WebSocket upgrades.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Web default egress is public IPv4 with unstable Lambda-managed source IP. Optional egress connector accesses a customer's VPC, only for HomeRegion endpoints; dual-stack requires explicit connector/subnet configuration.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Event VPC attachment enables private SQL/network access; placing a function in a public subnet does not itself provide internet access. NAT/IPv6 routing can be needed and separately billed.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: MicroVM HTTPS ingress supports HTTP/2, gRPC and WebSockets with service authentication; configurable public/VPC egress and logical target ports.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Event /tmp and Web /tmp are temporary execution-environment filesystems; reuse may preserve files briefly but replacement/shutdown loses them.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Event persistent filesystem integration supports Amazon EFS or Amazon S3 Files, but not both simultaneously; object/API access to S3 is also a separate data-service path.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: MicroVM memory/disk can survive suspend/resume within the session; snapshot state and image retention are billed, and not a substitute for data retention beyond its lifespan.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Lambda itself has no bundled PostgreSQL, Redis, object store, queue or end-user authentication service. RDS/Aurora, DynamoDB, S3, EFS, SQS and related AWS services are separate integrations.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: C database dependency: RDS PostgreSQL Single-AZ db.t4g.micro, us-east-1, two burstable vCPUs/1 GiB RAM; US$0.016/instance-hour, plus storage/other RDS charges.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: us-east-1 RDS PostgreSQL Single-AZ gp3 storage US$0.115/GB-month; choose documented minimum 20 GiB, above the requested 10 GB. Additional backup storage US$0.095/GB-month beyond the regional free backup allocation.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Event Function URLs and Web endpoints include AWS-managed HTTPS domain/certificate; they do not directly attach a custom domain in the selected built-in endpoint model.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Separate CloudFront can supply alternate custom hostname plus ACM-managed TLS; standard non-exportable ACM public certificates used with integrated services have no additional certificate fee.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Event immutable published versions and aliases permit rollback/routing to prior code/config; alias traffic weights and deployment tools can support staged releases.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Web immutable revisions/endpoints support routing to one or two revisions for canary/blue-green deployments; dedicated endpoints can expose a selected preview revision.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: MicroVMs use image versions; rebuilding an image produces a new image artifact, not an in-place database rollback. Runtime/base image updates require a version/rebuild workflow.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Event stdout/stderr and system logs go to CloudWatch Logs when the execution role permits; there is no extra Lambda log fee, but CloudWatch ingestion/storage/query fees apply.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: CloudWatch log retention is configurable; default logs are kept indefinitely unless a retention policy is set. CLI/console/API access and export options belong to CloudWatch.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Web publishes service metrics at no charge; logs bill local ingestion/storage and centralized home-Region storage, with initial centralization free.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring

facts.label: Free-plan inactivity/deletion
facts.value: No SWA-specific inactivity duration, sleep-after-inactivity rule, or automatic deletion timetable established.

facts.value: Standard westus2: 100 GB/month included per subscription; excess USD $0.20 per GB.

facts.value: Standard southeastasia3 catalog: first 100 GB tier free, then USD $0.24/GB.

facts.label: App-to-database and other network traffic
facts.value: General Azure ingress and transfer within the same Availability Zone are free; inter-region and other egress have separate rates. PostgreSQL pricing refers to standard networking charges.

facts.label: Build engine and duration
facts.value: Oryx builds in a Linux Docker runner; custom builds/prebuilt output are supported. App/API build timeout defaults to 15 minutes and is configurable.

facts.label: Selected private-repository builder
facts.value: GitHub standard ubuntu-latest private-repository runner: 2 CPU, 8 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD, x64.

facts.label: CI charges and storage
facts.value: GitHub Free: USD $12 monthly included compute usage; Linux 2-core x64 $0.006/minute; 500 MB artifact storage and 10 GB cache/repository. Excess artifact storage $0.25/GB-month.

facts.label: Optional Enterprise-grade Edge
facts.value: Standard Azure Front Door add-on, westus2: USD $0.024/hour; southeastasia3 $0.0288/hour. Standard and a custom domain are required.

facts.label: Optional logs and monitoring
facts.value: Application Insights has an independent bill; it is required to obtain the documented managed-API logs.

facts.label: Other external resource charges
facts.value: Linked backends, PostgreSQL, other storage, CI storage, and support are independent services. Standalone Functions normally create a separately billed storage account.

facts.label: Budget alerts
facts.value: Opt-in Cost Management budgets notify; they do not stop resources or consumption. Usage usually arrives in 8–24 hours; evaluation is daily.

facts.label: Free versus paid overage protection
facts.value: Free stops serving above quota. Standard permits paid bandwidth overage. GitHub's own payment method and budgets separately govern CI overage.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Static production files use managed distribution. Managed APIs use Consumption, which can scale to zero and have startup latency. Standard retains its base plan meter independently of request volume.

facts.label: Request and runtime limits
facts.value: Both plans: 30 MB request-size quota. Integrated API request maximum 45 seconds; fixed /api route prefix.

facts.label: App and file ceilings
facts.value: Subscription: 10 Free apps or 100 Standard apps; contact support for more Standard apps. Each app: 15,000 files; Standard allow-list maximum 25 IP ranges.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: Eligible new Azure customers: USD $200 for 30 days; one free account per new customer. Services disable at trial end without a pay-as-you-go upgrade.

facts.label: Card, identity, and country requirements
facts.value: Free-account setup needs a phone, non-prepaid credit/debit card, and Microsoft/GitHub account. Hong Kong and Brazil require credit cards. Published available-country list includes India.

facts.label: Commercial hosted applications
facts.value: Azure's MCA Customer Solution clause allows third parties to access Azure services as part of the customer's solution, subject to contract and law. Standard is positioned for production.

facts.label: Free-plan commercial eligibility
facts.value: Pricing says hobbies/personal projects and plans say personal projects; a clear contractual yes/no for a solo commercial site was not established.

facts.label: Acceptable use
facts.value: Online-service AUP restricts illegal activity, rights violations, malware, spam, unauthorized access, cryptocurrency mining, and API-limit circumvention. Excess usage can be throttled.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Managed globally distributed static hosting, with optional service-managed Azure Functions APIs.

facts.label: Bring-your-own backend
facts.value: Standard can link separately managed Azure Functions, App Service, Container Apps, or API Management.

facts.label: Suitable app types and overlap
facts.value: Static sites and browser apps; HTTP APIs through supported backends. A custom server/container belongs in a linked backend service.

facts.label: Code versus delivery locations
facts.value: Production static assets are globally distributed. Selected resource location determines the managed Functions region; westus2 is explicitly used in CLI creation examples.

facts.label: Complete current selectable region list
facts.value: A complete current managed-Functions/SWA creation-region matrix was not established from product docs.

facts.label: Managed runtime versions
facts.value: Configuration lists .NET 8 in-process/isolated, .NET 9 isolated, .NET 10 isolated; Node 20/22; Python 3.9/3.10/3.11. .NET uses Windows and Node/Python Linux, Functions 4.x.

facts.label: Conflicting runtime lists
facts.value: APIs/Functions guide still lists older runtimes and Node 20 preview, while configuration and CLI docs include Node 22 and newer .NET/Python versions.

facts.label: Static frameworks
facts.value: Built HTML/CSS/JavaScript and client-side apps can be deployed as static output; build paths/commands and fallback routing are configurable.

facts.label: Hybrid streaming/version completeness
facts.value: Full current Next.js version/streaming compatibility and a precise ISR feature matrix were not established.

facts.value: GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps Pipelines, and SWA CLI deployment of local built folders and optional API source. Azure CLI manages resources and source integration.

facts.value: Managed Functions: HTTP triggers/bindings only; no Durable Functions. A persistent worker or Timer-triggered job is not included in this managed API mode.

facts.label: Separately hosted jobs
facts.value: Standard's bring-your-own Functions supports all Functions trigger/binding types, separately deployed and billed. SWA routes only to its HTTP endpoints.

facts.label: HTTP and live connections
facts.value: Backend integration is HTTP-only, with no WebSocket support; API request maximum 45 seconds.

facts.label: Private networking and filtering
facts.value: Standard supports an inbound private endpoint and IPv4 allow-list configuration. Private endpoint restricts access to the VNet and removes global POP delivery.

facts.label: Deployed site files
facts.value: Uploaded output remains deployed within the plan's environment storage quota; later deployments replace the served application.

facts.value: Customer-attachable durable filesystem/volume and its backup guarantees were not established for SWA managed Functions.

facts.value: Database overview says the feature ends November 30, 2025; pricing still advertises Database Connections as a free public preview.

facts.label: Built-in app authentication
facts.value: Preconfigured GitHub and Microsoft Entra ID login on both plans; custom provider registration is a Standard feature.

facts.label: Domains and automatic HTTPS

facts.value: Free: 2. Standard: pricing and plan guide say 5, quota guide says 6.

facts.label: Wildcard custom domains
facts.value: Current authoritative wildcard-binding/certificate rule not established.

facts.value: Free: 3 staging environments/app; Standard: 10. PR previews disappear on PR closure; branch/named previews can have stable URLs.

facts.label: Recovery workflow
facts.value: Keep source and build settings in Git; reverting a merged PR can create a new revert PR, whose production merge triggers the configured deployment workflow.

facts.label: Build and runtime logs
facts.value: Build logs belong to the chosen CI run. Managed API request/failure/trace logs, queries, and performance views use Application Insights; client-side instrumentation is separate.

facts.label: Monitoring retention
facts.value: Application Insights-related Log Analytics tables retain data 90 days at no retention charge by default; individual-table retention can be adjusted.

facts.label: Account and teammate access
facts.value: Azure uses resource-scoped role-based access. Mandatory MFA rollout covers Azure portal sign-ins and, from October 1, 2025, progressively CLI/PowerShell control-plane writes.

facts.label: Secrets and settings
facts.value: SWA application settings are encrypted at rest and serve backend API/auth configuration; settings can differ by environment. Frontend build variables are handled separately in CI.

facts.label: Managed API security limitations
facts.value: Managed Functions do not support managed identity or Key Vault references; bring-your-own Functions supports both.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to Free/Standard managed hosting; no customer-operated SWA controller/server is installed.

facts.label: Data-processing terms
facts.value: Microsoft DPA, November 2026: international transfers subject to its safeguards; Geo/EU-boundary commitments depend on covered-service definitions and Product Terms.

facts.label: Complete SWA data-location promise
facts.value: No SWA-specific commitment covering static copies, build artifacts, API data, logs, and backups all inside one selected country was established.

facts.label: Native SWA backup schedule
facts.value: No automatic customer-restorable SWA app/settings backup schedule, retention, or volume snapshot guarantee established.

facts.label: Separate Postgres backups and restore
facts.value: Flexible Server takes daily snapshot backups plus WAL backups; default retention 7 days, configurable up to 35. Backup capacity up to 100% of provisioned server storage is included.

facts.value: DPA generally retains stored Online Service Customer Data in a limited-function account for 90 days after subscription end, then deletes within another 90 days, with exceptions.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership

facts.label: Operating and signup status

facts.label: Contractual availability

facts.label: Entry cost
facts.value: Static-only apps: first three apps $0/month; each further static-only app $3/month. Dynamic container entry: $5/month for one shared 1-vCPU, 512-MiB container.

facts.label: Base fees and seats
facts.value: No separate paid team-seat charge in the listed App Platform plans; unlimited team members are included. Paid prices apply to the selected component size and container count.

facts.label: Currency and tax
facts.value: Billing API explicitly denominates invoice items in USD. General terms exclude taxes unless stated otherwise and allow collection of applicable sales tax, VAT or GST.

facts.label: Payment timing and commitment
facts.value: Usage accrues over the calendar month and is due on the first day of the next month; new teams can be charged earlier at their trust-tier threshold.

facts.label: Cancellation and continuing charges
facts.value: General service account can be cancelled through settings/support; accrued balances remain payable. Archiving keeps databases and dedicated egress IPs billable; deleting resources/account follows the documented resource/team cleanup steps.

facts.label: Shared fixed compute
facts.value: apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb: 1 shared vCPU, 512 MiB RAM, 50 GiB outbound/month, $5/month. apps-s-1vcpu-1gb-fixed: 1 shared vCPU, 1 GiB RAM, 100 GiB outbound/month, $10/month.

facts.label: Shared scalable compute
facts.value: apps-s-1vcpu-1gb: 1 shared vCPU/1 GiB/150 GiB outbound/$12 per month; apps-s-1vcpu-2gb: 1/2 GiB/200 GiB/$25; apps-s-2vcpu-4gb: 2/4 GiB/250 GiB/$50.

facts.label: Dedicated compute — smaller sizes
facts.value: Dedicated 1-vCPU containers: 512 MiB/100 GiB outbound/$29; 1 GiB/200 GiB/$34; 2 GiB/300 GiB/$39; 4 GiB/400 GiB/$49 per month.

facts.label: Dedicated compute — larger sizes
facts.value: Dedicated containers: 2 vCPU/4 GiB/500 GiB outbound/$78; 2/8 GiB/600 GiB/$98; 4/8 GiB/700 GiB/$156; 4/16 GiB/800 GiB/$196; 8/32 GiB/900 GiB/$392 per month.

facts.label: Architecture and local disk
facts.value: Only Linux AMD64 binaries/images are supported. Runtime local filesystem is limited to 4 GiB and is ephemeral.

facts.label: Container billing meter
facts.value: Selected size price multiplied by instance count, prorated per second; one-minute minimum. Creation followed by deletion in less than one minute still incurs the documented $0.01 minimum.

facts.label: Monthly cap and rename condition
facts.value: Components are billed for the first 28 days of the month after creation. Renaming a component restarts that count and can create additional charges within the same calendar month.

facts.label: Jobs and database meters
facts.value: Services and jobs use the chosen monthly container rate prorated per second; jobs charge only while running. Development and production databases are billed hourly with a one-hour minimum.

facts.label: Function component meter
facts.value: Functions include 90,000 GiB-seconds/team/month across standalone and App Platform functions; excess $0.0000185/GiB-second, with a 100-ms invocation minimum.

facts.label: Ongoing free static allowance
facts.value: Up to three apps containing only static-site components; each can contain multiple static sites. Each such app has 1 GiB outbound/month; excess $0.02/GiB.

facts.label: Static component inside paid app
facts.value: Static components added to a paid app have no extra static-component fee and do not add a separate bandwidth allowance.

facts.label: Free-tier inactivity and retention
facts.value: No explicit static-site inactivity deletion period or promised indefinite retention found in the checked free-tier, static-site, limits and service terms pages.

facts.label: Ingress and outbound rates
facts.value: Inbound App Platform transfer is free; outbound above the included pool is $0.02/GiB. Bandwidth billing states there is no regional variation.

facts.label: Allowance pooling and accrual
facts.value: Transfer usage and allowance pool across the team's App Platform apps, not with Droplets. Allowance accrues per second up to the 28-day monthly maximum; no rollover or transfer between teams.

facts.label: Transfer visibility
facts.value: Ingress bandwidth is visible for an individual app; accrued allowance and cumulative App Platform transfer-pool usage cannot currently be viewed.

facts.label: Database and log-forwarding transfer
facts.value: Traffic to/from DigitalOcean Managed Databases does not count against bandwidth billing allowance. Forwarded application logs likewise do not count toward App Platform bandwidth usage.

facts.label: Build service and price
facts.value: Built-in source builds/deploys are included in the published free/paid feature set; the product FAQ says there are no hidden build or platform image-storage charges.

facts.label: Build resource specification
facts.value: Features/scaling guides say default XL builds have 8 CPUs and 20 GiB RAM. The limits page instead states 8 CPU cores, 15 GiB RAM and 24 GiB build disk.

facts.label: Build duration and unpublished quotas
facts.value: Build timeout is one hour. Monthly build-minute allowance, build concurrency and deployment-count ceilings were not found in the current pricing, limits, scaling and buildpack documentation.

facts.label: Included delivery and domains
facts.value: Published plan features include global CDN, DDoS mitigation, automatic HTTPS, custom-domain attachment and unlimited team members; no separate mandatory App Platform load-balancer/IP fee for the standard public route.

facts.label: Optional dedicated outbound IP
facts.value: A pair of dedicated egress IPs costs up to $25/app/month, prorated per second with a 60-second minimum.

facts.label: Optional services and staging
facts.value: Development/managed databases, NFS shares/snapshots, extra containers, additional static-only apps and external log sinks can add charges; clones are separate app instances with their own resources.

facts.label: Budget protection
facts.value: Team/organization spend alerts email owners and billers at chosen percentages of a monthly budget; the docs explicitly say the budget is not a spending cap.

facts.label: Scaling and pause controls
facts.value: Autoscaling maxima bound container count; archive manually stops app-component billing except databases and dedicated egress IPs. No App Platform-wide automatic hard spending stop is documented by these controls.

facts.label: Normal running and manual scaling
facts.value: Container capacity is billed while allocated, including idle time. Vertical size changes are manual; scalable sizes permit horizontal replicas, while $5/$10 fixed shared plans list one container only.

facts.label: Autoscaling plan conflict
facts.value: CPU-based autoscaling requires dedicated CPU. New scaling/features docs also permit request-based autoscaling on shared or dedicated CPUs, while pricing tables/FAQ show shared autoscaling as unavailable.

facts.label: Autoscaling triggers and limits
facts.value: Fixed/CPU-based instance count up to 250; request-based maximum 100, minimum at least one. External HTTP rate/P95 metrics use a five-minute rate window; mixed metrics scale up on any threshold and down only below all.

facts.label: Private-preview inactivity sleep
facts.value: External web service can sleep after 10 minutes–24 hours without an external request. Sleeping container charge is 10% of the normal rate; databases/other resources retain normal charges.

facts.label: Manual archive and restore
facts.value: Archive takes the app offline and stores its configuration; app-component charges stop except databases and dedicated egress IPs. Restore redeploys the app; current archive storage is free.

facts.label: Runtime/request limits
facts.value: Local disk 4 GiB; uploads time out after 600 seconds; no platform-set concurrent-connection count, but each connection consumes the allocated container's resources.

facts.label: Account and size ceilings
facts.value: Container scaling is capped as above; 500 domains/app. Team resource limits can vary with trust tier and payment history and may require prepayment or support approval to increase.

facts.label: Unpublished request and app quotas
facts.value: A universal request-body byte cap, HTTP request lifetime, total app count and component-count ceiling were not established by the checked limits, app-spec and team resource-limit pages.

facts.label: Signup credit and payment requirement
facts.value: First team automatically receives $5 signup credit, expires after 90 days, excludes SaaS Add-Ons, cannot be transferred; a valid payment method is required before creating resources.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Credit/debit cards including Visa, MasterCard, Amex, Discover, UnionPay, Diners Club and JCB; third-party options include PayPal, Google Pay, Apple Pay, Alipay and Link; qualifying U.S. customers can use ACH.

facts.label: Buyer age, verification and countries
facts.value: Terms require age 18 or sufficient legal consent/capacity, accurate account details and compliance with applicable sanctions/export controls. Indian cards must allow international transactions.

facts.label: Complete country and identity-check matrix
facts.value: Exhaustive permitted-country list and universal identity-document requirement not published in the checked account/payment, credit and general terms pages.

facts.label: Commercial use
facts.value: General terms expressly allow offering services to end users and charging those end users. No separate non-commercial-only condition found for the static free offer.

facts.label: Acceptable use
facts.value: Policy prohibits unlawful/infringing or harmful activity, unauthorized access/security abuse, unsolicited bulk messaging and cryptocurrency mining without explicit written permission.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Managed application platform: DigitalOcean builds or accepts container images, runs them on its infrastructure, handles routing and platform maintenance; users maintain application code and configuration.

facts.label: App types and directory overlap
facts.value: Static websites, public or internal web services/APIs, continuously running background workers, lifecycle/scheduled jobs and on-demand function components.

facts.label: App types — important exclusions
facts.value: Linux AMD64 container workloads within the gVisor sandbox; unrestricted virtual machines, SSH/SFTP servers and public SMTP ports are outside the documented App Platform model.

facts.label: Compute regions
facts.value: Dynamic apps available in NYC, AMS, SFO, SGP, LON, FRA, TOR, BLR, SYD, ATL, RIC and MKC; no App Platform availability is marked for MEM in the current table.

facts.label: Static origin and delivery regions
facts.value: Static availability marked directly in NYC/AMS/SFO/FRA/SYD/ATL; SGP/LON/TOR/BLR/RIC/MKC are marked Cloudflare CDN only. CDN caches serve globally and route misses to the serving region.

facts.label: Region mapping caveat
facts.value: VPC how-to lists ten app-to-datacenter mappings and omits RIC/MKC; the newer NFS guide includes RIC1/MKC1 and notes NYC apps can use NYC1 or NYC3.

facts.label: Native language and container routes
facts.value: Buildpack index lists Node.js, Python, Go, PHP, Jekyll, Hugo, Ruby, Rust, .NET, Bun and Aptfile support. Dockerfile/prebuilt-image route covers other compatible Linux AMD64 stacks.

facts.label: Node.js runtime selection
facts.value: Node.js buildpack version 375; Node 22.x is the default when engines is unspecified. Package version selection uses package.json and the documented supported ranges.

facts.label: Python runtime selection
facts.value: Python buildpack version 358; unspecified Python defaults to 3.14.x. Detection includes requirements.txt, Pipfile and setup.py.

facts.label: Promoted frameworks
facts.value: Provider lists Express/Next/Nuxt, Django/Flask, Laravel/Symfony, Rails, Gin/Echo and static Gatsby/Hugo/Jekyll/React; a Next.js sample explicitly uses the Node.js buildpack.

facts.label: SSR, streaming and regeneration detail
facts.value: Container web services and Next.js deployment are documented; a complete versioned matrix for Next.js server rendering, React streaming and shared multi-instance ISR/cache behavior was not found.

facts.label: Next.js cache caveat
facts.value: Limits page warns of Cache Poisoning Denial of Service for Next.js apps and recommends omitting cache-control or setting it private for responses that must not be cached.

facts.label: Source deployment inputs
facts.value: Connect GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or a public HTTPS Git repository; set branch and optional source directory for monorepos; platform builds source through a Dockerfile or detected buildpack.

facts.label: Container deployment inputs
facts.value: Public and private images from DigitalOcean Container Registry, Docker Hub and GitHub Container Registry; automatic redeployment on registry image push is not available for Docker Hub/GHCR.

facts.label: Deployment control and source limitations
facts.value: Dashboard, doctl CLI, API and downloadable YAML app spec. Git LFS only for GitHub; SSH-based submodules fail and must use HTTPS; SHA-256 Git repositories unsupported.

facts.label: Background workers
facts.value: Managed non-routable worker components run application code continuously; select container resources and count separately from the web service.

facts.label: Scheduled and lifecycle jobs
facts.value: Pre-deploy, post-successful-deploy and post-failed-deploy jobs plus cron-scheduled jobs; minimum schedule interval is 15 minutes. Charges apply only during execution.

facts.label: HTTP, streaming and gRPC
facts.value: HTTP/2/h2c to containers and gRPC are explicitly supported by the configuration guide; default relay is HTTP/1.1. The general limits page still says HTTP/2/3 are downgraded and gRPC unsupported.

facts.label: SSE and edge cache
facts.value: SSE is documented: HTTP/2 is recommended and disabling dynamic-service edge caching avoids stream interference. Edge toggles require a custom domain and do not apply to the starter domain.

facts.label: WebSockets and universal connection timeout
facts.value: A product-specific public guarantee for user-app WebSocket support and its idle/maximum lifetime was not established in the checked network, limits, HTTP/2, edge and reference pages.

facts.label: Private networking and exposed ports
facts.value: Services communicate through app-internal names/ports; VPC integration connects eligible app components to DigitalOcean private resources. Dedicated public egress IPs and VPC attachment are mutually exclusive; functions do not support VPC.

facts.label: Fixed IP and IPv6 scope
facts.value: Shared public ingress IPs are free; optional fixed IPv4 egress pair is per app, excludes function and log-forwarding traffic, and cannot be reused across apps. No dedicated IPv6 egress is offered.

facts.label: Ordinary runtime filesystem
facts.value: Local runtime files are lost on deployment/container replacement; filling the 4-GiB filesystem makes a container unhealthy and triggers replacement. General-purpose Droplet volumes are not a normal attachment option.

facts.label: Persistent files — NFS preview exception
facts.value: Private-preview NFS mounts give services/workers/jobs persistent shared files; one app per share, same team and supported datacenter. Multiple replicas/components in that app can use the share.

facts.label: NFS allocation and bill
facts.value: Standard $0.15/GiB-month, minimum 50 GiB; High Performance $0.30/GiB-month, minimum 500 GiB; share maximum 32 TiB. Snapshots $0.06/GiB-month based on used storage.

facts.label: Development database
facts.value: App development PostgreSQL database is $7/month, 512 MiB in the pricing FAQ (512 MB in docs wording), app-only/default database, no automatic backup feature; deleting the app deletes it.

facts.label: Managed PostgreSQL minimum price conflict
facts.value: Standard Basic shared Regular 1 GiB/1 vCPU with 10–30 GiB storage shows $0.02254/hour and $15.15/month in the managed-database table; PostgreSQL docs instead say single-node plans begin at $15/month.

facts.label: Database edition and eligibility changes
facts.value: For accounts with no previous PostgreSQL/MySQL cluster since 15 October 2026, new Standard clusters are limited to 1/2/4-GiB shared plans without standby/read-only nodes; applies to all new clusters from 30 November 2026.

facts.label: Other supporting services
facts.value: App Platform links DigitalOcean Managed Databases and external databases; the pricing catalog includes MySQL, MongoDB, Kafka, Valkey and OpenSearch. Spaces object storage is a separate managed product.

facts.label: Custom domains and HTTPS
facts.value: Included starter address on ondigitalocean.app plus custom domains; DigitalOcean manages issuance and renewal of HTTPS certificates. Can use external DNS via CNAME or free shared ingress IPs.

facts.label: Wildcard and certificate conditions
facts.value: Wildcard domains supported after root-domain setup and TXT verification; CAA must allow letsencrypt.org and pki.goog. DNSSEC-enabled domains cannot be added.

facts.label: Domain ceiling
facts.value: Up to 500 domains per app.

facts.label: Deployment and checks
facts.value: New containers are made healthy before replacing the serving containers. Readiness checks stop traffic to unhealthy instances; optional liveness checks restart services/workers.

facts.label: Roll back releases
facts.value: Can roll back to one of the ten most recent successful deployments, in the same region with the same database resources/configuration; restores app code/config/spec but not database contents.

facts.label: Staging and branch preview workflow
facts.value: Clone an app for staging/testing or a feature branch; choose branch/resources and database connections. Encrypted app-level variable values are not copied and must be re-entered.

facts.label: Graceful termination
facts.value: Current termination guide defaults to 15 seconds drain and 120 seconds grace after SIGTERM; maxima 110 and 600 seconds respectively.

facts.label: Build, deploy and runtime logs
