An XS server with 2 vCPU and 2 GB, for 730 hours, plus 5 GB of persistent disk = €11.1325 before tax. CI overage and setup are not included. Capacity is untested.
S cluster + 15 GB disk subtotal €21.7175. The required daily 7-day backup service and storage are not priced.

facts.label: Pay as you go entry
facts.value: €0/month subscription; prepaid top-ups fund running clusters, storage and optional AI. No monthly commitment; topped-up balance does not expire.

facts.label: Pro subscription
facts.value: €20/month, with the full €20 added to the balance; 5% discount on AI usage and higher limits / Pro features.

facts.label: Ultra subscription
facts.value: €100/month, with the full €100 added to the balance; 10% discount on AI usage; announcement says no daily AI usage limit.

facts.label: Enterprise pricing
facts.value: Contact sales; tailored pricing, direct priority support, migration/integration services and custom components.

facts.label: Tax and contractual cancellation
facts.value: Listed fees exclude VAT / applicable taxes. Terms permit customer termination with 5 days' written notice and price changes with 30 days' prior notice.

facts.label: Billing model / renewal disagreement
facts.value: Current pricing and August 2026 notice say prepaid, with no end-of-month bill; October 2025 terms section 11.1 still says usage is billed afterwards at least monthly, and section 12.2 describes post-trial auto-renewal.

facts.label: Top-up / refund details
facts.value: Minimum paid top-up, refundability of unused balances, Pro/Ultra cancellation cutoff and exact subscription billing anchor were not found.

facts.label: XS cluster resources
facts.value: 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM; displayed rate €0.014/hour. Storage is separately metered.

facts.label: S cluster resources
facts.value: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM; displayed rate €0.026/hour. Storage is separately metered.

facts.label: M cluster resources
facts.value: 2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM; displayed rate €0.048/hour. Storage is separately metered.

facts.label: L cluster resources
facts.value: 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM; displayed rate €0.089/hour. Storage is separately metered.

facts.label: XL cluster resources
facts.value: 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM; displayed rate €0.182/hour. Storage is separately metered.

facts.label: Default storage allocation
facts.value: A new deployment starts with 5 GB persistent storage; it can grow in 5 GB increments and cannot shrink.

facts.label: CPU tenancy and architecture
facts.value: Physical CPU model, shared versus dedicated processor entitlement, guaranteed CPU performance, and selectable runtime architecture were not published in the checked specifications.

facts.label: Resource meters
facts.value: Running cluster-hours and storage-hours; same cluster usage rates for development, testing and production. Requests and team seats have no separate Diploi charge.

facts.label: Storage rate and precision
facts.value: Pricing visibly displays €0.00025/GB/hour. Terms default to hourly increments. The calculator uses finer constants than the displayed rounded rates.

facts.label: Invoice precision / rounding boundary
facts.value: Exact invoice rate precision, partial-hour treatment beyond 'hourly increments', storage GB versus GiB definition and minimum per-meter billing were not established.

facts.label: Ongoing free entitlement
facts.value: Current offer describes €50 credit for 14 days and then funded usage; its own comparison explicitly says no free/hobby plan, while the docs FAQ claims free development deployments with basic resources.

facts.label: Traffic charging
facts.value: Diploi's own pricing comparison states no additional charges for data traffic, seats or monitoring; current pricing separately lists requests as free and includes global CDN.

facts.label: Transfer detail
facts.value: Numeric outbound/CDN allowance, fair-use traffic threshold, inbound/internal meter definitions and region-specific network exceptions were not published in the checked sources.

facts.label: Build execution / inputs
facts.value: Production and staging builds use generated GitHub Actions; a define-components job creates a matrix and parallel build jobs build/push images into Diploi's registry.

facts.label: External private-repository build cost
facts.value: GitHub charges repository owners for eligible private-repository runner usage after the account's shared included compute amount; GitHub Free currently includes $12 USD/month.

facts.label: GitHub runner rates / rounding
facts.value: Standard Linux 2-core ARM64: $0.005 USD/minute; standard Linux 2-core x64: $0.006 USD/minute. Each job's partial minutes round up to a whole minute.

facts.label: Diploi build limits
facts.value: No separate numerical Diploi build-minute allowance, build-duration ceiling, concurrent-build quota or build-deploy count cap found.

facts.label: Potential extra charges
facts.value: Storage and each additional active development/staging/preview/clone cluster cost extra usage. Optional AI consumes the same balance. GitHub Actions overage and external backups can add separate costs.

facts.label: Platform feature / seat inclusion
facts.value: Custom domains, automatic SSL, cloud IDE, SSH and global CDN are included on Pay as you go; team seats and app features have no separate Diploi fee.

facts.label: Prepaid balance / automatic top-up
facts.value: Manual top-up limits the balance available; optional automatic top-up adds money when the balance falls below a configured threshold. Pro/Ultra automatically add their monthly amounts.

facts.label: Meter visibility / generic warnings
facts.value: Billing insights show current/prior usage and top-ups with almost real-time AI usage. FAQ promises notification before limits and possible temporary feature restriction.

facts.label: Exhaustion / residual costs
facts.value: Exact pause timing at zero balance, data-retention grace period, monthly hard-cap configuration and stopped-storage charges remain unclear.

facts.label: Enabled/idle behavior
facts.value: Production/staging stay enabled without a default time limit until manually shut down; development deployments default to automatic shutdown after 12 hours.

facts.label: Scaling
facts.value: Manual cluster-size changes are supported after disabling the deployment. Current standard architecture is single-node; higher-throughput horizontal scaling is described as future work.

facts.label: Public connection duration
facts.value: 60 seconds per service request/response connection; longer handling terminates the connection. Docs suggest polling / webhook-style asynchronous responses.

facts.label: Request / stack limits
facts.value: Pricing says no request limits or fees; catalog says component/add-on count is limited by available compute, rather than a published numeric per-project maximum.

facts.label: Additional ceilings
facts.value: No numerical body-size/upload limit, concurrency cap, account/project/deployment quota, max-disk size or per-component CPU/RAM reservation guarantee found.

facts.label: Registered trial
facts.value: New registered users: €50 free credit valid for 14 days; no credit card required for the public offer; trial AI includes €1 per day.

facts.label: Anonymous trial duration
facts.value: Current get-started guide and website FAQ say 1 hour; docs FAQ says anonymous deployments expire after 12 hours.

facts.label: Trial end / payment enforcement
facts.value: Terms reserve trial eligibility changes, possible payment details, post-trial renewal, and account/data deletion without further notice if the trial expires without a valid payment method.

facts.label: Buyer eligibility
facts.value: Terms allow both personal and commercial users; sanctions/export restrictions apply, including embargoed regions such as Crimea and North Korea.

facts.label: Payment methods / geographic detail
facts.value: No exhaustive accepted-card, bank-transfer, wallet, local-currency, country-availability or routine identity-verification list found.

facts.label: Commercial hosting
facts.value: Terms explicitly design the services for commercial and personal use and permit supporting end-customers; no noncommercial-only restriction is stated for Pay as you go.

facts.label: Acceptable use
facts.value: Unlawful/harmful use, unauthorized IP use, infrastructure disruption or data mining, fraud, spam, malware and impersonation are prohibited; sanctions rules apply.

facts.label: Hosted management model
facts.value: Managed platform: every deployment gets its own single-node Kubernetes cluster, with application components and add-ons running as containers.

facts.label: Server control and Enterprise mode
facts.value: Standard hosted users cannot choose the OS or configure host-server settings; SSH reaches development environments and component/add-on containers. Enterprise offers private-cloud / own-cloud and on-premise arrangements.

facts.label: Suitable apps and overlap
facts.value: Static sites, server-rendered frontends, HTTP APIs, full-stack monorepos, background processes, and packaged apps such as Ghost and n8n.

facts.label: Arbitrary applications / custom components
facts.value: Existing GitHub apps can be analyzed and imported, but unsupported layouts may require Dockerfile, start-command and configuration changes; standard custom and inline components remain roadmap items.

facts.label: App compute region
facts.value: Standard hosted deployment data is in AWS datacenters in Ireland, Europe; multi-region support is described as being worked on.

facts.label: Delivery feature
facts.value: Global CDN included in standard pricing; the Chat App starter specifically documents edge delivery via Cloudflare.

facts.label: Delivery regions
facts.value: No current CDN point-of-presence list, cache-region controls or country-by-country availability table found.

facts.label: Supported runtime families
facts.value: Catalog covers Node.js/Bun/Deno, Python frameworks, ASP.NET/Blazor, frontend frameworks and static sites; packaged components include Ghost, n8n, Metabase and Supabase.

facts.label: Versioned packages / Dockerfiles
facts.value: Current examples pin Node component v24.14.0, Python component v05.2026 and PostgreSQL add-on v18.3-pgvector; package references can be Git tags or branches.

facts.label: Bring-image boundary
facts.value: Supported components include editable Dockerfiles; prebuildImage can provide an initial component image, especially for starter kits. Full custom/inline component authoring remains roadmap / Enterprise-assisted.

facts.label: Next.js behavior
facts.value: Next.js package v16.3.3 is documented; website FAQ explicitly claims App Router, Server Actions, API routes and SSR support; production builds a Node image and starts it with npm start.

facts.label: Astro behavior
facts.value: Package v7.3.5 uses @astrojs/node standalone mode with output: server; pages can opt into prerendering. Runtime build is enabled by default and runs again at container start.

facts.label: SvelteKit behavior
facts.value: Package v2.70.3 uses @sveltejs/adapter-node and serves the build on port 3000; package manager is detected from the lockfile.

facts.label: Static Website behavior
facts.value: Static Website v2 uses official Caddy, HTTPS and gzip; production embeds static files in an image. Caddyfile can be edited for redirects, custom headers and rewrites.

facts.label: Source / deployment methods
facts.value: Create or import GitHub repositories; own public/private repositories are supported, external public repositories can be imported by URL. YAML config, dashboard, Git push and remote development CLI are documented.

facts.label: Repository requirement / import caveats
facts.value: Production/staging require repository-backed builds. A project launched without a repository is development-only and cannot have a repository added later.

facts.label: Import maturity versus framework support
facts.value: Import guide labels broad repository import beta and some frameworks experimental; current docs require reviewing detected configuration and fixing Docker/start commands when necessary.

facts.label: Background workers / scheduled work
facts.value: Node component explicitly supports background workers; own-feature comparison describes worker/cron task-runner components in the same cluster, using resources from that deployment.

facts.label: Job scheduling limits
facts.value: No published minimum cron interval, retry policy, execution-duration ceiling, queue guarantee or missed-run recovery policy found.

facts.label: Public endpoints / private service access
facts.value: hosts maps container ports to public HTTPS endpoints or internal-only service names using endpoint:false; add-ons are private to their deployment by default.

facts.label: Streaming / realtime examples
facts.value: Web App starter documents React Router SSR streaming; Chat App starter documents realtime messaging. Internal AI Gateway supports streamed model responses.

facts.label: Long-lived protocols / fixed addresses
facts.value: No explicit supported WebSocket/SSE streaming policy, public raw TCP/UDP offer, static outbound IP option, outbound-port restrictions or cross-deployment private network guarantee found.

facts.label: Persistent files
facts.value: Deployment storage is persistent; development code survives restarts/shutdowns. Add-on data such as PostgreSQL uses persistent storage.

facts.label: Disk attachment / deletion
facts.value: Storage belongs to the deployment, increases in 5 GB steps without restart, and cannot shrink. Deleting a deployment permanently deletes its code/database/data associated with the instance.

facts.label: Databases and support services
facts.value: Native add-on catalog: PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis and MinIO; these run within the deployment's cluster. Supabase is a supported component providing an additional full backend stack.

facts.label: PostgreSQL maintenance boundary
facts.value: Postgres runs from its official Docker image plus extensions. Major upgrades require pg_dumpall from the old version and restore to a fresh data directory; in-place downgrade is not supported.

facts.label: Included operational email
facts.value: Internal SMTP relay is included at no extra cost: 10 messages/hour and 30/day, for development/low-volume operational mail; higher volume requires discussion or an external provider.

facts.label: Domains / certificates
facts.value: Custom domains and automatic SSL are included. Project-level diploi.app base subdomains and deployment-level custom domains are documented; public component endpoints get certificates automatically.

facts.label: DNS target conflict
facts.value: Dedicated custom-domain guide / troubleshooting use edge.diploi.me, while deployment-lifecycle and import blog use edge.diploi.com.

facts.label: Wildcards / domain counts
facts.value: Deployment-lifecycle guide says wildcard domains are not fully supported yet; no numeric included custom-domain/endpoint count was found.

facts.label: Environments / cloning
facts.value: Development, staging and production are separate deployments with their own configurations/resources and shareable endpoints; cloning can copy a deployment including database and configuration.

facts.label: Release and code rollback
facts.value: Git pushes rebuild/update deployments tracking that branch; failed CI leaves the last successful complete build running. Troubleshooting recommends reverting code/config and restarting as needed.

facts.label: Health checks / rollout guarantees
facts.value: Status tree, pod readiness/events and component restart tools are documented; configurable user health probes, guaranteed zero-downtime updates, canary routing and instant release rollback retention are not specified.

facts.label: Logs / metrics
facts.value: Dashboard exposes component/add-on process logs, health/status tree and resource charts with 1-minute, 1-hour and 1-day views.

facts.label: CLI log access / export
facts.value: Development CLI logs defaults to the last 200 lines, supports live follow and --since; commands accept JSON and streaming commands emit JSON objects per line.

facts.label: Retention / external alerts
facts.value: No numeric runtime log retention, export-destination integration list, ingestion limit or managed incident-alert/notification pricing found.

facts.label: Authentication / access
facts.value: GitHub authenticates registration; SSH public keys enable access to deployment containers; central team access/permissions are advertised with isolated environments.

facts.label: Secrets / build separation
facts.value: Runtime ENV can be edited per deployment and imported between components. CLI masks declared secrets unless --reveal; sensitive build values can use GitHub Secrets + BuildKit mounts.

facts.label: Postgres credential defaults
facts.value: Postgres reference shows default user/password postgres and database app, with parameters configurable on deployment Setup tab; add-on is internal-only by default.

facts.label: Starter demo-account warning
facts.value: Chat App starter seeds a public test account and explicitly requires changing or removing it before production.

facts.label: Detailed security controls
facts.value: No documented role-by-role permission matrix, native MFA setup/enforcement, SSO entitlement, secret encryption-at-rest/key-management specification or audit-log retention found.

facts.label: Standard hosted self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable: ordinary Pay as you go / Pro / Ultra users consume Diploi-managed clusters, with no controller installation required.

facts.label: Enterprise own-cloud requirements
facts.value: Enterprise on-premise/bring-your-own-cloud is advertised, but supported OS/architecture, minimum hardware, control-plane layout, update/backup split and controller-outage behavior were not published.

facts.label: Personal-data location / transfers
facts.value: Privacy policy says personal data is stored in EU/EEA; necessary transfers outside it may involve affiliates/providers, including AWS, Stripe, Linear and Sentry.

facts.label: DPA / complete residency commitment
facts.value: No public DPA, full subprocessor register or per-data-type location schedule for customer payloads, logs, builds, AI and backups was found.

facts.label: Backup responsibility / optional help
facts.value: Customer is required to maintain external backups. Docs FAQ says regular backups can be provided on request, with configuration controls still being developed.

facts.label: Backup schedule / restore terms
facts.value: No standard daily-backup schedule, seven-day retention, database-consistency method, destination/residency, numeric backup price or restore recovery objective found.

facts.label: Source / infrastructure portability
facts.value: Source lives in the customer's GitHub repository; public Dockerfiles/Helm charts and normal runtimes can be used to migrate to another container/Kubernetes or server host.

facts.label: Data / settings export
facts.value: FAQ says data and configurations can be exported with support assistance; Postgres guide documents pg_dumpall/restore for changing data directories/major versions.

facts.label: Deletion / retention
facts.value: Deployment deletion is permanent for its associated data. Terms require deletion of all Customer Data within 60 days of termination unless legal retention applies; privacy allows necessary/legal account-data retention.

facts.label: Identity and operator
facts.value: Diploi, operated by Diploi Oy / Diploi Ltd, Finnish business ID FI34195512; address Malminkatu 30, 00100 Helsinki, Finland.

facts.label: Current offer and access
facts.value: Active public development, staging and production platform; registration uses a GitHub account. A no-registration demonstration is also offered.

facts.label: Lifecycle / material product notice
facts.value: August 25, 2026: Diploi announced that its new prepaid balance billing was live, replacing monthly pay-per-use billing; existing paying users received initial credit.

facts.label: Availability contract
facts.value: No public uptime percentage, eligible-plan SLA, exclusions or service-credit schedule found; terms provide commercially diligent efforts and otherwise as-is service.

facts.label: Public status history attempt
facts.value: Could not verify a public service-status dashboard or historical uptime record; attempted status.diploi.com did not resolve.

facts.label: Standard support
facts.value: Discord for public/non-private issues; support@diploi.com for private information under terms. Website/docs also offer hello@diploi.com and documentation GitHub issues.

facts.label: Enterprise priority support
facts.value: Enterprise advertises direct priority support plus migration and integration assistance; price is by agreement.

facts.label: Support hours / response guarantee
facts.value: No public staffed hours/time zone, guaranteed first-response/resolution time or numeric support-package fee found.

facts.label: Hosted software terms
facts.value: Hosted service is governed by Diploi terms; Diploi retains service/software intellectual property and grants a revocable access licence. Customer keeps Customer Data rights.

facts.value: The official component-nodejs repository LICENSE is MIT, copyright 2026 Diploi.

facts.value: App Space native recurring scheduler, worker duration guarantees and minimum schedule frequency not found.

facts.value: App Space WebSocket/SSE proxy guarantees, raw TCP/UDP exposure matrix, maximum HTTP body/timeout and dedicated egress-IP offer not established.

facts.value: Active public VM and App Space offers, documented email/Google signup and prepaid provisioning.

facts.value: Plans billed monthly; pricing permits cancel/upgrade/downgrade at any time. Terms reserve suspension for late payment, 1.5% monthly late interest or legal maximum if lower, and 15-day fee-policy notice before the affected billing cycle.

facts.value: Pricing/home promise a full refund if unhappy within 30 days of purchase. Terms section 4.2 makes refunds discretionary and service-credit-only; section 11.2 says account cancellation receives no refund.

facts.value: A process is a startup command such as node server.js; every app needs at least one. More processes are load-balanced. Metrics chart combined CPU/memory use for all app processes against available resources.

facts.value: No standard-tier vCPU/core allocation, physical CPU model, shared-versus-dedicated CPU guarantee or runtime architecture inventory found.

facts.value: Standard tiers list 2/4/10/15/20 GB app storage; AUP separately sets maximum free MongoDB storage at 1 GB, soft limit.

facts.label: Base and usage billing
facts.value: Monthly tier plus possible storage excess; no public CPU-second/function-duration/request-invocation price or separately priced build-minute rate found.

facts.label: Storage overage
facts.value: €2 per started excess GB per month, based on the highest storage usage during the previous billing period.

facts.label: Meter accounting gaps
facts.value: Exact GB/MB binary versus decimal definitions, overage aggregation across apps, counted build/cache/runtime paths, MongoDB excess tariff and partial-month proration not published in checked pages.

facts.label: Recurring free hosting
facts.value: No documented ongoing free hosting allowance/reset/resource table found; public entry is signup/trial followed by paid monthly plans, while terms generically mention free usage up to limits.

facts.label: Network allowance / enforcement
facts.value: AUP lists Network Bandwidth 2 TB/month as a soft limit; hard limits are automatically enforced and soft limits may produce quota-exceeded responses or termination for repeated excess.

facts.label: Network excess rates / CDN
facts.value: No public per-GB overage tariff, separate internal/CDN transfer pricing, regional rate table or included global CDN entitlement found.

facts.label: Native builds / dependencies
facts.value: Git push checks out code, installs dependencies and restarts the app. Node uses npm install --production; Python uses pip install -r requirements.txt and runs Django collectstatic when Django is listed.

facts.label: Build fee / machine / limits
facts.value: No public build-minute allowance/rate, current builder CPU/RAM, concurrency limit, timeout, maximum artifact size or deployment-count quota found.

facts.label: Optional GitHub CI
facts.value: GitHub deployment uses customer-configured GitHub Actions, then pushes to EvenNode's Git remote. Native local Git/FTP deployment does not require GitHub Actions.

facts.label: Included operational features
facts.value: Standard paid table marks load-distribution/scaling, failover, runtime logs/metrics, HTTP/2, custom domains, free/custom SSL and email support as included.

facts.label: Other likely costs
facts.value: Storage peak overage, external PostgreSQL/persistent services or backup destinations, optional GitHub CI and custom dedicated capacity can add costs.

facts.label: Legal / administrative assistance fees
facts.value: DPA security, data-subject, breach, impact-assessment and audit assistance may be charged at prevailing fees plus expenses; no numeric schedule published.

facts.label: Limits versus spend caps
facts.value: AUP has a hard 30-second request limit and soft network/MongoDB limits; terms permit enforcement. Storage is billable above quota using a high-water mark.

facts.label: Budget / billing alerts
facts.value: No documented user-set monthly hard cap, storage-overage opt-out, prepaid stop, numeric spend alert or automatic billing pause found.

facts.label: Scaling / processes
facts.value: Upgrade plan or enable more processes; platform routes requests across active instances and advertises automatic failover to healthy servers.

facts.label: Sleep / stopped billing
facts.value: No published idle-sleep interval, wake/cold-start promise, automatic scale-to-zero behavior, stopped-app fee discount or hourly billing/proration rule found.

facts.label: Request / soft quotas
facts.value: AUP: Request Length 30 seconds hard; Network Bandwidth 2 TB/month soft; maximum free MongoDB storage 1 GB soft.

facts.label: Other ceilings
facts.value: No published HTTP body/upload-size cap, precise concurrency ceiling, build timeout, app-count quota or exact OOM/restart enforcement threshold found.

facts.label: No-card signup / payment options
facts.value: Pricing says app launch/signup needs no card; paid plans accept PayPal or wire transfer as alternatives to credit card.

facts.label: Trial length / current detail
facts.value: Official August 5, 2017 notice announced 30-day free trials; currently linked signup/pricing/docs do not restate a numeric trial duration or full trial-resource/end policy.

facts.label: Buyer / country eligibility
facts.value: Terms require users to be over 13, legally eligible under Slovakia/other applicable laws and export rules, with accurate registration details.

facts.label: Commercial-use scope
facts.value: Paid platform intended to develop/run applications; no personal/noncommercial-only standard-tier restriction found. AUP bans unauthorized exploitation/resale of the service.

facts.label: Acceptable-use restrictions
facts.value: AUP prohibits gambling, phishing, malicious/hate/violent content, unlawful activity/IP abuse, spam, illegal P2P and cryptocurrency mining. Significant load tests need prior written consent.

facts.label: Management model
facts.value: Provider-managed app platform: upload Node.js/Python source, use supplied startup/runtime/build workflow, and manage processes through web console; platform supplies load balancing and failover.

facts.label: Dedicated mode
facts.value: Custom dedicated servers, dedicated MongoDB and dedicated account manager appear only in the custom-price column; servers are tailored on request.

facts.label: App types / overlap
facts.value: Node.js/Python web apps, HTTP APIs, WebSocket apps, separately started background processes, Django and Meteor examples. Static assets can be served through the application.

facts.label: Persistence limitation
facts.value: Runtime filesystem is ephemeral and not shared across processes; app-created/modified files reset on restart/deploy. Use a persistent database/external service for durable data.

facts.label: Current marketed locations
facts.value: Current feature/runtime marketing says Europe and United States; exact current cities, provider region codes, availability zones and plan-specific region list not published there.

facts.label: Singapore / geographic scaling status
facts.value: June 17, 2020 notice announced Asia Pacific Singapore, alongside Europe/North America and GeoDNS/multi-location scaling. Current standard marketing mentions Europe/US without explaining Singapore's current availability.

facts.label: Runtime behavior
facts.value: Native Node app starts with npm start when package.json is present, otherwise app.js/server.js; Python uses configured startup command, binds 0.0.0.0 and PORT and declares requirements.txt.

facts.label: Current runtime versions / custom images
facts.value: No current exhaustive Node/Python version matrix, end-of-support dates, Docker/private-image deployment specification or selectable CPU architecture found.

facts.label: Historical Deno support
facts.value: June 23, 2020 announcement enabled Deno for all customers; no current Deno guide/version inventory found in the present Node/Python docs navigation.

facts.label: Django behavior
facts.value: Python guide starts a Django app with Gunicorn; build installs requirements and automatically runs manage.py collectstatic when Django is a dependency.

facts.label: Meteor / static behavior
facts.value: Meteor is uploaded as an os.linux.x86_64 bundle and run as a Node app. New-stack notice deprecated direct public/ static serving and says the app can serve static files, e.g. Express static middleware.

facts.label: Advanced framework guarantees
facts.value: No versioned SSR/streaming/ISR/Next.js adapter matrix or framework-specific cache durability guarantee found in official current runtime/deployment guides.

facts.label: Deployment inputs
facts.value: Git push to a per-app EvenNode SSH remote, FTP with optional explicit TLS, or optional GitHub Actions automation; web dashboard supplies app settings.

facts.label: Git workflow
facts.value: Add public SSH key, add EvenNode remote, push master; platform checks out code, resolves dependencies/cache and restarts. Each app has its own target Git repository.

facts.label: Background jobs
facts.value: Included feature supports a separate startup process for background work rather than blocking the web process; process count is constrained by the chosen plan.

facts.label: Scheduled jobs
facts.value: Cron guide uses a cron npm package within a running application; its example fires every second. No native independent managed scheduler is described.

facts.label: Job durability / limits
facts.value: No published managed retry policy, missed-run catch-up, exactly-once guarantee, worker duration ceiling or persistent scheduler history found.

facts.label: HTTP / WebSocket support
facts.value: HTTP/2 and WebSockets included; docs provide socket.io example. Metrics explicitly describe WebSocket sessions appearing as minutes/hours/days until connection closes.

facts.label: Networking details
facts.value: No public raw TCP/UDP port service, fixed outbound IP entitlement, private VPC/network contract, outbound restriction list or per-app IPv6 guarantee found.

facts.label: Ephemeral filesystem
facts.value: All app-created/changed files are cleaned on restart/deploy; fresh source comes from FTP/Git. Files are not shared across processes.

facts.label: Persistent-data path
facts.value: Vendor recommends included MongoDB, including GridFS for uploaded images/files/sessions. No persistent volume/block-disk/object-store product documented in checked catalog.

facts.label: Native database
facts.value: Each app gets one included MongoDB database; vendor describes primary/secondary/backup member in a three-member replica set. Dedicated MongoDB available in custom tier.

facts.label: Mongo connection / upgrade behavior
facts.value: APP_CONFIG supplies connection information; password is set/reset in web console and external Mongo shell access is documented. September 2022 notice made MongoDB 6.0 available and says existing deployments stay on prior versions until migrated.

facts.label: Postgres / other service catalog
facts.value: No public native PostgreSQL, Redis/cache/queue/object-store/auth tier or quantified PostgreSQL memory/storage/backup package found.

facts.label: Domains / HTTPS
facts.value: Unlimited custom domains and wildcard subdomain routing; current paid table includes free Let's Encrypt and custom SSL certificates. Free certificate deployment uses dashboard and renews automatically.

facts.label: DNS / wildcard certificate detail
facts.value: Custom-domain guide uses CNAME to the app's assigned hostname. No general apex A/ALIAS prescription, wildcard-certificate challenge workflow, certificate cap or custom SSL upload procedure found.

facts.label: Git release / overlap
facts.value: Restart spawns new processes while old processes still receive traffic, then stops old processes after 30–40 seconds; provider calls this zero-downtime deployment.

facts.label: FTP deployment trigger mismatch
facts.value: Homepage/features say upload automatically rebuilds/deploys latest code; Node/Python dependency guides and Python quick start instruct a restart to detect FTP changes and rebuild.

facts.label: Preview / rollback / health detail
facts.value: GitHub events can trigger a customer workflow; creating a separate app and switching DNS is documented for legacy migration. No native automatic PR-preview creation/deletion or immutable release-history rollback procedure found.

facts.label: Logs / metrics
facts.value: App stdout/stderr live logs in web console; build/NPM logs are referenced by migration docs. Metrics include combined CPU/memory, throughput and response-time p90/p95/p99.

facts.label: Log retention / export / alerts
facts.value: No numeric log retention, exact metrics retention window beyond 'last weeks', log-drain/export API, storage ingestion tariff or alert-delivery policy found.

facts.label: Account two-step verification
facts.value: January 20, 2020 vendor guide documents optional authenticator-app codes, pairing from account settings, trusted-device remembering and support recovery.

facts.label: Deployment / database secrets
facts.value: Git uses account public SSH keys; FTP has separate password setup/reset and optional TLS. MongoDB password must be set before first connection; example CI uses GitHub Secrets.

facts.label: Permissions / host access details
facts.value: No documented role-by-role team matrix, native SSO/audit log, secrets-at-rest key/rotation policy, user shell/root access or self-managed OS entitlement found.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable for the documented managed service. No customer controller installation, own-cloud setup guide or self-host hardware minimum published.

facts.label: Data-processing agreement
facts.value: Public DPA applies where GDPR governs user data; customer is controller/processor and EvenNode processor/subprocessor; processing follows written instructions and the DPA prevails on its subject matter.

facts.label: Data residency / backup exception
facts.value: DPA section 3.4 lets the customer choose storage region but consents to backups in any region; section 3.5 permits necessary processing outside EEA/Switzerland with compliance measures.

facts.label: Account-data privacy
facts.value: Privacy effective January 1, 2014 permits worldwide transfer/access to customer data, including US/Slovakia; providers may process billing/customer information. Access/change/delete requests are handled within 30 days.

facts.label: Subprocessors / security schedule
facts.value: DPA grants subprocessor authorization with 15-business-day objection opportunity after notice, but no named current register or detailed technical-security/region schedule found.

facts.label: Backups / responsibility
facts.value: Terms make customer responsible for securing/backing up applications and content; data-loss/storage warranties are disclaimed. MongoDB replica set is the documented native data-protection mechanism.

facts.label: Backup schedule / restore
facts.value: No standard automatic snapshot schedule, seven-day retention, point-in-time recovery, backup tariff, restore UI/procedure or restore-time objective found.

facts.label: Exit / source / data access
facts.value: Retain local/upstream source; Git/FTP is the deployment basis. MongoDB external connection is documented, providing a data-access route before exit.

facts.label: Deletion / retrieval
facts.value: Pricing says plan expiry/cancellation deletes all data; terms require export before termination and promise reasonable retrieval opportunity if provider terminates. DPA requests secure personal-data deletion within a reasonable period, subject to law and pre-expiry retrieval request.

facts.label: Identity / operator
facts.value: EvenNode, operated by Adhouse, s.r.o., Bajzova 6, Bratislava, 82108, Slovakia.

facts.label: Current status / signup
facts.value: Active public Node.js/Python hosting offer, priced plans and public email/password registration; provider status page reports Applications, load balancers, MongoDB, deployments and dashboard operational.

facts.label: Lifecycle / dated notices
facts.value: No whole-service shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in checked current site, company, blog and status/history. Blog index's latest visible article is MongoDB 6.0, September 6, 2022.

facts.label: Availability marketing / mechanism
facts.value: Homepage/features claim average 99.99% monthly availability/'SLA' and advertise load-balanced health checks/failover.

facts.label: Formal SLA / credits
facts.value: No public eligible-plan uptime contract, measurement/exclusion schedule, claim window or service-credit formula found; terms sections 12–13 provide as-is/as-available service and broad liability exclusions.

facts.label: Status history
facts.value: Official status/archive accessible; checked page reports operational and recent days without reported incidents. Archive includes January 21, 2023 DNS outage and March 2021 datacenter-fire migration.

facts.label: Support / plan distinctions
facts.value: Email support@evennode.com included in all displayed tiers; company lists sales phone +44 2 033 227 110, 10am–7pm CET. Dedicated account manager is custom-tier feature.

facts.label: Support response guarantee
facts.value: No numeric guaranteed technical first-response/resolution time, staffed support timezone schedule or escalation/on-call SLA found.

facts.label: Hosted software licence / terms
facts.value: Hosted service uses proprietary-rights/access-licence terms; customer keeps application/content rights. Open-source component licences are separate, not a licence to self-host the entire EvenNode platform.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing

facts.label: Runtime and request limits

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: No complete public buyer-country eligibility matrix or universal identity-document requirement found.

facts.value: Managed Postgres is provider-maintained. Unmanaged Fly Postgres is customer-maintained and unsupported by Fly.io support.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: GitHub Actions integration runs flyctl with a scoped deploy token; Machine/API management is also documented.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs

facts.label: Network and connection support

facts.label: Network and connection support

facts.label: Persistent app files

facts.label: Persistent app files

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: MPG Basic: shared-2x/1GB USD 38/month; Starter: shared-2x/2GB USD 72; Launch: performance-2x/8GB USD 282; Scale: performance-4x/32GB USD 962; Performance: performance-8x/64GB USD 1,922.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Rolling is the default deploy strategy; immediate, canary and bluegreen are also documented. Smoke checks monitor startup and service health checks can gate traffic.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Rollback uses a prior release image with fly deploy --image; no dedicated rollback command. Current configuration/secrets and database changes are not automatically reverted.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: App stdout/stderr can be tailed with fly logs. Searchable application logs are retained 7 days; search is beta and currently free.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Managed Prometheus-compatible metrics and Grafana currently have no additional charge; metrics retain approximately 15 days.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Member and Admin organization roles; Members broadly manage/deploy apps and resources, while Admins also manage membership/billing and delete the organization.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: App/org deploy tokens, read-only org tokens, SSH-only and restricted Machine-exec tokens are documented; tokens can be named, expired and revoked.

facts.label: Access and secret handling

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: No customer-facing audit log of organization actions or Fly.io staff access is currently provided in the public security explanation.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms

facts.label: Backups and restore

facts.value: Largest component plan booked during a day is charged for that day; downgrade effective next day. Traffic's final monthly volume determines its plan for the whole month.

facts.label: Ongoing free hosting

facts.value: SSH/SFTP, deployments, MySQL connections and app-to-other-service requests, including external APIs/email, are not counted in the Traffic component.

facts.label: Traffic limit behavior
facts.value: With autoscaling on, traffic moves to its final monthly tier; off, the environment goes offline when its traffic plan is full until next month or manual scale-up.

facts.value: GitHub push triggers a deployment container with build commands; environment price is the sum of booked components. No separate build-minute price is listed.

facts.label: Build tools and isolation
facts.value: Node.js 24 default, 22 available during deployment; Composer, npm and pnpm supported. Global npm installs and downloaded headless browsers are restricted.

facts.label: Unpublished build ceilings
facts.value: Numeric maximum build duration, builder concurrency/CPU/RAM and monthly build allowance were not established.

facts.label: Mandatory and optional cost components
facts.value: Every environment includes paid PHP, storage, traffic and backup. MySQL/Jobs optional; staging repeats its own component bill. External domains need separate registration.

facts.value: Current PHP settings/update policy describe possible monthly legacy-PHP support fees per environment; no numeric current fee or definitive offered-version tariff found.

facts.value: Disable autoscaling per environment to fix booked tiers: full storage rejects writes, full MySQL rejects new rows, traffic exhaustion takes environment offline.

facts.value: Booked components remain billable without visitors; no refund for unused booked capacity. Deletion takes immediate effect and stops billing from the following day.

facts.label: Idle billing and sleep
facts.value: Booked resources remain charged without visitors. No idle HTTP-app scale-to-zero or automatic request-based sleep price is described.

facts.label: Scaling model
facts.value: New platform scales components vertically; PHP/Jobs/manual backup count by user choice, storage/MySQL/traffic automatically only when enabled.

facts.label: Memory/process/database connection limits
facts.value: PHP XS/SM/MD/LG/XL/2XL: 2/2/4/6/8/12 processes and 8/8/12/16/20/28 MySQL connections; component memory shared among processes.

facts.label: Request settings and missing numeric caps
facts.value: post_max_size, upload_max_filesize, max_execution_time, max_input_vars and output_buffering configurable; no current documented numeric universal defaults/maxima established.

facts.label: ENV and job count ceilings
facts.value: Up to 200 ENV vars; names up to 128 characters and values up to 8,192. Jobs plans allow 1 to 32 registered jobs, total RAM 128 MiB to 4 GiB.

facts.label: Trial period and card
facts.value: Each new app gets seven days without a credit card; larger plans may have a shorter trial and the largest require payment details even during trial.

facts.label: Trial end and deletion
facts.value: Without a payment method, app, all environments and their data are deleted at trial end; advance email is sent. With payment details, billing begins unless the app is deleted beforehand.

facts.label: Buyer eligibility conflict
facts.value: TOS §1 allows businesses, public authorities and self-employed persons and excludes consumers. Detailed pricing says the service can also be used B2C.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Automatic card billing and SEPA for EU bank accounts via Stripe; current page also lists Apple Pay, Google Pay, Visa, PayPal, Mastercard, AmEx, Amazon Pay and Klarna.

facts.label: Commercial and restricted use
facts.value: Intended for professional websites, web apps and APIs. Illegal/infringing content, pornography/erotic content, spam, open relays, gambling and crypto mining/brokering are restricted.

facts.label: Reselling and disruptive workloads
facts.value: Subletting service requires agreement under TOS; unauthorized scanning/access, disruptive crawling, DoS and evading limits prohibited.

facts.label: Managed hosting model
facts.value: Managed PHP application hosting on shared AWS infrastructure, orchestrated with Kubernetes; components run separately rather than as a customer-owned VPS.

facts.label: App/environment structure
facts.value: App groups environments; every environment is a separate running copy with its own components, settings, data, Git branch and bill.

facts.label: Supported workload types
facts.value: PHP websites, APIs and web apps; Laravel, Symfony, Craft CMS, WordPress, flat-file CMS and custom PHP. Static assets can be served, with PHP still part of the current component model.

facts.label: Related services and restrictions
facts.value: Managed MySQL, persistent files and paid jobs; external databases and transactional email can be connected. Node.js is build-time tooling, not the ordinary hosted web runtime.

facts.label: Application regions
facts.value: Ireland/EU on AWS eu-west-1 and Virginia/US on AWS us-east-1; chosen when creating the app.

facts.label: Delivery network scope
facts.value: Web traffic is served by the selected region's environment; an external CDN can front the app. AWS services used by fortrabbit do not establish a global app-region guarantee.

facts.label: Runtime model and confirmed version example
facts.value: PHP web runtime, version configurable/pinnable per environment; current Tempest guide explicitly deploys PHP 8.5. Same version applies to web, deployment and jobs.

facts.label: Complete version/legacy availability

facts.label: Containers, binaries and access
facts.value: Lightweight managed containers; no root shell or runtime software installation. Heavy tools such as ffmpeg/Chromium/image optimizers run only in Jobs, not web requests or SSH.

facts.value: Craft 5 guide separates code, database and assets; Composer/npm build before release, migrations/project-config/cache commands after release, merge strategy by default.

facts.label: Symfony and static/JS scope

facts.label: Deployment inputs
facts.value: GitHub App push-to-deploy, manual deploy button/API, or direct SSH/SFTP/rsync file transfer. Other Git providers can deploy by their own CI through code access.

facts.label: Private code repositories
facts.value: Private GitHub source is explicitly demonstrated in the Craft guide; GitHub App needs access to the selected user/org repositories.

facts.label: Workers
facts.value: Jobs workers run nonstop and restart after exit and successful deployment; optional Jobs container shares files, database/settings and ENV vars with its environment.

facts.label: Scheduled jobs
facts.value: Native crontab scheduling, including every-minute Laravel scheduler; UTC times. Each cron has configurable max runtime and exit timeout.

facts.label: Interruption and concurrency
facts.value: All jobs share booked memory; deploy/job changes send exit signal, then SIGKILL after configured timeout. Detached child processes are killed; overlapping crons can run until a platform limit.

facts.label: HTTP and live connections
facts.value: Managed HTTP with automatic HTTPS; WebSocket connections explicitly unsupported.

facts.label: Outgoing connections and IPs

facts.label: Incoming security controls
facts.value: Experimental incoming WAF uses nG Firewall rules in Apache to reject common attacks/bots before PHP; toggle per environment.

facts.label: Persistent filesystem
facts.value: Storage persists across restarts and deployments and is accessible by SSH/SFTP; code, uploads and runtime files share the booked space.

facts.label: Deployment overwrite warning
facts.value: Merge keeps existing files not in the deploy package; replace deletes them unless protected by exclude patterns.

facts.label: Native databases
facts.value: Optional managed MySQL 8, one database component/database per environment; no native PostgreSQL service.

facts.value: Official Neon integration uses always-on pgsql/pdo_pgsql extensions and credentials in ENV vars; choose external DB in app's AWS region.

facts.label: Domains and TLS

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Ordinary Cloud Billing budgets send alerts; a separately configured spend-cap budget can pause eligible Cloud Run workloads. Spend-cap feature is Preview.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Cloud Run cap effects: web requests return 5xx, new jobs fail to start, worker instances stop processing, standalone instances shut down. Monthly reset or manually lifting the cap restores access.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: General spend-cap guide allows in-flight requests to complete; Cloud Run specifically warns that in-progress job tasks fail to complete.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Service-level max instances helps constrain growth, but may be exceeded briefly during traffic spikes; revision tags/rollouts and other meters need separate attention.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Default services autoscale down to zero; startup/health checks apply on demand. Idle non-minimum instances are not kept idle longer than 15 minutes.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Request-based services throttle CPU outside requests; instance-based billing allocates CPU throughout life. Instance-based services still need minimum instances to retain background capacity.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Manual service scaling can hold a selected count, or disable by setting zero; idle charges still depend on billing mode.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Service request timeout defaults 300 seconds, configurable up to 3,600; per-instance concurrency maximum 1,000.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: HTTP/1 request maximum 32 MiB; non-streamed/non-chunked HTTP/1 response maximum 32 MiB; HTTP/2 request path has no corresponding 32 MiB limit in the quota table.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Regional quotas include 1,000 services, jobs and worker pools each/project; 100 standalone instances/project; 1,000 environment variables/container; 1,000 service revision history threshold.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Cloud Run's documented Cloud SQL connector path limits each service/job instance to 100 database connections; total connections multiply as instances scale.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Eligible new users receive US$300 Welcome credit valid for 90 days; no automatic usage charge until upgrading to a paid account.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Trial signup needs a valid credit card or other accepted payment method; identity/payment verification and country-dependent bank verification can apply.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: When trial credit/time expires without upgrade, billing closes and resources stop; a 30-day grace period allows possible recovery before permanent deletion.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Payment methods vary by billing country/currency. UPI is available for qualified Indian organizations paying INR; supported PayPal countries include Spain, Italy and Mexico with stated restrictions.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Commercial application use is governed by Google Cloud terms, service terms and AUP; no personal-use-only Cloud Run free-tier rule found.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: AUP prohibits illegal/fraudulent activity, abuse, malware, unauthorized disruption and spam. Terms require written approval for cryptocurrency mining and restrict high-risk, export-controlled and unapproved HIPAA uses.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Fully managed regional container platform: services, jobs, worker pools and individually managed instances; no customer-managed VM/cluster required.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Source-deployed services can opt into automatic Google base-image OS/runtime security updates; arbitrary custom base images are excluded.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Services suit public websites, APIs, webhooks, HTTP/gRPC and event-driven functions; jobs run tasks to completion; worker pools suit continuous pull consumers.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Standalone instances target individually addressable long-lived workloads, with explicit lifecycle operations and no horizontal autoscaling.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Cloud Run compute is regional; examples use us-central1 (Iowa). Region list includes Mumbai asia-south1, Delhi asia-south2, Tokyo asia-northeast1, Belgium europe-west1 and others.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Johannesburg africa-south1 price tier conflicts: pricing lists Tier 1, location guide lists Tier 2.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Feature availability varies: direct domain mapping is limited to ten listed Regions; standalone instances exclude Iowa, Belgium and South Carolina in the current location guide; GPUs have a smaller Region list.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Containers must support Linux x86_64/amd64; Docker/OCI formats are accepted and multi-architecture manifests must include linux/amd64.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Google managed base-image families include Node.js, Python, Go, Java, .NET, Ruby and PHP, with a dated runtime support schedule.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Official Next.js quickstart deploys a Next.js 16 application as a normal Cloud Run service; server-rendered optimized Git/CDN deployment is separately referred to Firebase App Hosting.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Complete Next.js/framework feature guarantees for ISR/shared cache across replicas were not established.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Deploy container images, source/Dockerfile, functions or Git continuous deployment using console, gcloud, YAML/API or Terraform. Source builds create registry artifacts.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Functions created through Cloud Run API use its management API; functions created through Cloud Functions v2 API can also be managed through Cloud Run. First-generation functions retain a separate deployment resource.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Jobs run independent tasks to completion; up to 10,000 tasks/execution, retry maximum 10, task timeout up to 168 hours. GPU task limit is 12 hours in Preview.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Run jobs on a schedule through Cloud Scheduler; Scheduler costs US$0.10/job/31 days after first three account-wide jobs, and paused schedules count.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Worker pools perform continuous non-request work, no public load-balanced URL; scale manually, or configure an external-metrics autoscaler such as CREMA.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Services expose HTTP(S), streaming/WebSockets and gRPC; TLS terminates at Cloud Run and optional end-to-end HTTP/2 uses h2c to the container.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: WebSockets stay subject to the configured service request timeout, up to 60 minutes; clients need reconnects and shared state between replicas.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Direct VPC: services/jobs support egress; worker pools/standalone instances also support private ingress. Direct VPC addresses are not stable.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Default writable container filesystem is memory-backed, counts against instance memory, and disappears when the instance stops.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Optional disk-backed ephemeral volumes are also deleted on shutdown/revision migration; volumes 1–100 GiB, default total 10 GiB/instance, maximum ten volumes; quota can constrain larger allocation.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Cloud Storage bucket mounts or external NFS/Filestore provide external persisted storage, configured separately.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Cloud SQL PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQL Server, Firestore, Cloud Storage, queues/events and other Google Cloud services are separate supporting products.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Selected C database: Cloud SQL Enterprise PostgreSQL, single-zone general-purpose dedicated-core, 1 vCPU and 3.75 GiB, 10 GiB SSD, Iowa.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Cheaper db-g1-small shared-core has 1.7 GiB RAM, Iowa US$0.035/hour, but Google describes shared-core machines as test/development-only and excludes them from the Cloud SQL SLA.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Default run.app HTTPS endpoint is included and Google terminates TLS. Custom memorable subdomains under cloud.run are Preview, without DNS or load-balancer setup.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Direct custom-domain mapping is Preview, limited to listed Regions, explicitly not recommended for production due to latency issues; managed certificates issue/renew automatically.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Google recommends global external Application Load Balancing for production custom domains; Firebase Hosting is another separate option.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Deployments create immutable service revisions; split traffic, tag a revision for a testing URL, and route traffic back to a previous revision.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Healthy container/startup probes gate serving; services can configure startup order for sidecars. Old non-addressable revisions can eventually be removed.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Request logs (services), container stdout/stderr and platform system logs are sent to Cloud Logging; view through Cloud Run console, Logs Explorer or supported CLI paths.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Logging standard log storage: US$0.50/GiB after first 50 GiB/project/month, includes 30 days; retention beyond 30 days US$0.01/GiB-month.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Run exposes built-in metrics and supports alerts in Cloud Monitoring; additional custom metrics, traces, exports and destinations can bill separately.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: IAM separates deployer/viewer/invoker roles and runtime service identity. Public services can disable the Invoker IAM check; authenticated invocation is also supported.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Google Cloud MFA rollout covers personal Google Accounts from May 12, 2025; organization/federation dates vary.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Secret Manager secrets can be mounted as files or injected as environment variables; file reads fetch the current selected secret value, env vars resolve at instance startup.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Self-hosted control-plane minimum hardware: not applicable. Google operates the hosted platform; builder must maintain app/container dependencies and persisted-service configuration.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: Cloud Run customer data is stored in the selected Region. Contractual at-rest residency permits specified same-country replication for backup, reliability, debugging, support, maintenance or security.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: DPA permits processing where Google/subprocessors maintain facilities, subject to specific residency/transfer commitments; Cloud Privacy Notice covers Service Data rather than Customer Data.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud Run replicas/ephemeral volumes have no durable data to recover after shutdown; recover code/configuration from retained images/source/revisions, and back up external persisted services separately.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud SQL standard automated backups can run daily, with retained backup count default 7; select retention explicitly. Restore a backup to a new or existing SQL instance.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud SQL standard backup storage, Iowa: US$0.000109589/GiB-hour used; actual incremental storage depends on data/churn/retention.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Export service configuration as YAML, retain/copy OCI images/source, migrate external files/data and repoint owned DNS. PostgreSQL exports use SQL/CSV via Cloud SQL/Cloud Storage.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Deleting a Cloud Run service deletes its revisions but not necessarily registry images, SQL instances, buckets, logs or load-balancer resources.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Google Cloud Run; Google Cloud managed application platform. Cloud Functions was renamed Cloud Run functions on August 21, 2024.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Google contracting company depends on billing address and service; India GCP contracts use Google Cloud India Private Limited.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Active public offer. No whole-product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the current offer, release notes, runtime support and function comparison.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Current release stages: worker pools GA April 14, 2026; standalone Cloud Run instances Preview August 25; spend caps Preview July 27; custom cloud.run URLs Preview September 28; ephemeral disk GA November 4.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Managed Node.js 20 runtime decommission date October 30, 2026; Node.js 26 and Python 3.15 are Preview.

facts.value: Cloud Run service SLA, CPU-only: 99.95% monthly outside Stockholm; Stockholm 99.9%. GPU service with zonal redundancy follows those percentages; without it, 99.5%.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: SLA credits 10%, 25% or 50% by outage tier, maximum 50% monthly covered-service fees; request within 30 days with logs.

facts.value: Public Google Cloud Service Health and history are readable; Cloud Run history includes multi-product incidents October 19 and September 1, 2026.

facts.value: Basic support includes documentation, community, billing support and recommendations. Standard Support is a separate organization/account purchase.

facts.value: Standard Support: minimum US$29/month or 3% of monthly Cloud charges, whichever is higher; P2 initial response four hours during business hours.

facts.value: Installable Cloud Run service software license: not applicable. Hosted use is governed by Google Cloud terms/service terms/AUP.

facts.value: Managed instance groups can autoscale or repair VMs when configured; extra running capacity and any attached resources are billed normally.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits

facts.label: Runtime and request limits

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: The exact current quota for a particular project was not checked; it is project-specific and visible to authorized users in Cloud Quotas.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: New eligible customers receive USD $300 in Welcome credit for 90 days; the trial ends earlier if the credit is exhausted or the customer upgrades to a paid billing account.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Trial eligibility requires that the user has never been a paying customer of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform, or Firebase and has not previously signed up for the Google Cloud Free Trial.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The trial account is not billed while it remains a Free Trial account; after the credit is spent or 90 days pass, its resources stop unless the user upgrades.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The trial requires a valid credit card or other accepted payment method; Google may require bank verification depending on country. The authorization hold is typically USD $0–$1 and is not a charge.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Trial accounts cannot add GPUs, use Google Cloud Marketplace, request quota increases, or create Windows Server VM instances before upgrading.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Google says Cloud Billing is available in most countries, but restricts some services in examples including China, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Syria; India billing accounts require identity verification within 30 days.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Supplemental Free Trial terms exclude U.S. and Mexican federal, state, and local government entities unless Google agrees in writing.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Google Cloud's terms apply to business use of paid Cloud services, subject to the customer agreement, service terms, payment terms, and policies.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: The Google Cloud AUP prohibits unlawful activity, rights violations, phishing/fraud, unauthorized service interference, malicious software, and unsolicited mass email or spam.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Compute Engine is infrastructure as a service: you rent virtual machines in a Google data center and choose their zone, machine type, disk, network, and OS image.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Google operates the physical infrastructure and virtualization; you manage the guest OS, application, runtime, firewall choices, credentials, and app-level recovery.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: VMs can be created through the console, gcloud CLI, REST API, or infrastructure tools that call the API.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: A VM can run a public site, API, long-running application, worker, scheduled process, or self-managed database if its OS and resources fit.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Compute Engine supports Linux and Windows public images, custom images, and imported boot images; some images can run containers.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Google Cloud Run, App Engine, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Build, and Cloud DNS are separate products and are not included in the VM price.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Compute Engine runs in Google's selectable regions and zones. E2 is documented as available in all regions and zones; actual capacity and other machine-type availability can vary.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: The worked VM and storage prices are for Iowa (us-central1); egress is priced by source/destination geography, and the IP rate is listed for standard VMs across the pricing page.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Compute Engine accepts public or custom Linux and Windows images; E2 uses x86 processors, with Intel or AMD selected at VM creation.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: You can install language runtimes and container tools in the guest OS; Compute Engine does not impose a fixed managed runtime list for a VM.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Common web frameworks can run if the chosen OS, architecture, VM resources, and installed dependencies support them; server rendering, streaming, caching, and framework upgrades are customer-configured.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: A managed framework preview or framework-specific deployment feature is not part of raw Compute Engine VMs.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Deployments can use SSH/SCP, gcloud, REST APIs, custom images, startup scripts, or a customer-built CI/CD pipeline.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Google Cloud supports Linux SSH connections through console, gcloud, or SSH tools; Windows VMs use Remote Desktop and the customer's OS access setup.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Startup scripts run when a VM boots and can be supplied directly up to 256 KB or from Cloud Storage when larger.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Long-running workers can run as OS services on an always-running VM; there is no separate Compute Engine worker fee or worker quota.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Scheduled work can use OS tools such as cron or a separate scheduler product; Compute Engine does not include a managed cron service.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: VMs support TCP and UDP protocols and customer-configured network interfaces; VPC firewall rules must permit required inbound and outbound traffic.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: HTTP, HTTPS, WebSockets, and streaming can run on VM software over allowed TCP ports; Compute Engine does not provide a universal application request or WebSocket timeout.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: An official networking troubleshooting page points to a default 10-minute idle TCP timeout and recommends TCP keep-alive; it is path-specific, not a universal Compute Engine connection limit.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Static external IPv4 addresses persist while a VM is stopped; ephemeral IPv4 is released on stop. Internal addresses and private VPC networking are configurable.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Persistent Disk volumes provide durable block storage across VM stop/start and can be separate from the boot disk.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Standard, balanced, and SSD Persistent Disks are priced by provisioned capacity; writes and unused provisioned capacity do not reduce the storage charge.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Local SSD is temporary storage and not supported on E2 shared-core machine types; use Persistent Disk for app data that must survive VM lifecycle changes.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Compute Engine includes no managed database, cache, queue, auth, or object-storage service; you can self-host software or buy separate Google Cloud products.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: A Marketplace or premium OS image can add third-party license fees; the OS image's license terms remain separate from Compute Engine.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: You can point a domain to a VM using DNS you control; domain registration and Cloud DNS are separate services.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Google-managed certificates are available through separate load-balancing or certificate services, not bundled with the VM; wildcard and renewal rules depend on that separate setup.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Compute Engine has no managed branch previews; create separate VMs or use a separate deployment service if previews are needed.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: You can make a custom image or disk snapshot before release and restore a VM from it, but this is infrastructure recovery rather than application or database transaction rollback.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Managed instance groups support health checks and repair policies when configured; this is not enabled automatically for a standalone VM.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Compute Engine sends basic VM metrics to Cloud Monitoring; guest OS and application logs need customer configuration, commonly the Ops Agent.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring charge for applicable ingestion, retention, and billable metrics; these costs are not part of E2 compute rates.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Monitoring alert policies can send notifications or trigger integrations; an alert alone does not stop a VM.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: IAM and OS Login can restrict who may administer or SSH into a VM; service-account IAM roles give a workload access to Google APIs.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: An attached service account can supply short-lived credentials to software on the VM; Google recommends least-privilege IAM roles rather than long-lived keys.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: VPC firewall rules govern traffic to and from VMs; Google recommends restricting exposed access rather than allowing unnecessary ports.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Self-hosting the Compute Engine control plane is not applicable; Google runs the cloud service and physical infrastructure.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: The customer handles OS patching, app deployment, firewall design, secrets, capacity, incident response, and backup decisions for software inside the VM.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: Compute Engine VM disks are created in a selected zone or region; standard snapshots can be globally scoped by default or regionally scoped to restrict creation and restore locations.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: Google Cloud's privacy notice describes collection and use of account and service information, while the DPA covers customer data processed under the Cloud agreement.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Standard disk snapshots are remote, redundant backups; snapshot schedules can run hourly, daily, or weekly and have configurable retention.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Snapshot charges are based on stored snapshot data; copying snapshots between locations can add network transfer fees.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Console-created instances may preselect a default snapshot schedule or Backup and DR plan depending on whether the API is enabled; the user can change the choice.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Disk snapshots do not back up application deployment settings, external services, DNS, or data stored outside the included disks.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: VMs can be recreated from public or custom images; custom images can be exported/imported through supported image and disk workflows.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: The customer must export application files, databases, secrets, DNS, and infrastructure configuration; a VM image alone is not a complete managed app migration.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Google Cloud terms let customers terminate for convenience with notice, but outstanding fees remain due and access to customer data can end when the agreement terminates.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Google Compute Engine is Google's cloud virtual machine service, within Google Cloud.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: The Google Cloud contracting entity and billing country depend on the customer's billing profile and location.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Compute Engine is actively documented, priced, and offered through Google Cloud.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: To use Compute Engine, a project must be linked to an active Cloud Billing account, even when the project uses only free products.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: The public Google Cloud status dashboard reports service incidents; it is not a historical uptime measurement for a specific project or VM.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Under Premium Tier, the Compute Engine SLA promises 99.9% monthly uptime for a single instance of families other than memory-optimized, and 99.95% for a single memory-optimized instance; multiple-zone deployments have a different SLO.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: The SLA excludes pre-GA features and customer-caused failures; a credit request must be filed with technical support within 60 days and include logs.

facts.label: Support channels and terms

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Paid Customer Care packages provide technical case support and response targets that vary by plan and priority; Compute Engine has no separate free VM response-time promise.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Google Cloud documentation, community, status dashboard, and Billing Support are self-help or account support channels; community responses have no contractual response time.

facts.value: Compute Engine is a proprietary hosted infrastructure service; an open-source license for the hosted VM product is not applicable.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: Paid commercial use is subject to Google Cloud terms, service terms, AUP, and any third-party image license.
