facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: No single all-in ECS starting price is established. A published instance-specification reference card shows T6 t6.small.1, 1 vCPU/1 GiB, at USD 6.13/month in ap-southeast-3 (AP-Singapore).

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Published compute-specification references: C6s c6s.large.2 (2 vCPU/4 GiB) USD 42.25/month, C7n c7n.large.2 (2 vCPU/4 GiB) USD 51.30/month, both ap-southeast-1 (CN-Hong Kong).

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Published compute-specification references: aC8 ac8.large.2 (2 vCPU/4 GiB) USD 36.69/month and C9 c9.large.4 (2 vCPU/8 GiB) USD 56.98/month, both ap-southeast-3 (AP-Singapore).

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: ECS offers yearly/monthly prepaid, pay-per-use postpaid, and spot billing. Pay-per-use is measured by the second and settled hourly; yearly/monthly is paid upfront for the term.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Tax is determined by account country/region and applicable local terms. General customer-agreement prices exclude applicable VAT, sales, GST or similar transaction taxes unless country-specific terms say otherwise.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Monthly/yearly subscriptions renew at the then-current checkout/renewal amount; automatic renewal can be disabled. Unsubscribe/refund rules depend on order discounts and applicable country terms.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: The smallest verified reference flavor is T6 t6.small.1: 1 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM, USD 6.13/month reference, AP-Singapore (ap-southeast-3).

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: ECS flavors span 1–160 vCPUs on listed families and x86/Kunpeng architectures. C6s/C7n/aC8 examples above each provide 2 vCPU and 4 GiB; C9 example provides 2 vCPU and 8 GiB.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: ECS compute flavor and its boot/system EVS disk are separate billed items. New ECS creation commonly uses a system disk default of 40 GiB; additional data disks are optional and separately billed.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Public image choices include Linux distributions and paid commercial OS images; Windows images are third-party KooGallery offers. Image availability is flavor/region dependent.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Pay-per-use compute charges by second and settles hourly. The published billing guide's example uses c7n.large.2 at USD 0.0976/hour, but labels the example prices illustrative; it is not a current region-specific quote.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Other metered ECS bill items include EVS system/data disks, paid images, and EIP/public bandwidth or traffic. The billed amount depends on region, disk type, billing mode, usage and selected image.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: A 2025-11-24 official billing PDF has illustrative EVS and bandwidth rates (for example USD/GiB/hour and USD/Mbit/s/hour) but states actual prices are the current ECS pricing-details values and vary by region.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: No recurring, always-free ECS resource allowance was established from the current international free-package catalog and ECS pricing/docs checked. Limited-time/new-customer promotions may be available and are not an ongoing free plan.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Internet access for an ECS requires an EIP, a public NAT gateway or a load balancer; EIP is the direct public-IP route. EIP and ECS must be in the same region.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: EIP bills internet egress under selected bandwidth or traffic billing. The international docs say only outbound bandwidth/traffic is billed; inbound bandwidth capacity depends on the selected outbound bandwidth and region exceptions apply.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: ECS-to-ECS networking is private within the VPC/region. Cross-region/private interconnection uses separate networking services such as Cloud Connect or VPN; those charges are outside ECS.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Exact current EIP bandwidth/traffic rates and any included data amount could not be retrieved as a static published price table for one international region from the price calculator pages checked.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: ECS provides no managed source build minutes, build concurrency, build-time cap, preview-build allowance or deployment-count meter. Builds can run on the purchased VM or an external CI service.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: The customer can operate their own build and deployment tools on a compatible OS/container setup; Huawei's ECS product does not supply a managed build pipeline or Git preview workflow.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: A complete public web-server bill can include compute, required boot/system EVS disk, OS image where paid, and EIP/public bandwidth or traffic. The line items and rates vary by region.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Optional data disks, EVS snapshots, CBR backup vaults, paid marketplace/OS images, security products, public NAT, load balancing and cross-region network services are separate from ECS compute.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: The ECS system disk is released with its ECS, but separately attached data disks are not automatically deleted. A stopped pay-per-use ECS may still incur disk, EIP and bandwidth charges.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Domain registration, managed DNS, CDN delivery, managed database, TLS certificates from other services, and application monitoring are not part of the ECS compute product.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Cost Center supports daily/monthly/quarterly/yearly budget scopes and actual or forecast alert thresholds; a cost budget can be scoped to pay-per-use ECS.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Cost budget checks run hourly; a threshold notification can arrive within an hour, after actual cost has already exceeded the budget. The documentation describes alerts, not automatic suspension at the threshold.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Stopping an ordinary pay-per-use ECS stops its basic compute/image charges, but attached EVS disks, EIPs and bandwidth continue billing; some local-disk, FPGA, bare-metal and spot-block resources continue charging while stopped. Delete the instance and associated resources to stop charges.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: ECS is an always-provisioned VM until the customer stops/deletes it. No automatic scale-to-zero or request-triggered wake-up behavior is documented for ECS.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Customer can resize a VM within supported flavors; horizontal Auto Scaling policies can create/release ECSs but Auto Scaling is a separate product and its resources are separately billed.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Pay-per-use stopped ordinary instances stop billing vCPU/RAM and image but keep billing attached resources; special flavors may keep charging compute while stopped. Yearly/monthly stays prepaid until expiry.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: ECS quota caps total instance count, vCPU and RAM per account/project/region. General documented simultaneous creation caps: 100 yearly/monthly or 500 pay-per-use; actual quotas are account and region specific and can be raised by request.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Published family specs list a range up to 160 vCPU and flavor-specific memory; there is no single ECS-wide request concurrency, HTTP body, request duration or connection cap.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: ECS operations documentation advises disabling Linux kdump on 1-vCPU/1-GiB instances due to memory use. Windows guidance recommends at least 2 GiB for normal use.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Network performance, PPS, intranet bandwidth and disk IOPS ceilings vary by flavor family; the product page publishes family-level maximums, not a universal workload throughput.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Huawei Cloud account registration asks for country/region, email verification, password and a linked mobile number; an individual selects their residence country, an enterprise selects its registration country. Account country cannot be changed later.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Huawei's international free-offer FAQ says a valid payment method is needed to buy, and its free-trial FAQ lists Visa/Mastercard and says Brazil, Peru and Chile accounts are not eligible for free trials because payment methods cannot be specified there.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: No ECS-specific universal free-trial amount, duration, or payment-card requirement was published in the ECS pricing and free-offer pages checked. A time-limited offer may differ by country, new-user status, account and region.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: International customer agreement restricts transactions with sanctioned or otherwise prohibited persons/territories and requires compliance with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. It identifies sector restrictions involving Russia and Venezuela.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Paid ECS use is governed by the general customer agreement and acceptable-use policy; ordinary commercial websites and applications are not identified as categorically barred in the checked policy.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Prohibited use includes illegal or infringing conduct, harm to minors, pornography, illegal gambling, Ponzi schemes, network attacks, phishing, malware, unauthorized access, security disruption, unsolicited mass messages and deceptive offers. Huawei may suspend or terminate service for violations.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Rented, provider-hosted virtual machines. Huawei manages the cloud infrastructure and control plane; the customer selects the image/flavor and manages the guest OS, app, runtime, patches, and application data.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: ECS can run on x86 or Kunpeng Arm families. Supported virtualization architectures include KVM and QingTian; Xen is legacy/EOS.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Suitable for websites, APIs, databases, development/test environments, and long-running processes that can be installed on a supported guest OS.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: General-purpose VM can host arbitrary OS-compatible application code, subject to flavor support, quota, law, customer agreement and acceptable-use rules. It does not provide managed static-site, app-platform or serverless hosting features.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: ECS can be placed in the international sites' listed China and overseas regions, including Hong Kong, Bangkok, Singapore, Jakarta, Kuala Lumpur, Manila, Riyadh, Cairo, Johannesburg, Istanbul, Mexico City, São Paulo, Santiago, Buenos Aires and Lima, plus listed mainland China regions.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Price-card region codes used here: ap-southeast-1 = CN-Hong Kong; ap-southeast-3 = AP-Singapore. Values are stated only for those exact regions.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: ECS compute runs in the selected region/AZ. Region and AZ cannot be changed after purchase; creating a server in another region requires a separate ECS/migration.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Instance and vCPU/RAM quotas differ by region. Yearly/monthly mode allows up to 100 ECSs created at one time; pay-per-use allows up to 500, subject to account and regional quotas.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: ECS images include supported Linux distributions and Windows choices; x86 and Kunpeng Arm architectures are offered on different flavor families.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Customer can install OS-compatible languages, runtimes and web frameworks, or bring a compatible image; containers can be run as guest-OS software but ECS does not manage them as a container platform.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: The exact runtime versions included with each current ECS image and availability by region/flavor were not presented as one stable product-wide matrix in the image and ECS pages checked.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: No ECS-managed framework adapter or feature matrix for Next.js SSR/streaming/ISR, Django, Rails or similar app frameworks was published in the ECS product pages checked.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: ECS best-practice examples show manually deploying websites, Docker, Node.js and WordPress on a customer-managed VM; they do not certify framework-specific streaming, server rendering, cache revalidation or request behavior.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Create/manage ECS through the Huawei Cloud console and ECS REST APIs; SSH/RDP or console access can be used to copy or install app code.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Source repositories can be pulled with customer-installed Git/CI tools or code copied from a local machine. No native GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket deployment connection or private-repository feature is listed for ECS.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Custom system images may be created from ECS or imported; private images can package OS and application software for reuse.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Long-running worker processes can run under the guest OS, under the customer's service manager/process supervisor. ECS does not impose a separate worker class or per-worker price.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Cron and OS-level scheduled jobs are self-managed. There is no ECS-managed cron schedule, job duration limit or scheduler price in the product docs checked.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: ECS provides VPC networking; security groups control inbound/outbound protocols and ports. A security group is associated with the instance, with a default group created if none exists.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: TCP/HTTP(S), streaming and WebSockets are handled by the customer-installed OS/app/network configuration; ECS does not publish an application-protocol or WebSocket guarantee. UDP can be configured at network/OS level subject to security rules and selected network features.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Public IPv4 uses a separate EIP or gateway/load balancer. EIP is static and region-bound; traffic and bandwidth rates depend on the EIP mode and region.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Private networking is available within VPCs and can be linked across regions using separate Cloud Connect or VPN products.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: ECS system/data disks use EVS persistent block storage; system disk is tied to its ECS lifecycle, but attached data disks may remain after instance deletion. Local-disk flavors have different persistence/recovery behavior.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Disk capacities/types and expansion depend on EVS and flavor constraints; EVS is billed separately. Files stored only on local ephemeral disks may be lost during host or flavor events.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: No product-wide app filesystem capacity/backup guarantee is published independently of the selected EVS/local disk and backup configuration.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Customers can install and administer self-managed databases on ECS. Huawei's separately managed RDS/GaussDB services are not part of ECS.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: EVS is block disk; OBS is object storage; EIP/VPC supplies networking; CBR provides backups. These attach to or support ECS but are separately metered services.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Auto Scaling, ELB, Cloud Eye and Cloud Connect can support multi-instance deployments; these are separate products and do not turn a single ECS into a managed app platform.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: ECS does not include a registered custom domain. Use a separately acquired domain and DNS record that points to the ECS public IP/load balancer.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: HTTPS/TLS is configured by the customer in the guest web server, or by a separate Huawei service such as ELB/SCM. ECS itself does not promise automatic certificate issue or renewal.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: No ECS product-level included domain count, managed wildcard certificate or certificate-renewal limit was published in the product/docs pages checked.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Build, staging, rollout, health checks, traffic switching and rollback are customer-managed using OS tools or separate services. ECS is not a managed preview-deployment system.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Customer can create images/backups and create/restore ECS resources from them; image/backup is not a transaction-aware app release or automatic database rollback feature.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: ECS documentation does not set a universal health-check gate, rolling deploy, preview URL, or automatic application rollback workflow.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: ECS supports Cloud Eye basic instance metrics; installing the supported agent enables additional OS/process monitoring metrics. Cloud Eye is a separate service.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Application and OS logs are generated and retained on the guest OS according to customer configuration. No ECS-managed application log retention period or export allowance was published.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Eye alarm rules and service logs/metrics can be configured separately; no complete ECS app-log rate, retention or paid-export schedule was established from the ECS monitoring page.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Console access is through Huawei Cloud accounts/IAM; ECS supports SSH key pairs/passwords for Linux and remote console/VNC access. SSH exposure requires appropriate security-group and guest-firewall rules.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Secrets inside the app/OS are customer-managed. IAM roles/permissions and credential policies are account configuration; ECS does not document a separate app-secret vault feature.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: ECS is a VM rather than a no-root managed app runtime; guest OS administrative access is available subject to image and account permissions.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Not a self-hosted control panel or software deploy tool: Huawei operates the cloud control plane and physical infrastructure. No customer hardware minimum or controller installation is required.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Customer maintains OS/runtime/app, secrets, firewall, patches, backups and application recovery. The guest OS and app continue on ECS; customer must maintain service access and recovery configuration.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: If the Huawei Cloud console/control plane is unavailable, guest workloads may remain running but management operations can be impaired; no ECS-specific customer-facing control-plane outage behavior guarantee was found in the service guide.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The privacy statement says customers choose the region where service content is stored and Huawei does not move content across regions without authorization, subject to applicable agreement and law.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The privacy statement describes account/personal information and operational/support data processing, including possible cross-border access/transfer under stated safeguards and consent/legal bases. It does not promise that all logs, billing records, support records and backups remain in the ECS region.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: CBR vaults and replicated backup locations are separate configuration choices; backup/data location cannot be inferred from the compute region alone.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: ECS does not include automatic backup by default. CBR cloud-server backup can cover all EVS disks, or cloud-disk backup can cover selected disks; the customer buys a vault and enables a policy.

facts.label: Backups and restore

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: The base VPS plans are sold at a monthly price, not by request, build minute, CPU second, or memory second. The page advertises unlimited traffic up to 1 Gbit/s.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: The current offer describes optional additional VMs, load balancing, private networking, block storage, and object storage as add-ons. The price of each VPS+-specific add-on was not published on the checked public product pages.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: No recurring free VPS plan is listed. IONOS advertises a 30-day free-trial or money-back offer for VPS; this is a time-limited purchase guarantee, not an ongoing free allowance.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: VPS+ pages advertise unlimited inbound/outbound traffic at up to 1 Gbit/s and no additional traffic charge for ordinary use.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Server terms reserve IONOS's right to reduce bandwidth for excessive use or use that impairs shared infrastructure. No public per-GB overage rate for ordinary VPS+ traffic was found.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: VPS+ is not a hosted Git build service. The product includes one-click installation of selected apps; custom builds and deployment pipelines must be run by the customer on the VM or through a separate CI provider.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: If builds run on the VM, their CPU, RAM, and disk use the plan's included resources; no separate build-minute meter is listed. Separate CI-provider fees are outside the VPS price.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: One-time setup is advertised as $0 in the US; £10 in the UK; and €10 in Germany. UK prices exclude VAT; Germany prices include VAT; US sales tax may apply.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: One IPv4 address and an IPv6 /80 network are listed as included. Additional IPv4 is listed at $5/month in the US, £5/month before VAT in the UK, and €5/month in Germany.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Optional Cloud Backup starts at $0.065/GB/month in the US, £0.045/GB/month before VAT in the UK, and €0.06/GB/month in Germany. Plesk is listed at $6/month, £5/month, and €5/month respectively.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Current pages mark extra VMs, load balancing, block storage, and object storage as optional/pay-as-you-go, but the exact VPS+-specific rates are not shown. Optional domain registration is also separate.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: The base VM is a fixed monthly subscription. Optional VPS+ add-ons are pay-as-you-go and may add variable charges. The Cloud Panel provides cost and invoice views for server services.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: I found no public customer-set hard spending cap or automatic stop-at-budget control for VPS+ in the pricing pages, help pages, or server terms checked.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: The base VM is a fixed subscription, not scale-to-zero or request-metered compute. Suspending/stopping the VM is available in the Cloud Panel, but the VPS subscription does not become a free plan when the VM is off.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: VPS+ markets up to 5 additional VMs by default, optional load balancing, and pay-as-you-go add-ons; a VPS+ help page says its base plan cannot be changed. The generic server terms say VMs cannot be added or removed.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: No platform-level request count, request-duration, or app-concurrency quota is published for the self-managed VPS. App limits depend on the server resources and customer software.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: The current public plan limits are the selected vCore, RAM, base NVMe disk, and up-to-1-Gbit/s external connection.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: IONOS advertises 30 days to try the VPS or receive a refund in the US, UK, and Germany. The public pages do not clearly state whether payment is collected first for each country's current VPS+ promotion.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: IONOS.com account eligibility is limited to the countries listed in its Geoscope Optimization help page; the list includes India and the United States. IONOS says accounts with addresses outside the supported list may have to be cancelled.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Public pages checked did not state a VPS+ credit-card requirement, identity-check rule, or complete country-by-country payment-method list.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: IONOS says VPS+ may be used for commercial or non-commercial purposes.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: US server terms prohibit cryptocurrency mining and unauthorized copyrighted content. UK acceptable-use rules also prohibit spam, illegal material, and adult material; they require customers to avoid excessive server load.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: This is a rented, fully virtualized server with a public IP, root or administrator access, and a fixed base plan. IONOS supplies the underlying server, network, and Cloud Panel; the customer administers the operating system and applications.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Current product pages advertise extra VMs, VM cloning, load balancing, private networking, block storage, and object storage as VPS+ options. The US and UK server terms describe a VPS as one VM with no add/remove-server feature, API, load balancing, VPN, or shared storage.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: IONOS names web servers, email servers, online shops, and development servers as VPS use cases. It explicitly says the product can be used for commercial and non-commercial purposes.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: A static site or arbitrary-code web app can be installed on the VM, but the VPS plan itself is not a managed static-site deployment service or global CDN.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Current VPS+ pages list the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and Spain as selectable data-center countries. The German page summarizes the choices as EU, US, and UK.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Server location is chosen when ordering and cannot be changed afterward under the server terms. I found no VPS+-included CDN or edge delivery network.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Current pages list AlmaLinux, Debian, Rocky Linux, and Ubuntu, plus Windows Server 2022 or 2025. IONOS says the images use current OS versions; customer installs and maintains application runtimes.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: VPS+ includes full virtualization and full root access. The page does not provide a managed language/runtime version matrix or an explicit customer container-runtime guarantee; one-click app templates may install Docker for selected apps.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: No managed framework adapter or framework-specific deployment path is listed. With root access, the customer installs a framework and its dependencies on the selected OS.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: The one-click catalogue names apps such as n8n, OpenClaw, and Vaultwarden, but it does not document supported versions or framework feature matrices for every app.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: One-click app install is available during order or later. Linux access uses SSH; Windows uses RDP; the Cloud Panel also provides a KVM console and server/image management.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: A source repository can be checked out by the customer over SSH or through software installed on the VM. No built-in Git provider connection, private-repository integration, or automatic push-to-deploy workflow is listed.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Long-running workers and scheduled tasks can be installed and managed by the customer on the always-on VM, subject to the plan resources and server use terms.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Each VPS has a public IPv4 address and IPv6 /80. The hardware firewall is configurable; default image rules allow common inbound server ports, and extra inbound ports/protocols can be configured.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: The VPS getting-started guide says outbound SMTP port 25 is blocked by default and can be unblocked by contacting customer support.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: The current product page does not publish an application request timeout or a managed WebSocket/streaming service limit. Those behaviors are configured in the customer's OS and application; detailed fixed-IP, private-network, and load-balancer terms are unclear because the VPS+ feature list conflicts with generic VPS terms.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: The included NVMe disk is the VM's server storage. VPS+ also advertises attachable persistent block storage; the customer formats and mounts it in the OS.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Server images can be created manually or at regular intervals and used for restore/clone workflows. These images are not a substitute for a separately configured off-server backup plan.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: No managed PostgreSQL, MySQL, queue, or application authentication service is listed as part of the base VPS+ plan. The customer can install and manage a database on the VM.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Current VPS+ pages list optional extra VMs, private networking, load balancing, block storage, and object storage. Their VPS+-specific billing details are not shown publicly on the pages checked.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: The German canonical product page lists two 2-GB mailboxes and DNS management, and describes domains as optional add-ons.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Product pages list unlimited external domains, DNS management, an included IPv4, an IPv6 /80, and a wildcard SSL certificate. Domain registration is optional and billed separately.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: The VPS getting-started guide explains pointing a domain's A/AAAA record to the server IP. Customer configures the web server and application for HTTPS; no hosted preview-domain feature is listed.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: IONOS provides VM images and cloning features for recovery/testing, but the customer controls app deployment and release promotion.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: No managed pull-request preview, deployment health gate, or application-level rollback workflow is documented for VPS+.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: The product page describes high-speed server images as point-in-time snapshots for restoring a prior server state. Detailed VPS+ image retention, included image count, and any extra image charge are not given there.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: The Cloud Panel Monitoring Center can chart CPU, RAM, storage, network, ping, ports, and processes; the Monitoring Agent is needed for some disk/process details.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Panel monitoring can show resource charts, reports, and warnings. The checked pages do not state a fixed retention period for VPS+ app logs or provide a hosted build-log service.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Panel has an action log for account users, while server/application log collection and retention are the customer's responsibility.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: VPS+ provides SSH for Linux, RDP for Windows, a KVM console, and root/administrator access. The server terms assign security and software updates to the customer.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Cloud Panel supports additional user accounts, assigned roles, and two-factor authentication controls; no hosted application-secret manager is listed for the base VPS plan.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Server terms allow IONOS or technical suppliers to access physical hosts when needed to resolve technical incidents; they state that IONOS has no regular administrative access to the VM content.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Not applicable as a self-hosted deployment-control-plane product: IONOS rents the VM and runs the provider infrastructure. The customer must maintain the guest OS, app stack, security, and backups.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The server location is chosen at order time. IONOS offers a data-processing agreement for customers processing personal data; it is included in the UK terms for newer contracts.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The checked VPS marketing and server terms do not give a complete per-data-type residency commitment covering VM data, logs, support records, and optional backups.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud Backup is an optional paid add-on for VPS. It can back up full servers, disks, volumes, files, folders, and databases; the customer installs the agent and configures the schedule and retention.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud Backup starts at $0.065/GB/month in the US, £0.045/GB/month before VAT in the UK, and €0.06/GB/month in Germany. Extra stored GB may add to the invoice.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: IONOS server terms require customers to back up their own data; IONOS disclaims responsibility for backup loss or accidental deletion under the backup terms.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Linux customers can access the VM through SSH and can copy source, application data, or database dumps to another host. IONOS server images can restore within the same IONOS data center but are not documented as a general-purpose export format.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: On contract expiry, US terms warn that service access ends and underlying data, including server configurations, may be permanently deleted. Back up before cancellation.

facts.value: Current product page calls the current line IONOS VPS / VPS+. The listed directory URL is https://www.ionos.com/servers/vps.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: The IONOS company page says the brand changed from 1&1 IONOS to IONOS in January 2020, and says IONOS is a member of United Internet. The contracting company differs by market: IONOS Inc. in the US terms, IONOS Cloud Ltd. in the UK server terms, and IONOS SE in Germany.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Current US, UK, and German product pages list VPS+ plans and an order button. The product is marketed to new buyers.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Some legacy VPS customers are subject to a 2026 price adjustment. IONOS sends the affected account its exact new price and effective date.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Product pages advertise 99.99% VPS+ availability. The IONOS status page separately lists VPS and showed VPS Operational on 2026-11-06.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: I did not find a VPS-specific contractual 99.99% SLA, measurement method, or service-credit schedule in the US/UK/German server terms checked.

facts.value: VPS pages advertise 24/7 expert support. US support lists phone, help center, and live chat; the UK support page lists 24/7 phone support.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Included help covers IONOS interfaces, hardware, network, base installations, account issues, and provisioning. Programming, third-party software installation/configuration, and general website development are excluded or paid/unsupported.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Public product and support pages do not promise a VPS-specific response or resolution time.

facts.value: Not a software product with a customer-installed deployer license. The hosting service is governed by IONOS's market-specific general/server terms; customer-installed software remains subject to its own licenses.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: The US and UK server terms require the customer to keep required third-party software licenses and assign operating-system/application updates to the customer.

apps.name: Kamatera Cloud Servers
apps.line: Configure cloud servers with selectable compute, storage, and regions.

free.text: One-time 30-day trial: 1 server ≤$100, 1 TB; card required

work.math: 1 Type A VM = $4 a month server subtotal. 100 GB fits its 5 TB allowance (1 TB in some zones). Builds, domain and tax are not included.
1 Type B VM = $25 a month for 730 hours. 2 vCPU and 2 GB, and 5 TB, cover 100 GB, but request capacity is untested. Domain and tax are not included.

work.math: 2 × $25 = $50 a month server subtotal. The 7-day daily backup needs a quote, and private-network traffic pricing is not verified.

facts.label: Persistent app files

facts.label: Persistent app files

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Postgres, MySQL, Redis and other software can be installed and maintained by the customer on a Cloud Server. Kamatera also has self-install database guides and marketplace images.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Block storage, private networks, load balancers, firewall, object storage and DNS are listed as separate Kamatera products or add-ons, with their own charges or configuration.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Custom domains work by pointing DNS A records to the VM's public IP and configuring a guest web server; domain registration and DNS changes are handled by the customer or registrar.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: HTTPS can be configured by the customer with Certbot and Let's Encrypt on a Linux VM. Kamatera does not present an automatic app-platform certificate workflow for Cloud Servers.

facts.value: The customer manages releases and deployment checks in the VM. Server creation supports custom install scripts and disk images; image cloning supports reuse across zones.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: No managed preview environment, health-check gate, rolling app release or app-version rollback system is documented for Cloud Servers.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Application and build logs are produced by customer-installed software and remain the customer's responsibility to retain or export.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Customers can add users and assign permissions to servers; the VM itself is accessed with customer-managed credentials or SSH keys.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Customer is responsible for securing the virtual environment, account boundaries, OS, applications, access controls and secrets.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The DPA says customers can select data-center locations for Customer Data and Kamatera will not transfer Customer Data from the selected locations except as needed to provide customer-initiated services, as requested, or as required by law.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Manual snapshots are point-in-time disk copies that can be reverted or committed/deleted. They are distinct from the separately billed daily backup service.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Terms say Kamatera does not guarantee customer backups and makes the customer responsible for maintaining backups.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Customers can terminate hourly services at any time; monthly cancellation stops later billing but the prepaid current month is not refunded.

facts.label: Exit and portability

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Customer-uploaded disk images can be stored in chosen Kamatera zones and cloned into another zone.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Kamatera Cloud Servers; official product name “Cloud Servers”; parent company The OMC Group. Kamatera says OMC has offered cloud services since 1995.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership

facts.label: Operating and signup status

facts.label: Operating and signup status

facts.value: The product page markets a 99.95% uptime guarantee for Cloud Servers.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history

facts.label: Support channels and terms

facts.label: Support channels and terms

facts.value: Not a separate deploy-software license: Kamatera sells proprietary hosted infrastructure, while customer-installed software follows its own license. The service is governed by Kamatera Terms and AUP.

apps.line: Build and deploy Laravel apps on managed cloud infrastructure.

free.text: 31 days no fee; $5/mo credit; excess billed; payment required; evaluation only

work.math: $12 a month subtotal for an awake replica running 730 hours, after the $5 credit. Add $0.10 per GB over the earned allowance for 100 GB of data sent out, plus other traffic.
$12 a month subtotal after one $5 credit, for 730 hours. Add $0.10 per GB over the earned allowance. API capacity for 1 million requests is untested.
$55.69 a month subtotal: 0.5 compute units (CU) for 730 hours + 10 GB storage after one credit. The 10 GB database traffic, backup rate and 7-day copies are not confirmed.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Starter $5/month plus usage, including $5 monthly usage credit; first 31 days fee waived.

facts.label: Higher plan base fees
facts.value: Growth $20/month; Business $200/month, each plus usage and $5 monthly usage credit. Enterprise custom pricing/allowances.

facts.label: Currency, tax and renewal
facts.value: General terms specify United States Dollars, exclude taxes and state payments are from within the United States unless agreed otherwise; recurring plans renew at then-current rates.

facts.label: Cancellation and refund terms
facts.value: Written non-renewal notice at least 30 days before term end; account cancellation takes effect next renewal period; no ordinary prorated refund for the current term.

facts.label: Flex compute, current self-service sizes

facts.label: Pro compute and architecture
facts.value: US East table: Pro 1 vCPU/4 GiB, 2/8 GiB, 4/16 GiB, 8/32 GiB; compute runs on AWS Graviton EC2.

facts.value: Per replica, every 1 GB RAM gives 512 MB ephemeral disk; each replica has its own disk.

facts.label: Compute rates: other listed regions

facts.label: Meter and monthly cap
facts.value: App/Worker replica running time billed per second, capped at 28 days (2,419,200 seconds) per replica per billing cycle.

facts.label: Native Serverless Postgres rates
facts.value: Public price data: CPU $0.106/hour; database storage $0.50/GB-month. Docs say active compute is metered per second.

facts.label: Postgres backup history rate
facts.value: Numeric $/GB-month backup-history price could not be verified.

facts.label: Managed queue operation meter
facts.value: Standard $1 per 1 million operations; FIFO $1.10 per 1 million; polling baseline approximately $0.13/queue/month, plus worker time.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: No ongoing $0 subscription in the current offer: Starter renews at $5/month with $5 usage credit.

facts.label: Inactivity and retained resources
facts.value: Sign in/use at least once every two years unless an active subscription, credit balance or another listed activity keeps the account active.

facts.label: Transfer allowance and overage
facts.value: Running compute earns a per-second organization-wide allowance; Flex 1 GiB example earns 100 GB/month; excess $0.10/GB.

facts.label: Which traffic counts
facts.value: Cached edge delivery, app incoming request/response traffic, and external API/database connection request/response traffic count; internal Cloud Network transfers excluded.

facts.label: Database/cache transfer boundary
facts.value: Laravel MySQL, Valkey and Reverb are internal; partner-managed resources, including Serverless Postgres, count as external.

facts.label: Allowance precision
facts.value: Exact per-second allowance factor and treatment after the 28-day compute charge cap were not established for every size.

facts.label: Build costs and timeout
facts.value: Unlimited builds on all plans; build commands and deploy commands each time out after 15 minutes.

facts.label: Builder specification and concurrency
facts.value: Builder CPU/RAM/disk and concurrent build ceiling not found.

facts.label: Domains, people and optional services
facts.value: All current plans list unlimited team members; included custom domains vary by plan; extras $0.25/domain/month.

facts.label: Object storage rates
facts.value: $0.02/GB-month; Class A $0.005 per 1,000 operations; Class B $0.0005 per 1,000 operations; data access free.

facts.label: Log drain add-on
facts.value: Enterprise drains: $0.0685/hour metered per second, plus $0.25/GB uncompressed logs metered per byte; transferred bytes can incur bandwidth overage.

facts.label: Deletion does not remove every billable resource
facts.value: Deleting an application deletes its environments, but databases, caches and buckets remain until separately deleted.

facts.label: Spend protection controls
facts.value: Organization spending limits default to alerts; optional Stop all compute pauses compute and blocks new resource provisioning.

facts.label: Charges and restart after stop
facts.value: In-flight work may create a small overage; storage continues billing; limit raise/removal or a new billing cycle resumes paused compute.

facts.label: Marketing conflict
facts.value: Pricing promises never going over budget and an FAQ says compute pauses automatically; detailed spend docs make shutdown opt-in and allow residual charges.

facts.label: Scale-to-zero and billing
facts.value: Flex can sleep after no inbound app requests for its configured sleep timeout; no app compute charge while sleeping. Pro is for always-on workloads.

facts.label: Autoscaling plans
facts.value: Starter one replica/no horizontal scaling; Growth 1 to 10 replicas by default with increase requests; Business unlimited and scheduled autoscaling; Enterprise custom.

facts.label: Scheduled wake and stop
facts.value: Scheduler wakes sleeping environments; stopping an environment shuts all App/Worker clusters and tasks, but attached resources remain billable.

facts.label: Execution and allocation limits
facts.value: Build command 15 minutes; deploy command 15 minutes; one-off Commands non-interactive and at most 30 minutes; 30 linked organization secrets/environment.

facts.label: Apps and request capacity
facts.value: Unlimited apps/environments; current Flex tops at 2 GiB; PHP worker capacity estimated by provider as floor(memory MB/30), with one request per PHP worker.

facts.label: HTTP body and duration ceilings
facts.value: Exact maximum HTTP body size, request duration and adjustable proxy timeout range not found.

facts.label: Trial and payment details
facts.value: New Starter: first 31 days without the $5 fee and $5 usage credit; payment details required; excess usage is charged even during the first 31 days.

facts.label: Eligibility and payment unknowns
facts.value: Specific accepted card networks/payment methods, identity checks and complete country acceptance list not found.

facts.label: Age and sanctions
facts.value: Users must be at least 18; sanctioned persons and uses prohibited by applicable law are excluded.

facts.label: Commercial use: paid hosting
facts.value: Paid product is marketed for production SaaS and ecommerce; Starter documentation explicitly describes small real-world production apps.

facts.label: Trial/beta restrictions
facts.value: Terms restrict beta services, evaluations, free trials and promotions to personal, non-commercial evaluation.

facts.label: Acceptable use restrictions
facts.value: Terms prohibit illegal/infringing/harmful content, unsolicited bulk advertising, mining, proxy/VPN/VPS uses, scraping, competing hosting services, and primary downloadable-content/remote-storage uses.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Fully managed app platform on AWS EC2; Laravel provisions, builds, deploys, secures and patches infrastructure.

facts.label: Private Cloud edition
facts.value: Laravel-managed dedicated AWS account/VPC, Kubernetes cluster, isolated nodes, NAT gateways and optional RDS/ElastiCache.

facts.label: Suitable app types and overlap
facts.value: Public websites, APIs, server-rendered apps, Nuxt generated sites, long-lived workers and managed supporting resources; multiple supported languages.

facts.label: Application regions
facts.value: Virginia us-east-1; Ohio us-east-2; Canada Central ca-central-1; Frankfurt eu-central-1; Ireland eu-west-1; London eu-west-2; Singapore ap-southeast-1; Sydney ap-southeast-2; Tokyo ap-northeast-1.

facts.label: Region enum discrepancy
facts.value: Public API schema additionally includes Paris eu-west-3 and UAE me-central-1; current app docs/pricing do not list them.

facts.label: Delivery and data-resource regions
facts.value: Cloudflare global edge delivery is distinct from AWS app location; a Serverless Postgres attachment must match the app region.

facts.label: PHP and JavaScript runtimes
facts.value: PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5; Node.js 22, 24, 26; Bun 1.3/1.4; Deno 2.9. Current defaults PHP 8.5, Node 26, Bun 1.4.

facts.label: Other native runtimes
facts.value: Go 1.25/1.26/1.27; Python 3.10 through 3.14; Ruby 3.3/3.4/4.0; recent stable Rust or repository-pinned toolchain.

facts.label: Bring-your-own container
facts.value: Public Dockerfile/container-image import workflow not established.

facts.label: Laravel and Symfony behavior
facts.value: Laravel 9+ with documented minimum minors for 9/10/11; Symfony 7.4 LTS or 8.x. Octane/FrankenPHP and Inertia SSR toggles for Laravel.

facts.label: Next.js behavior
facts.value: Runs next start on Node/Bun/Deno; ISR/data cache is local per replica and reset at deploy unless a shared custom cache handler is configured.

facts.label: Nuxt and Python behavior
facts.value: Nuxt supports server or generated-static mode with default Nitro node-server preset; Python guides cover Django, FastAPI and Flask with WSGI/ASGI servers.

facts.label: Detailed streaming feature matrix
facts.value: App-router streaming, server-sent events and all framework-specific edge features are not individually certified by the checked deployment guides.

facts.label: Source inputs
facts.value: GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repositories via authorization; Cloud follows provider permissions, including private repository access granted to its integration.

facts.label: Deploy tools and automation
facts.value: Push-to-deploy, dashboard deploy, deploy hooks with optional branch commit hash, public API and cloud CLI; self-hosted GitLab for Private Cloud.

facts.label: Background workers
facts.value: Custom long-lived processes can run on App compute; dedicated Worker clusters size/scale independently and are offered from Growth upward.

facts.label: Managed queues
facts.value: Managed Laravel/Symfony queues: Starter 1, Growth 10 by default, Business/Enterprise 50 per environment; worker compute plus operation billing.

facts.label: Scheduler
facts.value: Laravel schedule:run every minute with toggle; Cloud Scheduler supports recurring commands for other supported stacks, wakes sleeping apps, and logs failures.

facts.label: Worker sleeping and legacy queues
facts.value: Dedicated workers can stay awake or follow App sleep; following sleep can interrupt jobs. Legacy queue cluster sunset September 30, 2026.

facts.label: HTTP routing and public ports
facts.value: Public HTTP traffic enters Cloudflare edge and reaches private app compute through Laravel's proxy; app runtime listens on PORT, typically 3000 for non-PHP.

facts.label: WebSocket service
facts.value: Managed Laravel Reverb WebSocket server is an additional resource; entry tier 100 concurrent connections, 200,000 messages/day, 10kb maximum message, $5/month.

facts.label: Outbound IPs and private networking
facts.value: Shared outbound IP ranges are published and may change; Private Cloud has customer-specific outbound IPs and private AWS connectivity.

facts.label: Protocol/timeout unknowns
facts.value: Arbitrary public TCP/UDP, generic app-proxy WebSocket/SSE guarantees and exact HTTP idle/connection timeouts not found.

facts.label: Persistent app files

facts.value: Laravel Object Storage automatically deletes .html and .htm uploads unless support grants an exception.

facts.label: Managed resources

facts.label: Private Cloud and legacy services
facts.value: Private Cloud offers managed RDS MySQL/Postgres and ElastiCache; Upstash Redis is deprecated and unavailable for new caches.

facts.label: Domains and HTTPS
facts.value: Free per-environment laravel.cloud address; custom domains and automatic certificate issue/renewal including wildcard setup.

facts.label: Domain quotas

facts.label: Preview environments
facts.value: Starter one preview automation per org for one target; Growth/Business unlimited. PR previews default to isolated resources, sleep and removal on PR merge/close.

facts.label: Release health and rollout
facts.value: Managed startup/readiness/liveness checks gate deployment traffic; default checks test infrastructure, optional HTTP health endpoint can validate the app.

facts.label: Recovery to earlier code

facts.label: Logs and retention
facts.value: Application, access and scheduled-command logs; retention Starter 1 day, Growth 7 days, Business 30 days, or storage quota first.

facts.label: Metrics and alerts
facts.value: Resource/request metrics and email/Slack alerts for high CPU/RAM, crashes, deploy failures, spend and domain/certificate issues.

facts.label: Log export and app monitoring
facts.value: Enterprise S3 log drains available; Laravel Nightwatch integration requires its package/token and is a separate monitoring product.

facts.label: Permissions and secrets
facts.value: Starter Admin/Developer roles; Growth all team roles; Business/Enterprise add custom roles and resource-scoped Restricted role. Organization secrets encrypted and injected on redeploy.

facts.label: Sign-in and infrastructure access
facts.value: Two-factor authentication listed across plans; Enterprise SSO on pricing, with SAML 2.0/OIDC documented. Private Cloud has no customer AWS console access.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to hosted and Laravel-managed Private Cloud editions; Laravel operates the infrastructure.

facts.label: Data location and privacy scope

facts.label: Object storage residency controls

facts.label: DPA and platform-wide residency
facts.value: Trust Center lists a Data Processing Agreement, but its full body was not available in these unauthenticated text fetches.

facts.label: MySQL backups
facts.value: Automatic daily backups configurable 1 to 30 days; presets Dev 1/Prod 7/Scale 14 days. Backup window 3AM to 6AM EDT; manual snapshots also available.

facts.label: Postgres backup/restore
facts.value: Postgres has configurable days of point-in-time recovery history; public restore API supports a timestamp or snapshot and creates a new database.

facts.label: Postgres daily backup detail
facts.value: Native seven-day daily copies, retention range and verifiable backup-history numeric rate remain unresolved.

facts.label: App/object backup duties
facts.value: Whole-app/filesystem restore guarantee and object bucket snapshot/version policy not established.

facts.label: Database and file exit

facts.label: Operating and signup status

facts.label: Complete SLA terms
facts.value: Self-service uptime percentage and full sales-led credit formula, claim deadline and exclusions not found in the checked public agreement pages.

facts.value: Hosted proprietary service governed by Laravel Cloud Terms; no customer-installed Cloud server license applicable.

facts.value: Deploying arbitrary customer Docker/OCI images as production app containers not established.

facts.label: Framework behavior

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Opt-in skew protection routes requests to matching deploy, but client fetch needs deployment ID handling; experimental automatic fetch feature not production-ready.

facts.value: Native Git deployment supports GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and Cursor Origin; CLI, API digest/ZIP and folder upload also documented.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools

facts.value: Background Functions available on credit Free/Personal/Pro and Enterprise, up to 15 minutes; return 202 immediately. Failed work can retry after one minute and again two minutes later.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs

facts.label: Network and connection support

facts.label: Domains and HTTPS

facts.label: Preview, release and recovery

facts.label: Preview, release and recovery

facts.label: Preview, release and recovery

facts.label: Logs and monitoring

facts.label: Logs and monitoring
facts.value: Lambda-compatible historical logs truncated to last 4 KB/invocation; log-drain entry max 700 KB. Enterprise Drains export traffic, Function, Edge, deploy and WAF logs.

facts.label: Logs and monitoring
facts.value: Observability history: Free/Personal one day, Pro seven days, Enterprise 30 days. Personal visitor analytics/RUM retention pricing says seven days, plan docs say 24h.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Environment variables stored encrypted; deploy-context/scoped values supported. Secret-marked values write-only except dev context, cannot unmark to reveal.

facts.label: Access and secret handling

facts.value: Current complete subprocessor/location list could not be retrieved: legal list redirects to inaccessible Trust Center item.

work.math: Assuming 730 hours: $2.7375 for runtime + $6 for 100 GB of data sent out + $0.3333 for 100 build minutes = $9.0708 before images ($0.08 per GB a month), logs (over 10 GB) and tax. API rounding gives $9.2533.
730 hours of runtime at $18.25 + 100 GB of data sent out at $6 + 100 build minutes at $0.3333 = $24.5833 before images, logs (over 10 GB) and tax. Capacity is untested.

The small app API's $24.5833 + $12.1667 for the database (0.5 vCPU and 1 GiB for 730 hours) + $1.1657 for a 10 GiB disk = $37.9157. Images, logs, 7-day backup storage and 10 GB database transfer are not priced.
