facts.label: Plan entry and base fees
facts.value: Sandbox is free with up to $20/month resources and resource-count limits. Pay as you go bills selected resources with no seat fee; Enterprise has a custom platform/usage/support agreement.

facts.label: Smallest paid compute
facts.value: Public plan list: nf-compute-10 has 0.1 vCPU/256 MiB, $2.70/month and displayed $0.004/hour; nf-compute-100-1 has 1 vCPU/1024 MiB, $18/month and $0.025/hour.

facts.label: Currency and taxes
facts.value: Payments are USD. Pricing estimates exclude VAT/GST; required taxes are added to invoices. Terms also allow adding sales tax.

facts.label: Billing timing
facts.value: Resources are configured/consumed and prorated to the second. Pricing describes end-of-month billing; newer billing-threshold docs default new accounts to a $50 automatic invoice/charge threshold.

facts.label: Cancellation and refunds
facts.value: All purchases/resource consumption are non-refundable under the general terms. Deleting an account bills remaining usage/pending invoices; resources must finish terminating to stop their charges.

facts.label: Larger deployment allocations
facts.value: Public plans include 2 vCPU/4, 8 or 16 GiB; 4/8 or 16 GiB; 8/8, 16, 24, 32 or 40 GiB; 12/24 GiB; 16/32 GiB; 20/40 GiB; 32/128 or 488 GiB.

facts.label: CPU tenancy and dedicated options
facts.value: Dedicated compute, custom managed-cloud plans and physical bare metal are documented, but a complete exclusivity/processor-tenancy rule for every standard nf-compute size is not established.

facts.label: Build allocations
facts.value: Plans supporting build include nf-compute-400-16: 4 vCPU/16 GiB and nf-compute-800-8: 8 vCPU/8 GiB, through 20 vCPU/40 GiB.

facts.label: Default runtime resources and disk
facts.value: Selected default managed-cloud quotas: 8 vCPU, 16 GiB memory, 2 GiB ephemeral disk and 64 MiB shared memory per standard CPU instance.

facts.label: CPU and memory usage rates
facts.value: Pricing displays $0.01667/vCPU-hour and $0.00833/GB-hour on Northflank Cloud, prorated per second; CPU and memory are allocated container resources.

facts.label: Displayed hourly/monthly precision
facts.value: For example, nf-compute-10 API displays $0.004/hour versus $2.70/month; pricing-widget monthly-to-hour conversion gives $2.70/720 = $0.00375/hour.

facts.label: BYOC fee
facts.value: Current public pricing charges $0.02083 per managed node-vCPU-hour; Northflank memory/disk/network columns say not billed. Underlying cloud bills remain separate.

facts.label: GPU and prepaid access
facts.value: Managed GPU prices are per second with model-specific hourly rates; BYOC GPU management is $1/GB VRAM-month in addition to the customer's GPU infrastructure. Managed GPU access requires a $50+ credit purchase.

facts.label: Recurring Sandbox allowance
facts.value: Up to $20/month Northflank Cloud resources, two services, two jobs, one database/addon and two projects; always on, without sleeping.

facts.label: Sandbox feature limits
facts.value: No horizontal scaling or autoscaling/HA; restricted vertical resources; unlimited users and secret groups. BYOC trial allowance is one cluster up to 12 vCPU/48 GB, with the cloud infrastructure still payable.

facts.label: Free tier production and excess behavior
facts.value: Billing guide says Sandbox should not be used for production. Exact over-allowance handling, inactivity deletion and long-term database retention were not found in the checked pricing/billing/threshold/terms pages.

facts.label: Public traffic charges
facts.value: Cloud ingress is free; network egress is $0.06/GB. No per-request HTTP tariff appears in the current container pricing schedule.

facts.label: Internal and inter-zone traffic
facts.value: Private project networking and private database connections are supported; the pricing module identifies $0.02/GB between zones/AZs when using zonal redundancy.

facts.label: Same-project database billing
facts.value: A precise exemption/rate for C's 10 GB app-to-database traffic was not established by the pricing, network, PostgreSQL and billing pages.

facts.label: CDN rate conflict
facts.value: CDN guide says no extra cost, while the public pricing component's CDN row says additional rates apply.

facts.label: Build methods and charged resources
facts.value: Git/Dockerfile or buildpack builds use a selected eligible build plan; build results occupy the project's registry. Resource billing separates build time, runtime and storage.

facts.label: Build image storage rate
facts.value: Stored build images are charged $0.08/GB-month in the pricing module's Other services section.

facts.label: Build duration and concurrency limits
facts.value: A universal maximum build duration, parallel-build quota and recurring free build-minute bucket were not found in the build, plan/quota, API schema, billing and terms pages checked.

facts.label: Other resource charges
facts.value: Persistent disk $0.11657/GiB-month; first 3,000 IOPS/140 MiB/s per disk included; extra IOPS $7.37/1,000 IOPS-month and throughput $5.85/100 MiB/s-month.

facts.label: Stored backups and observability
facts.value: Addon backup storage $0.08/GB-month; logs/metrics $0.20/GB after the first 10 GB/month. Basic DDoS protection is included.

facts.label: Optional dedicated egress and other deployments
facts.value: Dedicated egress gateway $15/gateway-month; previews, extra service/database replicas and extra build resources have their own usage charges.

facts.label: Spend visibility and alerts
facts.value: Current costs can be grouped by account, project or resource; usage updates hourly. Billing alerts notify registered/invoice emails and configured notification integrations at chosen thresholds.

facts.label: Automatic invoices and suspension
facts.value: New accounts default to $50 automatic invoice/charge threshold, with $100/$250/$500 options subject to prior-credit rules. CPU services suspend if threshold invoices cannot be paid.

facts.label: Bounded scale and residual costs
facts.value: Set maximum replicas and manually scale services to zero; CI can still build while a service has zero instances. Retained disk, images and backups have separate meters.

facts.label: Idle and manual zero-instance behavior
facts.value: Sandbox is advertised always on without sleeping. Paid continuously running allocations stay billable while allocated; manual zero instances makes a service unavailable while enabled CI may still build.

facts.label: Autoscaling configuration
facts.value: Paid deployment/combined services support CPU, memory, requests-per-second and custom Prometheus metrics with configured minimum/maximum instances.

facts.label: Autoscale reaction and downscale
facts.value: Checks occur every 15 seconds; mixed metrics choose the largest required count. Downscale uses a moving five-minute stabilization window; upscaling waits for the new containers to become running before adding more.

facts.label: Persistent-storage scaling constraint
facts.value: Single Read/Write volume limits a service to one pod and forces replacement before startup; Multi Read/Write allows shared mounting across pods/services/jobs with application-level coordination.

facts.label: Published account and resource defaults
facts.value: Selected defaults: 100 projects, 500 services and 100 jobs per account/team; ten instances/service, three replicas/addon and ten concurrent runs/job. Free jobs allow one active run.

facts.label: Payload and execution ceilings
facts.value: No universal HTTP request-body/concurrency or continuous-process execution cap was found in the quota, network, path-timeout, service schema, pricing and terms pages.

facts.label: Signup card requirement
facts.value: Pricing says Sandbox needs no card, while the billing guide says all users must add a payment method before creating any resources, including free plans.

facts.label: Payments and buyer age
facts.value: Pricing accepts Visa, Mastercard and American Express through Stripe. Terms state minimum age 16, while user representations also require the customer not to be a minor in their jurisdiction.

facts.label: Temporary trial and countries
facts.value: No separate universal signup cash-credit amount/expiry or exhaustive accepted-country/identity-document matrix found beyond the recurring Sandbox offer and paid-credit mechanism.

facts.label: Commercial use and policy qualification
facts.value: Paid production/business hosting is marketed and documented, but the terms restrict commercial endeavors to provider-endorsed/approved purposes and contain broad personal-use language for provider content/services.

facts.label: Acceptable-use restrictions
facts.value: General terms prohibit illegal/infringing content, security bypasses, malicious software, service disruption, unauthorized automation/data collection, spam, privacy violations and specified harmful/objectionable content.

facts.label: Managed cloud model
facts.value: Northflank Cloud builds and runs container services/jobs and managed data addons on provider-operated infrastructure, with UI, API and CLI management.

facts.label: Own-cloud and Kubernetes models
facts.value: BYOC provisions/manages Kubernetes in the customer's cloud account. BYOK imports an existing customer-operated Kubernetes cluster. Enterprise can arrange a forward-deployed/private control plane.

facts.label: Suitable applications
facts.value: Arbitrary compatible container websites, APIs/microservices, continuously running background services, one-off/cron jobs, databases, queues and GPU/agent workloads.

facts.label: Directory overlap
facts.value: Managed databases, Redis caching, RabbitMQ messaging and MinIO object storage; own-cloud orchestration and AI/agent sandboxes overlap other directory groups.

facts.label: Managed-cloud origins
facts.value: Current region guide lists 17 project regions: Africa South; Asia East, Northeast, South Delhi, Southeast; Australia Southeast; Canada Central; Europe West, Frankfurt, Netherlands, Zurich; Southamerica East; US Central, East Ohio, East1, West, West California.

facts.label: Region codes and build location
facts.value: Codes include africa-south, asia-east, asia-northeast, asia-south-delhi, asia-southeast, australia-southeast, canada-central, europe-west, europe-west-frankfurt, europe-west-netherlands, europe-west-zurich, southamerica-east, us-central, us-east-ohio, us-east1, us-west, us-west-california.

facts.label: CDN and own-cloud regions
facts.value: Optional Fastly CDN caches static content from a deployment; BYOC can use the connected provider's supported locations. GPU availability has a separate model/count/region matrix.

facts.label: Runtime and language routes
facts.value: Dockerfile or compatible external OCI/Docker image; selectable Cloud Native Buildpack stacks include modern Heroku Ubuntu 24.04/22.04, Paketo Jammy and Google Ubuntu 22 builders.

facts.label: Architecture scope
facts.value: Service API accepts infrastructure.architecture values x86 and arm; supported compute selection remains constrained by cluster, region and account quotas.

facts.label: Deprecated stacks and version care
facts.value: The buildpack guide distinguishes current Ubuntu 22/24 stacks from deprecated classic/older Ubuntu 18 stacks, and warns sample builders are not recommended for production.

facts.label: Framework deployment
facts.value: Official Next.js guide uses a Node app in a combined service or separate build/deploy services with Dockerfile/buildpacks and code.run/custom-domain access.

facts.label: Framework-specific advanced behavior
facts.value: No complete current Next.js version/adapter matrix for React streaming, edge middleware or coordinated multi-replica ISR/cache refresh was found in the guide, buildpack, networking, CDN, pricing or terms pages.

facts.label: Git and private-source workflow
facts.value: GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket integrations, authorized private repository access, selected branches/commits and monorepo build context/path filters; combined service provides simple source-to-runtime CI/CD.

facts.label: Other VCS edition scope
facts.value: Docs also describe Azure DevOps, Cursor Origin and self-hosted GitLab/GitHub Enterprise/Gitea/Forgejo integration; pricing gates some advanced integrations by plan.

facts.label: Images and automation
facts.value: Deploy public/private external registry images or images built/imported into the project; manage via dashboard, REST API, CLI, clients, JSON templates and GitOps.

facts.label: Continuous background work
facts.value: A continuously running container service can execute a worker or queue consumer without exposing a public HTTP port.

facts.label: One-off and cron jobs
facts.value: Jobs build from Git or run a registry/project image, exit on completion, or follow a five-field cron schedule. Concurrency choices are Allow, Forbid or Replace; retries and a seconds-based time limit are configurable.

facts.label: Public protocols
facts.value: Ordinary public/VPC service ingress supports HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, including WebSockets and gRPC; public HTTP ports are 80/443 with HTTP redirected to HTTPS.

facts.label: Internal TCP/UDP and public L4
facts.value: Internal ports support TCP/UDP. Public TCP/UDP services require a separate Layer 4 load balancer rather than ordinary public service-port settings.

facts.label: Private networks and access
facts.value: Projects are isolated by default; same-team/same-cluster multi-project ingress can be allowed one way. CLI forwarding and Tailscale support private access; eligible BYOC clusters support private VPC ingress.

facts.label: Fixed outbound address
facts.value: Managed-cloud egress gateway provides dedicated static outbound IP rules for selected projects/services/jobs; default outbound IPs are shared/unpredictable and addons are excluded.

facts.label: Timeout and streaming limits
facts.value: Per-domain-path HTTP timeout is configurable in seconds or milliseconds and returns 408 if the origin misses it. A universal WebSocket idle lifetime, body-size ceiling or SSE/response buffering guarantee was not established.

facts.label: Temporary files
facts.value: Runtime ephemeral storage is erased on restart/termination and cannot be shared across containers. Oversized writes can evict/restart a deployment.

facts.label: Persistent volumes
facts.value: Volumes persist data across restarts, support mount subdirectories and multiple mounts, and can move between services. Storage can expand but cannot shrink; delete after detaching.

facts.label: Volume backup schedule conflict
facts.value: Volume guide says snapshots must be manual and scheduled backups are unsupported; the 24 September 2026 changelog says scheduled platform-volume backups are available with failure alerts.

facts.label: Managed database addons
facts.value: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, MinIO and RabbitMQ are available as provider-managed addons with version selection, resources, private networking and supported backup/TLS features.

facts.label: PostgreSQL configuration
facts.value: Supported major versions listed are 18, 17, 16, 15, 14, 13 and 12; TLS can be enabled, public exposure requires TLS, and private connection secrets can be linked into workloads.

facts.label: Example-sized PostgreSQL allocation
facts.value: Use one nf-compute-50 allocation, 0.5 vCPU/1024 MiB, plus 10 GiB provisioned disk. Widget compute display $12/month; rate $0.11657/GiB-month for disk.

facts.label: High availability and supporting-service editions
facts.value: Paid plans support addon replicas/HA; Enterprise adds zonal redundancy and global/custom-destination recovery features. PostgreSQL uses Patroni for high availability.

facts.label: Domains and managed HTTPS
facts.value: Included generated code.run public endpoint; custom root/subdomains attach to service ports. Let's Encrypt certificates are generated automatically and renewed before expiry; user-supplied certificates are also supported.

facts.label: Wildcard scope and certificate limits
facts.value: Wildcard routing/certificates are supported; wildcard routing binds the parent to one region/cluster and public/VPC target, with no apex service under that routing choice.

facts.label: Private ingress domain validation
facts.value: Public ingress uses HTTP-01 by default; VPC-routed subdomains use DNS delegation validation or supported imported/wildcard certificates and cannot use Northflank CDN.

facts.label: CI/CD and release controls
facts.value: Automatic branch/commit builds and deployment, manual image/build selection, environment workflows, migrations and optional canary/gradual-release features.

facts.label: Health and graceful shutdown
facts.value: Configurable startup/readiness/liveness probes support HTTP, TCP or commands. Readiness gates traffic; liveness can restart unhealthy containers. Default termination grace is 30 seconds and is configurable.

facts.label: Previews and their costs
facts.value: Preview blueprints create isolated services/databases/volumes/URLs on Git PR/push, API, webhook or schedule; configurable expiry and Git close/delete events can clean them up.

facts.label: Return to an earlier version
facts.value: Retained built images can be selected/deployed again; pricing includes rollback/specific-build selection, and source can switch between project and external registry images.

facts.label: Log access and retention conflict
facts.value: Live/historical build, deployment, addon and job logs with UI filtering/API/CLI tailing; docs/pricing feature matrix state 30-day retention, but pricing's collapsed module labels 180 days.

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Build/runtime/database/job metrics include CPU, memory, network/HTTP and other resource data, collected on a 15-second scale, with API/CLI access.

facts.label: External observability
facts.value: Paid log sinks forward to supported vendors, S3 or a custom HTTP endpoint; project/account selection and text/JSON encoding are documented.

facts.label: MFA and account login
facts.value: Login via password or Google/GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket OAuth; optional authenticator-app one-time passwords also apply to SSO login, with recovery codes. Teams can enforce MFA.

facts.label: Roles, API and secrets
facts.value: Paid fine-grained roles can restrict resource CRUD permissions by project/team; API tokens inherit RBAC roles. Build arguments, runtime variables, secret groups and secret files supply app credentials.

facts.label: Incident credential scope
facts.value: Northflank's Nov 6 update says all users should rotate integration and project secrets and review provider logs; some customers reported unauthorized use of AI keys. It says there is no evidence workloads or workload data were accessed, while forensic review continues.

facts.label: Security page freshness conflict
facts.value: Northflank's security page still says the company has not had a breach since formation, while its active incident notice reports decrypted customer secrets and unauthorized use of some supplied AI keys.

facts.label: Audit availability during incident
facts.value: Incident update of 31 October, 01:04 UTC says audit logs were enabled for all customers including free users; pricing still places standard audit entitlement in Enterprise.

facts.label: Container access
facts.value: Service SSH identities can be restricted by project/tag, allow SSH and standard scp/sftp/rsync tools, and must be enabled per service; interactive container shell is also documented.

facts.label: BYOC hardware floor
facts.value: Minimum one node with at least 4 vCPU/8 GB each, at least 8 vCPU/16 GB per cluster; therefore a single-node cluster needs 8 vCPU/16 GB. Recommended three nodes and at least 12 vCPU/24 GB.

facts.label: BYOK requirements and duties
facts.value: Supported Kubernetes versions listed are 1.34/1.35; Cilium, compatible CSI and CoreDNS required. Initial import requires cluster-admin credentials; Northflank then creates a management service account.

facts.label: Provider responsibility and controller outages
facts.value: BYOC provider manages cluster lifecycle; BYOK customer operates the cluster. A general guarantee for app behavior during loss of the hosted Northflank control plane was not established.

facts.label: Data-location boundaries
facts.value: Security page places the hosted control plane in Google Cloud London or Amsterdam. In BYOC, workload runtime/data can be in the customer's account, while logs, builds/images and dumps can still be Northflank-hosted.

facts.label: Private control-plane edition
facts.value: Enterprise can arrange a forward-deployed control plane intended to keep platform data in the customer's network, including air-gapped deployments.

facts.label: Public DPA and subprocessor text
facts.value: A complete accessible DPA and named subprocessor schedule were not retrieved. The linked trust center exposed only a page shell; a guessed legal/dpa route returned 404.

facts.label: Personal-information privacy
facts.value: Policy identifies account/contact/payment/usage collection, Stripe payment handling and disclosures to service providers. Retention is necessity-based with a stated six-month-after-termination purpose limit, subject to legal/backup exceptions.

facts.label: Database backup scope and scheduling
facts.value: Database/addon snapshots are incremental disk backups; native dumps are compressed full exports for supported engines. Up to three schedules/addon: hourly, daily and weekly, with retention specified in days.

facts.label: Restore and export distinctions
facts.value: Native dumps can be downloaded as gzip/Zstandard and imported/restored; disk snapshots cannot be downloaded. Restore can overwrite existing user databases; forks create independent addons from a backup.

facts.label: Backup fees and global destinations
facts.value: Addon backup storage is $0.08/GB-month. Enterprise global backups allow cross-project recovery and custom S3-compatible destinations; storage credentials and destination cloud bills remain separate.

facts.label: File-volume recovery
facts.value: Volume snapshot/clone workflow restores to a new volume at least as large as its source; snapshots may miss in-flight writes. Newer release note says backups can outlive source-volume deletion.

facts.label: Data and backup responsibility
facts.value: General terms make the customer responsible for transmitted/user data and disclaim liability for its loss or corruption; ordinary backup features do not establish full-app recovery.

facts.label: Code, images and configuration exit
facts.value: Source stays in the chosen Git repository; Dockerfiles/OCI images remain usable elsewhere. Template JSON is viewable/editable and retained built images have pull instructions.

facts.label: Database and file export
facts.value: Download a native PostgreSQL dump rather than a non-downloadable snapshot; CLI/client or container curl/wget/SSH file tools can move data off persistent volumes.

facts.label: Account/team deletion
facts.value: Deletion is irreversible: team/user cleanup can remove owned projects, databases, backups, domains and configuration. Pending usage is invoiced; stop running resources and export first.

facts.label: BYOK exit and cleanup risks
facts.value: Deleting an imported cluster removes its ingress load balancers but leaves the underlying cluster and many installed components. Default volume cleanup can delete PVCs and linked workloads even if not managed by Northflank.

facts.label: Identity and ownership
facts.value: Northflank; contracting provider Northflank Ltd, company number 11918540, based in London, United Kingdom.

facts.label: Current operating and signup status
facts.value: Active public offer with Free Sandbox, Pay as you go and Enterprise signup/contact paths, but an unresolved security incident is displayed prominently.

facts.label: Security incident — current status
facts.value: Official incident remains Monitoring / Major outage. Latest visible update is November 6, 2026, 10:09 UTC. Northflank says first known secret decryption occurred October 30 at 02:39–03:08 UTC; the exploit was patched within 60 minutes of its first alert, customers were notified within two hours, and independent forensic review continues.

facts.label: Incident scope and action notice
facts.value: Northflank says running workloads remained online and it has no evidence workloads or workload data were accessed; reported unauthorized use of some user-supplied AI keys occurred. Users were told to rotate all secrets, review provider logs and reconnect integrations revoked during response.

facts.label: Status page and unresolved incident
facts.value: Official status page has component state and incident history; at this check the security incident remains open with platform components marked Major outage while app/API entries are Operational.

facts.label: Advertised SLA by edition
facts.value: Enterprise pricing advertises 99.99% uptime, custom support and guaranteed response. Sandbox/Pay-as-you-go columns do not advertise the same contractual SLA.

facts.label: Full SLA remedy and exclusions
facts.value: Public credit brackets, eligible-service scope, claim deadline, outage measurement and maintenance exclusions were not established from pricing, Enterprise, legal and trust-center pages.

facts.label: Support by plan
facts.value: Pricing: Sandbox best effort, Pay as you go proactive, Enterprise custom with dedicated Slack and guaranteed response. Docs/incident provide support@northflank.com.

facts.label: Published response details
facts.value: No exact public response-time number/hours/timezone for ordinary paid or free support found; Enterprise guaranteed response is described without a public threshold or fixed support price.

facts.label: Software license
facts.value: Hosted platform access is proprietary under Northflank terms; no public self-hosted open-source platform license is established for BYOC/BYOK/private control-plane deployment.

facts.value: Oracle manages physical facilities, hardware, and the cloud control plane; the customer manages the guest OS, application, runtime, firewall rules, and app recovery.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap

facts.value: OCI offers selectable commercial compute regions worldwide; some shapes, including A1, can have limited host capacity in a region.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Plesk includes no server CPU, RAM or disk. Minimum panel requirements are 1 GB RAM plus 1 GB swap and 20 GB disk on Linux; Windows requires 2 GB RAM and 32 GB disk.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: A minimum CPU core or clock speed is not specified in the current Plesk system-requirements page checked.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Direct core licenses are sold as per-server monthly or yearly leases, not as Plesk CPU-hours, memory-hours, requests or data transfer.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: No ongoing free direct retail plan. Plesk says it does not offer free plans; a trial is separate.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Plesk does not provide the server's internet transfer allowance, egress rate, private networking or CDN. These are charged or included by the chosen infrastructure provider.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Plesk's own panel licensing does not meter app-to-database or visitor traffic; Plesk cannot give a product-wide rate per GB.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Plesk does not provide a managed build-minute service. Git-based file deployment runs on the customer's server and any build tools and CPU time use that server.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Git can deploy on push or manually; no per-build fee, hosted build quota or concurrent-build allowance is published for Plesk.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Server rent, public IP, bandwidth, domain registration, DNS provider, external mail delivery and remote backup storage are not part of the direct Plesk license.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Some Plesk extensions, add-on security/email products and paid third-party tools require separate licenses; the extension catalog labels paid items.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Plesk does not host the server account and has no Plesk-wide VM spend cap, usage alarm, or automatic stop for a cloud-provider bill.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Canceling a Plesk lease stops future license renewal, but server, disk, IP, storage and provider-side backups can continue billing.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Plesk does not sleep or scale hosted apps to zero; it manages services on an always-provisioned server. Provider billing may continue while an app or panel is idle.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Linux Cgroups Manager can set resource controls for customer accounts on supported setups; this does not autoscale server capacity.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: A general per-request duration, app count, request-size ceiling or total concurrency limit for a self-managed Plesk server was not published in the checked docs.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Node.js/PHP versions, sites and databases consume resources from the same server unless the operator places them elsewhere; no equal-performance capacity claim can be made from the license tier.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: WebPros terms reserve the right to verify identity for higher-risk, sanctions, export-control, fraud-prevention or partner/reseller onboarding cases.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: No separate Plesk application-content AUP covering ads, affiliate sites or online-store categories was found in the checked pricing and license terms. Server-provider abuse rules remain separate.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Self-hosted control-panel software installed on a customer's or hosting provider's server. Plesk supplies the panel and license; the server provider or operator supplies and maintains the machine and its network.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Direct store licenses are per server. Plesk also appears as a preinstalled or hourly license option in selected hyperscaler images; in those cases the cloud provider supplies the server.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: The customer or hoster chooses the OS, operates the server, applies panel and OS updates, configures sites and mail, and arranges infrastructure backups.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Suitable for websites, CMSs, static files, PHP sites and supported app runtimes on a server. The operator can manage sites, databases, DNS, email accounts and server settings.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Node.js applications can run as server processes and Plesk can deploy website files with Git; the customer still supplies and operates the server.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Plesk does not run apps on its own shared compute regions or delivery network. The server location and any CDN depend on the selected VPS/dedicated/cloud provider.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Plesk provides marketplace images through hyperscaler partners, but this research does not establish a complete cross-provider region list or availability by image.

facts.value: Monthly billing with one-month minimum, cancel any time; paid plans advertise a no-quibble 30-day money-back guarantee.

facts.label: Free network and paid-only features

facts.label: Inactivity deletion

facts.label: Numeric network limits and tariffs
facts.value: No numeric monthly GB allowance, current per-GB excess schedule, incoming-byte fee or app-to-native-Postgres transfer price was established.

facts.value: No separate managed build-minute package; the builder runs dependency installation/build commands in account consoles/tasks or builds elsewhere, then uploads/pulls files and reloads.

facts.label: Build-specific ceilings
facts.value: No distinct hosted-builder concurrency, maximum build duration or deploy-count allowance was established.

facts.label: Optional off-platform services
facts.value: Domain registration external; Redis/MongoDB or other external DBs can be paid dependencies; fixed outbound IP can need an external proxy service; backup export storage is customer-selected.

facts.label: Current bill controls
facts.value: Fixed subscribed plan and daily CPU tarpit; storage quota rejects further writes when full. No automatic CPU overage purchase is described.

facts.label: Hard monetary cap and residual fee

facts.label: Worker scaling
facts.value: Add workers/apps by changing Custom plan settings; standard workers queue requests when all are busy.

facts.label: Request execution limit
facts.value: Standard web workers have a five-minute request timeout and are restarted if they do not respond in that time.

facts.label: HTTP upload body limit
facts.value: 100 MiB upload limit applies globally, independent of plan; large files need chunking/reassembly or a separate storage path.

facts.label: Concurrency and queue behavior
facts.value: Standard WSGI: Beginner one worker, Developer three; incoming requests queue when workers are busy and can fail with 502-backend if queue fills.

facts.label: Acceptable-use restrictions
facts.value: PythonAnywhere TOS incorporates the AWS AUP: illegal/fraudulent activity, rights violations, serious harm, child exploitation, security/availability violations and spam prohibited.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Managed shared Python hosting with browser IDE/consoles, persistent account storage, WSGI web workers and provider-managed web serving.

facts.label: Shared responsibility
facts.value: Customer responsible for development, application maintenance, security and appropriate backups; provider security page describes patched operating systems and security scans.

facts.label: Native app types
facts.value: Python websites/APIs using Django, Flask and other WSGI frameworks; scripts, notebooks and paid always-on jobs. Static-only HTML/JS sites also supported.

facts.label: Non-Python and async scope
facts.value: Node can be installed for command-line tooling; experimental website system can run a server that listens on the supplied Unix-domain socket.

facts.label: App hosting regions
facts.value: US system on AWS us-east-1, Northern Virginia; EU system on AWS eu-central-1, Frankfurt.

facts.value: EU/US systems are separate; official EU launch post directs existing-user migration requests to support. Cloudflare can be configured as an external delivery/cache layer on paid custom domains.

facts.label: Legacy Python system image

facts.label: System upgrades and packages
facts.value: Users can change their system image and install packages with pip/virtualenv. Files/data remain, but runtime/package changes can require rebuilding virtualenvs.

facts.label: Docker and OS control
facts.value: Customer Docker containers are not supported according to official staff; no root access or apt package installation.

facts.label: Django behavior
facts.value: Django supported through virtualenv, dependency installation, settings, WSGI config, migrations, static collection/mapping and reload.

facts.label: Flask behavior
facts.value: Standard Flask uses the provider’s WSGI server; import the Flask app as application and do not call app.run() during hosted import.

facts.label: FastAPI and async Django
facts.value: Experimental system documents Uvicorn with FastAPI, FastHTML and async Django, via pa CLI/API and a Unix-domain socket.

facts.label: SocketIO and Streamlit
facts.value: Dedicated experimental guides provide Gunicorn/eventlet Flask-SocketIO and Streamlit launch procedures.

facts.label: Code inputs and CLI/API
facts.value: Browser file upload/editor, Git/hg/svn checkout, paid SFTP/SSH, and API automation. pa CLI manages experimental websites.

facts.label: Private repositories
facts.value: Private Git repositories supported via customer credentials/SSH keys; free accounts face outbound protocol/allowlist restrictions.

facts.label: Always-on background processes
facts.value: Paid always-on tasks restart on crashes/hardware failure; Developer includes one, Custom chooses a count. Consoles are not the reliable permanent-process mechanism.

facts.label: Paid scheduled jobs
facts.value: Up to 20 hourly/daily tasks, each up to 12 hours; 20 is a soft limit support can raise reasonably.

facts.label: Legacy free scheduled jobs
facts.value: One daily task, maximum two hours, only for free accounts predating January 2026 regional cutoffs.

facts.label: HTTP and streaming
facts.value: Standard HTTP/HTTPS WSGI hosting; streaming can disable nginx buffering with X-Accel-Buffering: no and appropriate application flushing.

facts.label: Live connections by mode
facts.value: Experimental async/SocketIO deployment can support its documented live-server patterns; standard WSGI is not interchangeable with that mode.

facts.label: Outbound network and static IP
facts.value: Free accounts use HTTP(S) allowlist; paid accounts have unrestricted Internet access. Outbound IP is not fixed and can vary with the server running code.

facts.label: Private database access
facts.value: Hosted Postgres can be accessed externally through an SSH tunnel; external database connections are permitted on paid plans.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Account file storage is writable persistent storage for code, uploaded files and installed packages; image changes preserve files/data.

facts.label: Quota effects and native database storage
facts.value: Full file quota causes write errors; native MySQL is subject to account storage quota, while Postgres has a separately chosen disk allocation.

facts.label: Database catalogue
facts.value: SQLite for everyone; MySQL for paid and grandfathered free accounts; provider-hosted Postgres paid add-on. External Redis/MongoDB/MS SQL can be connected from paid accounts.

facts.label: Current Postgres engine and operations
facts.value: PostgreSQL 15 available and default for new databases; older versions can be upgraded through support. Databases page has a restart button.

facts.label: Authentication and queues
facts.value: App authentication is implemented in the chosen framework or an external service; documented background-queue recipe can use database/files plus an always-on worker.

facts.label: Custom domains and hosted subdomains
facts.value: Paid plans support custom domains for each configured web app; free gets username.pythonanywhere.com or username.eu.pythonanywhere.com.

facts.label: HTTPS provision and renewal
facts.value: Hosted PythonAnywhere subdomains have provider TLS. Custom-domain Let's Encrypt setup is free and auto-renewing after DNS points correctly; custom certificates also supported.

facts.label: Apex and wildcard scope
facts.value: Apex domains need the documented redirect/ALIAS/CNAME-flattening approach; ordinary CNAME advice applies to subdomains. No general automatic wildcard-domain/certificate promise established.

facts.label: Reload and release behavior
facts.value: Code changes normally require reload. Reload finishes active requests, stops workers, drops queued requests and redirects new requests to themselves until workers restart.

facts.label: Preview and rollback workflow
facts.value: Use additional configured apps/subdomains or local environments for staging; source can be reverted with Git and reloaded. No automatic PR-preview or deployment-snapshot product established.

facts.label: Logs and access
facts.value: Web app access/error/server logs available; API exposes logs/files, and standard access logs include response-time fields. Always-on task logs can be viewed/tail-followed.

facts.label: Log-retention conflict
facts.value: Staff answer 7 July 2021: daily rotation above 100 KiB, retaining through .10.gz; another answer 21 July 2021: daily above 100k, rotated logs kept one week.

facts.label: Basic metrics and monitoring
facts.value: Dashboard exposes task CPU/disk usage; access-log response times aid capacity checks. Worker-busy historical metrics are available by asking support in the capacity guide.

facts.label: Two-factor authentication
facts.value: Optional authenticator-based TFA with emergency codes; support says it cannot override loss of both device and emergency codes.

facts.value: Railpack detects Node, Python, Go, PHP, HTML/static, Java, Ruby, Deno, Rust, Elixir, shell.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Custom Dockerfile supported; auto-detected at source root or custom path configured.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Next.js deployment guide uses standalone output and Node server; covers GitHub/CLI/Dockerfile and Postgres. Exact framework version and ISR/cache-sharing/streaming guarantees not specified.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: GitHub repository, local directory via CLI, public Docker image; linked branches auto-deploy.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Private Docker registry credentials require Pro; Docker authentication registries supported.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Long-running persistent services can run workers.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Managed cron starts services; UTC runs at least five minutes apart; unfinished preceding job causes next run to be skipped. Railway does not automatically terminate jobs.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: HTTPS HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, WebSockets over HTTP/1.1; TCP proxy available. WebSockets exempt from HTTP duration/inactivity limits.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Encrypted WireGuard private networking within each project/environment.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Static outbound IPv4 on Pro; not for inbound traffic.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: SMTP only Pro and above; Free/Trial/Hobby need HTTPS email APIs. Outbound IPv6 opt-in, off by default.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Persist writes on attached volume; build/pre-deploy writes do not reach volume. CLI can browse, upload and download volume files.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: One volume/service; volumes cannot use replicas; volume deployments incur brief downtime. Free 0.5 GB, Hobby 5 GB; Pro defaults 50 GB, expandable to 1 TB. Bills used bytes including about 2% to 3% filesystem metadata.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Railway maintains PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis and MongoDB deployment templates/images; users enable backups, HA and pooling. Schema, queries, data, disk sizing and major upgrades stay user responsibilities.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: PostgreSQL template deploys one node from Railway's SSL-enabled image based on official Postgres; external TCP access costs egress.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Object storage $0.015/GB-month with free egress.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Railway-provided and custom domains; automatic free SSL certificates.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Wildcards supported; custom domains require CNAME and verification TXT. Let's Encrypt certificates valid 90 days, renewal with 30 days remaining.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Persistent staging and temporary PR environments; PR environment deleted on merge/close.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Configured endpoint must return 2xx before traffic switches; default timeout 300 seconds. Not an ongoing health monitor. Volumes prevent zero-downtime deploys.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Rollback restores earlier image and custom variables within retention; redeploy and restart supported.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Build/runtime stdout/stderr logs in dashboard and CLI. Retention Free 3 days, Trial/Hobby 7, Pro 30, Enterprise up to 90. Limit 500 lines/second/replica; excess dropped.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: CPU, RAM, disk and network graphs, up to 30 days. App latency/error/business metrics require external telemetry.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Authenticator TOTP and passkeys; team admins can enforce MFA.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Service and shared environment variables carry configuration/secrets into builds/runtime and CLI.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Not applicable to ordinary hosted app plans. User maintains app code/configuration, Railway operates deployment platform. Enterprise BYOC is a separately advertised mode, requirements unknown.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: DPA exists; no complete country-only commitment established for app data, builds, logs and backups. Exhibit C mentions backups across sites/regions.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Opt-in volume backups: daily every 24 hours retained 6 days; weekly every 7 days retained 27; monthly every 30 retained 89. Incremental exclusive bytes at volume rate.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Volume file export through CLI download.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Standard Postgres external connection available through TCP proxy. Complete outward DB/settings migration and backup-file export procedure not established.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Railway; contracting company Railway Corporation. Ultimate parent and former names unknown.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Active public offer. New signups reopened November 2, 2026; the recovery notice required new customers to subscribe to Hobby or Pro before deploying, while free-trial deployments remained temporarily unavailable.

facts.label: Security incident — customer credentials
facts.value: On October 21, 2026, Railway disclosed unauthorized access to internal systems and exposure of encrypted environment variables for a subset of customers; some stored secrets, including credentials, were decrypted. Its October 22 preliminary report estimated at most 1.85% of workspaces (about 100,000) had variables potentially compromised.

facts.label: Security incident recovery
facts.value: Railway said the security incident was resolved for existing users on October 26; its recovery incident was marked resolved on November 2 when new signups reopened. The October 22 preliminary report said external forensics remained ongoing.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Public incident/component status page.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Pricing calls Hobby 99.9%, Pro 99.99%, Enterprise 99.999% availability targets. Public Enterprise agreement instead states 99.5% monthly availability with credits.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Enterprise agreement credits: 10% for 98.5% to below 99.5%; 25% for 95% to below 98.5%; 100% below 95%. Notify within 72 hours; exclusions include maintenance, third parties, causes outside control and DoS.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Free/Trial/Hobby community via Central Station, no guaranteed response. Pro Railway support usually within 72 hours, excludes support SLOs/app debugging. Enterprise/Business Class negotiated support. No general email support.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: Hosted proprietary platform; installable platform license not applicable. Hosted use governed by terms and acceptable-use policy.

apps.name: RamNode Cloud VPS

cells.selfhost: Yes; root access, manage the guest OS

work.math: $2 a month VM cap + $2 for an IPv4 address. 100 GB of data sent out fits the 500 GB allowance. Building and deploying are self-managed, and tax is not included.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no new sale, shutdown, rebrand, or qualifying incident found for RamNode Cloud VPS.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Lite 1 GB: USD $2/month cap or listed $0.003/hour for an IPv6-only instance; public product page says IPv4 can be added for $2/month, making the listed IPv4-enabled total $4/month. Offered in EWR, LAX, and NLX.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Lite 2 GB: USD $3/month cap or listed $0.004/hour IPv6-only; add $2/month for IPv4, for a listed IPv4-enabled total of $5/month.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Standard VPS is listed from USD $4/month ($0.006/hour) for 512 MB RAM, 1 core, 20 GB SSD and 1 TB bandwidth; its 1 GB / 1-core / 40 GB / 2 TB tier is $5/month ($0.007/hour). Higher Standard sizes are $10, $15, $20, $30, $40, and $80/month.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Premium VPS price ladder is USD $14, $24, $36, $48, $96, and $192/month by listed size.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Storage VPS price ladder is USD $4, $6, $12, $17, $22, $43, and $64/month by listed size.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: VDS price ladder is USD $50, $90, $170, and $320/month by listed size.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: The cloud usage guides describe hourly billing capped at the listed monthly rate, no long-term commitment, and stopping compute charges when an instance is deleted. The public rates are not introductory-versus-renewal promotions.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: The linked Universal Terms describe automatic renewal for a term set by the order and a minimum $50 early-cancellation charge, while the Cloud VPS product and billing pages describe hourly usage, no long-term commitment, and deletion to stop compute billing.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Initial cloud funding minimum is not settled: one official cloud overview says add at least $3, while the billing FAQ says the minimum initial PAYG credit is $10.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Public VM rates are shown in USD. The terms allow prices in other currencies at checkout and say local VAT/GST or taxes may be added based on billing details; a country-specific final price or exact tax amount is not published in the public rate table.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Lite: 1 GB RAM, 1 virtual core, 15 GB NVMe and 500 GB bandwidth at $2/month IPv6-only; 2 GB RAM, 1 virtual core, 20 GB NVMe and 500 GB at $3/month IPv6-only. Add $2/month for IPv4.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Standard sizes (public USD per month): 512 MB/1 core/20 GB/1 TB $4; 1 GB/1 core/40 GB/2 TB $5; 2 GB/2 cores/80 GB/4 TB $10; 3 GB/2 cores/100 GB/6 TB $15; 4 GB/4 cores/120 GB/8 TB $20; 6 GB/4 cores/160 GB/10 TB $30; 8 GB/4 cores/180 GB/12 TB $40; 16 GB/8 cores/260 GB/14 TB $80.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Premium VPS is listed at 2–32 GB RAM, 2–16 virtual cores, 80–600 GB NVMe and 6–18 TB bandwidth, for $14–$192/month. Storage VPS is listed at 512 MB–12 GB RAM, 1–4 cores, 160–4,000 GB HDD and 2–150 TB bandwidth, for $4–$64/month.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: VDS is listed with 8–64 GB RAM, 2–16 dedicated cores, 200–1,600 GB NVMe and 10–60 TB bandwidth at $50–$320/month.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: The hardware guide lists AMD EPYC and Intel Xeon processors, ECC memory, NVMe on Premium, enterprise SSD on Standard, and HDD on Storage VPS. It does not map a processor model or architecture guarantee to each flavor and region.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: The getting-started guide calls CPU, RAM, and storage dedicated/guaranteed, but the AUP says VPS CPU cores and disk I/O are shared and may be reduced if a VM disrupts neighbors.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: VM compute is metered hourly while the instance exists, with a monthly cap; no separate CPU-time, memory-time, request, or build-minute meter is listed for a standard VM.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Published hourly rates are rounded display equivalents of monthly caps. Exact sub-hour billing rounding and the precise hourly calculation for every add-on are not fully stated.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: A Cloud account is offered for $0, but the account-only offer is not a free VM allowance. The listed cloud-credit bonus requires a customer deposit. An ongoing free-compute allowance is not published.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Plan tables list 500 GB–150 TB of bandwidth by tier. The Cloud bandwidth guide says outbound IPv4/IPv6 traffic counts, inbound and private-network traffic do not, and private network traffic is free.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Cloud bandwidth guide states excess traffic is billed at $0.004/GB per hour after the monthly allotment, without throttling. The public pricing add-on table labels additional bandwidth as hourly at $0.004/GB/month.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: RamNode Cloud VPS does not document a managed source build pipeline or preview-build product. App builds can run on the customer's VM or external CI.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: The resource-quota page lists “3 concurrent builds,” but does not define whether this means instance provisioning or application source builds; the Cloud VPS and pricing pages do not clarify it.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Lite public IPv4 is listed as +$2/month; standard plans include one IPv4 in the product table. Additional DDoS-filtered IP is listed at $5/month.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: NVMe block storage is $0.085/GB/month, billed hourly; 10 GB is listed at $0.85/month. Object storage is $5/month for 250 GB, billed hourly, and is offered in NLX, LAX, and EWR.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Snapshot/image and volume-backup storage are listed at $0.10/GB/month and billed hourly. A load balancer is $0.012/hour, approximately $8/month; extra bandwidth is separately priced.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: A floating IP is billed hourly, but the public pricing table does not state its hourly amount.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Managed app administration is not included. Optional professional services are listed at $80/hour in half-hour increments.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Billing FAQ says Cloud usage can be monitored in the control panel; auto-pay invoices monthly or at $40, PAYG services suspend at a $0 credit balance, and post-pay is available by request.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Terms say usage can continue while an instance exists even when it is powered off, and service may be suspended/terminated after cloud credit falls below $0. No hard user-set account spend cap or guaranteed zero-negative balance is documented.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: A user-configurable maximum monthly bill, forced shutdown threshold, or alert delay for all billable resources is not published.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: A powered-on instance runs continuously and incurs hourly charges up to the monthly cap; Cloud billing FAQ says shelving stops compute charges while preserving data. The terms separately say a powered-off instance can remain billable while it exists.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Instance resizing and manual horizontal scaling are documented. The autoscaling guide describes customer-configured scripts and load balancers; no managed automatic instance scaler or scale-to-zero service is described for Cloud VPS itself.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: The VM does not impose a hosted-function request duration or concurrency cap; those are set by the customer’s OS, web server, and application. Account defaults list 10 instances per region, 20 vCPUs, and 40 GB RAM, with increases available by support request.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: The quota page also lists 25 snapshots/account, 10 custom images/account, 10 block volumes/region and 1 TB total volume capacity. It lists 1,000 API requests/hour; the page does not say that these are runtime request limits.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Maximum application throughput, request size, or execution time for a particular workload is not published as a RamNode VM guarantee.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The current credit offer adds a bonus to deposits: e.g. deposit $10 and receive $12 credit, deposit $500 and receive $1,000 credit. The page also advertises up to $500 of bonus credit per calendar year for active accounts in good standing. This is a deposit promotion, not a no-payment trial.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: RamNode lists credit card, PayPal, cryptocurrency, and Alipay as payment options. For non-card payments, the terms require a cloud-credit balance; credit-card billing is available as auto-pay.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The terms require users to be at least 18 or legally able to contract and not barred under applicable US or other law. Fraud screening may require extra documents. No public country-by-country availability or sanctions list was found in the terms, support, product, or billing pages checked.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: A universal requirement for a payment card, identity check, or company registration for every new cloud account is not published.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: RamNode's AUP says products are for lawful use and reasonable business use, and it prohibits spam, illegal activity, abuse, malware, and activity that harms network or service performance.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Shared VPS CPU/disk I/O use is subject to intervention for disruptive sustained use; excessive CPU, bandwidth, disk use, spam, proxies on shared hosting, and other policy violations can trigger extra charges, suspension, or termination.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: KVM virtual machines on RamNode's OpenStack cloud. RamNode maintains the physical host, network, and cloud control plane; the customer gets root access and installs, patches, secures, monitors, backs up, and operates the guest OS and apps.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Standard and Lite VPS virtual CPU and disk I/O are shared. VDS is a separate tier whose listed cores are dedicated; it costs more.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: A Linux-compatible website, API, worker, scheduled task, database, or container can run when the customer configures and maintains the software. Custom OS images and full root access support customer-installed software.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Directory scope is VPS/VM hosting. RamNode also sells separate object storage, block storage, load balancers, and managed professional services; those are separate charges and are not bundled database or app-hosting features.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: RamNode's data-center page lists EWR (Piscataway, New Jersey), ATL (Atlanta), LAX (Los Angeles), SEA (Seattle), and NLX (Amsterdam). The same public price table is in USD and does not list per-region VM rates.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Lite is listed for EWR, LAX, and NLX; its product page says Atlanta is coming soon, while the current data-center page lists ATL and SEA as available and the pricing page's older Lite text says SEA is coming soon.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: RamNode supplies Linux cloud images, supports custom ISO/image installation, and permits customer-selected software. Listed images include Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS Stream, Rocky, AlmaLinux, Fedora, and Arch; custom images may be RAW, QCOW2, or VMDK.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Windows is not officially supported on the cloud platform, although the OS guide says a customer can install it from ISO using their own license. The public server-hardware page does not specify a per-flavor guest CPU architecture.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Cloud VPS can run compatible frameworks installed by the customer, but no managed framework runtime or framework-specific SSR, streaming, or cache invalidation guarantee is documented.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Create an instance from a cloud image or ISO; upload supported custom images; administer by SSH, VNC console, Cloud Control Panel, and OpenStack API/CLI.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: No built-in Git repository connection, automatic branch deployment, or managed private-repository integration is documented. Git and CI can be installed/run by the customer or used through an external CI service.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: A customer can run persistent processes and scheduled jobs on the Linux VM using their own process manager and cron/systemd timers. The VM must remain running; no separate managed worker or scheduler is included.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Public network interfaces, private networks, security groups, and IPv4/IPv6 are documented. Security groups can control network ports; VM users manage HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket, streaming, and app-level connection behavior.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Product marketing says all cloud instances include DDoS protection, while the terms describe DDoS filtering as shared and available for filtered IPs ordered separately, with no guarantee.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Lite sales text says IPv6-only with IPv4 available for an extra $2/month, while the Cloud IPv6 guide says all instances receive one IPv4 address.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Outbound SMTP port 25 is blocked by default in some regions and RamNode says it will extend the block to all regions by December 1, 2026. Bulk email is prohibited. A case-by-case exception may be requested; RamNode does not guarantee mail deliverability.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: VM system disk persists across normal restarts. Lite and Standard plans include 15–260 GB NVMe/SSD by size; separate NVMe Block Storage starts at 10 GB and costs $0.085/GB-month, billed hourly.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Shelving preserves VM data while stopping compute charges. Deleting the instance stops its compute billing; data should be backed up or saved as a separately billed image/volume before deletion.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, queues, and other software can be installed and self-managed in the VM. No managed database or database backup is included in the instance price.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: RamNode separately lists S3-compatible Object Storage and NVMe Block Storage. These are optional adjacent services with separate rates, not bundled VM database/storage credits.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: A custom domain can resolve to the VM public IP. RamNode's DNS-zone feature is listed in account quotas, but the VPS plan does not include domain registration. Customers can install and renew TLS certificates in the OS; the Cloud VPS guide includes a Let's Encrypt/Certbot guide.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Cloud snapshots can be created manually or on a schedule, then used to restore or launch an instance. This is a whole-image recovery path rather than branch previews or application-version rollback.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: No built-in preview deployment, promotion workflow, health-checked app release, or app-only rollback is documented for the VM.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Control Panel exposes usage and estimated costs; the documentation also describes resource monitoring and Linux log commands. The status page reports provider components and incidents.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Managed application-log retention, export, log-drain endpoints, alert rules, and long-term VM metric retention are not published in the Cloud docs checked.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Cloud Panel uses separate credentials or Client Area SSO; customers have root access and can use SSH keys. SSH 2FA is documented as an OS-level option.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Additional cloud users can currently be added by support; a user-management guide says the self-service team system is under development. The quota page lists five team members/account, while the user guide says support can add as many as needed.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: No managed runtime secret vault or environment-variable manager for app code is documented. The customer controls root and must store application credentials in their own OS/app setup.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: No customer-hosted RamNode control plane is required. RamNode operates the cloud; the customer maintains the guest OS, app, firewall, updates, database, secrets, backups, monitoring, and recovery.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The VM is selected in a named data-center region. The InMotion DPA and privacy terms govern personal-data processing, but do not promise that all account, support, logging, backup, or control-plane data stays in the selected VM country.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Manual snapshots and scheduled instance/volume backups are available but are not automatic by default. Snapshot/image and volume-backup storage is billed by used GB at $0.10/GB-month, billed hourly.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Restore points can restore an instance or launch a new one; snapshots must be launched on equal or larger disk. Backup retention defaults, incremental/deduplication behavior, exact restore time, and automatic schedule retention are not specified.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud snapshot/backups are stored within the project/region; the backup-strategy page says cloud snapshots are in the same region and are not offsite disaster-recovery copies.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: OpenStack API/CLI access, custom images, snapshots, SSH, and file-transfer tools provide ways to migrate a VM or its data. RamNode documents image and manual file migration from other providers.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Deleting an instance stops compute billing; ending service or deleting a server can remove customer data. The terms do not give a fixed post-deletion retention or recovery window.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: The terms offer a three-day refund period for an initial payment, exclude Bitcoin payments, require a support-ticket refund request after cancellation, and separately state a $50 minimum early-cancellation charge for term services.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Current product name: RamNode Cloud VPS, a self-managed cloud virtual server service.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: InMotion Hosting, Inc. acquired RamNode's assets in February 2021. RamNode's acquisition notice said the brand would continue independently; current legal terms identify InMotion Hosting, Inc. and its affiliates as the company operating/owning the linked RamNode service.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Cloud VPS and instance plans are currently offered for ordering. The public order links, current product/pricing pages, and current status board indicate an active service. No login or order was attempted.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Legacy KVM and OpenVZ services have separate documentation and control panels; Cloud VPS is described as RamNode's currently supported KVM platform. No dated end-of-sale or shutdown notice for Cloud VPS was found in the RamNode News archive or InMotion press archive checked.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: The Cloud getting-started guide advertises a 99.99% uptime SLA. The linked Universal Terms say uptime is not guaranteed, and the older official Pre-Sales knowledgebase page describes a 99.98% VPS uptime guarantee.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: The status board showed website, Client Area, Cloud Control Panel, and Legacy Control Panel operational; it listed no incidents for Nov 1–5, 2026.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Current support page lists ticket, live chat, documentation, and Discord community. The Universal Terms say qualified technical support is via ticket, in English; typical response is 1–3 US business days but not guaranteed.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Professional Services are listed at $80/hour in half-hour increments. The linked terms describe them as paid, non-subscription assistance for eligible current customers.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: RamNode Cloud VPS is a hosted infrastructure service, not installable deployment software. A customer does not acquire a separate RamNode server-software license; installed OS, panel, and application licenses remain separate.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Team: pay as you go, no platform base fee, no seat limit, and no per-seat charge.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Annual selector applies 15% off module prices: standard is $4.25/month equivalent and container is $25.50/month equivalent.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Pricing says annual billing; whether the annual option is paid upfront or billed monthly, and any minimum commitment, are not specified.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Enterprise pricing is custom; volume pricing and annual contract are listed.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Prices are shown in USD; whether tax is included or added at checkout is not stated.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: AWS Marketplace is offered as a way to bill the Ravion subscription through an AWS account.

facts.label: Included compute and storage

facts.label: Included compute and storage
