facts.value: Standard: Starter 512M €7.20, 1G €14.40, 2G €28.80; Business 512M €20, 1G €40, 2G €80 per 30 days, ex VAT.

facts.label: Restricted-region Postgres rates
facts.value: SecNumCloud-region column: Starter 512M €8.64, 1G €17.28, 2G €34.56; Business 512M €24, 1G €48, 2G €96 per 30 days, ex VAT.

facts.label: Database excess storage
facts.value: Included disk is evaluated in GB-hours; extra osc-fr1 storage €0.0007/GB-hour; pricing also quotes €0.0008333/GB-hour for a region named snc-fr1.

facts.label: Excess-storage region naming
facts.value: The pricing FAQ uses snc-fr1 while its plan table/docs use osc-secnum-fr1; the checked sources do not explicitly map the names for the excess-disk rate.

facts.label: Ongoing free app offer
facts.value: No recurring free app-container plan is listed; the public offer is a 30-day trial followed by paid resource use.

facts.label: Legacy Sandbox database access
facts.value: New Sandbox databases are unavailable from March 2, 2026; requests are substituted with the smallest corresponding Starter plan.

facts.label: Public inbound/outbound charges
facts.value: No ingress fees and no egress fees; outbound traffic is free of charge, without a per-GB paid overage stated in these network docs.

facts.label: Bandwidth and database connectivity
facts.value: Per-container bandwidth 20 MB/s (160 Mbit/s), burst 1.6 GB/s (12.8 Gbit/s) as published. Shared DBs are reachable from same-region Scalingo apps by default.

facts.label: Builder capacity and deploy limits
facts.value: Build container: 6 CPUs, 8 GB RAM, 4 GB swap; maximum build 30 minutes; ten parallel builds per owner, excess queued; maximum app image 2 GiB.

facts.label: Build minute pricing
facts.value: No explicit separate build-minute tariff, included minute allowance or unambiguous statement that all builds are free was found.

facts.label: Source archive and previews
facts.value: Source archive maximum 300 MB uncompressed; completed app image 2 GiB. Review apps are normal separately billed resources, with configurable automatic cleanup on PR closure.

facts.label: Included standard features
facts.value: Custom domains, automatic Let's Encrypt, performance metrics, unlimited collaborators and log archives are included with containers.

facts.label: Optional network/export charges
facts.value: TCP Gateway free with unlimited traffic; Docker Image export €50/30 days; OpenVPN €30/30 days, excluding VAT.

facts.label: Persistence and compliance extras
facts.value: Persistent uploaded files need an external object-store provider. HDS has no certification surcharge for equal infrastructure, but requires Business/Enterprise DB class and at least two app containers.

facts.label: Consumption visibility and alerts
facts.value: Consumption reports update daily around midnight UTC; GTC say Budget Line overruns are alerted and charged automatically or invoiced.

facts.label: Enforced whole-account budget cap
facts.value: No documented hard account-wide cap or immediate automatic pause at a user-set euro amount was found.

facts.label: Resource bounds and stopping caveats
facts.value: Autoscaler enforces chosen minimum/maximum instances; manual zero stops long-running processes but does not stop scheduler jobs/one-offs or delete database/add-on resources.

facts.label: Failed-payment behavior
facts.value: Retries use the selected method only; SEPA failure does not fall back to card. Persistent failure suspends all apps/add-ons; unresolved failure may lead to deletion.

facts.label: Idle behavior and manual scaling
facts.value: Containers never sleep automatically under the public paid offer; manual horizontal/vertical scaling supported. Default maximum ten containers per process type, support can increase.

facts.label: Managed autoscaling limits and cost
facts.value: Built-in autoscaler is free, requires minimum two containers, respects selected maximum; newly started containers are billed normally.

facts.label: Request and router limits
facts.value: Request body 75 MB; combined headers 32 kB, single header 8 kB; each router queues at most fifty requests per web container, then returns 503.

facts.label: Environment-value limit inconsistency
facts.value: Environment guide first says values up to 8,192 characters, later limits section says up to 32,768; variable names consistently maximum 64.

facts.label: Existing PHP upload restriction
facts.value: Multipart requests on PHP apps created before October 21, 2026 remain disabled until explicitly re-enabled with CLI 1.51.0+; affected upload/form requests return 403.

facts.label: Trial limits and payment prerequisite
facts.value: Eligible accounts: 30 days; billing profile plus valid payment method required. Maximum one app, five S/M containers, one smallest Postgres/MySQL/Caching instance each; no review app.

facts.label: Trial ending conflict
facts.value: Current guide: resources keep running and automatic paid billing starts. GTC Article 4: without a new subscription, use ceases and resources are deleted after 30 more days; Article 9 says trial automatically expires.

facts.label: Professional and academic eligibility
facts.value: GTC cover professional natural/legal persons and professional or academic Orders; GTU defines Client as a professional registered in a commercial register.

facts.label: Payments and SEPA conditions
facts.value: Visa, MasterCard, American Express; PayPal prepaid credit from €5; SEPA for EU customers after three consecutive invoices of at least €100 paid by another method, arranged with support.

facts.label: Trial anti-abuse checks
facts.value: Scalingo may reject trial applications using temporary email, disposable card, newly created domain or newly created GitHub account.

facts.label: Ordinary-region country coverage
facts.value: A complete osc-fr1 buyer-country/identity acceptance matrix was not found.

facts.label: Commercial-use scope
facts.value: Professional paid app/database hosting is allowed; customer retains its code/data rights. No separate non-commercial-only S/M plan restriction appears in the paid tariff or terms.

facts.label: Prohibited uses
facts.value: GTU prohibit unlawful/discriminatory/fraudulent content, infringement, malicious code, intrusion, security bypass, trial-limit evasion and cryptocurrency mining.

facts.label: Management model
facts.value: Fully managed Linux application containers and managed database services on Outscale infrastructure; Scalingo maintains the hosting platform.

facts.label: Supported workloads and overlap
facts.value: Websites, arbitrary compatible application/API code, continuous background process types, scheduled tasks and static files served by an app container; managed databases overlap databases/backend.

facts.label: Compute regions
facts.value: Two current public regions, both Paris, France: osc-fr1 on Outscale eu-west-2; osc-secnum-fr1 on Outscale cloudgouv-eu-west-1.

facts.label: Restricted-region admission
facts.value: osc-secnum-fr1 apps must be owned by an EU-established company/public body with EU physical presence and a legitimate need; individuals ineligible.

facts.label: Delivery and CDN scope
facts.value: Normal delivery uses region-local front-end reverse proxies; no included worldwide edge-cache location list or included CDN tariff found.

facts.label: Native runtime model
facts.value: Buildpacks detect/build Ruby, Node.js, PHP, Python, Java/JVM, Go and other compatible languages; custom and combined buildpacks supported.

facts.label: Current base stack and retirement
facts.value: Default scalingo-26 uses Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, supported through May 2031; scalingo-24 supported through May 2029; scalingo-22 deprecated through May 2027.

facts.label: Node.js versions
facts.value: Current Node guide lists 22 LTS through 22.23.4, 24 LTS through 24.22.2 and 26 through 26.13.0 across 22/24/26 stacks; latest 24 is default.

facts.label: Prebuilt Docker input
facts.value: No documented arbitrary prebuilt Docker image/Dockerfile deployment input found in checked deployment, stack, custom-buildpack and image-addon pages.

facts.label: Next.js deployment
facts.value: Official standalone guide uses output: standalone, a Node server on 0.0.0.0, and explicit copying of .next/static and public assets.

facts.label: Next.js advanced feature scope
facts.value: No feature matrix for managed ISR/shared cache, framework image transforms, version-specific SSR or streaming behavior found.

facts.label: Deployment methods and management tools
facts.value: Git push, GitHub/GitHub Enterprise, GitLab integrations, tar archive, built JAR/WAR; dashboard, CLI, HTTP API and Terraform operations.

facts.label: Private repositories and permissions
facts.value: GitHub linking requires repository admin rights/organization access, with repo-scoped authorization for Enterprise token integration; SCM links owned or organization repositories.

facts.label: Continuous background processes
facts.value: Procfile defines independent process types such as worker/clock as well as web; each process has its own container formation and size.

facts.label: Managed scheduler
facts.value: Scalingo Scheduler itself is free; up to five cron tasks, minimum ten-minute interval, UTC schedule; runs billed one-off containers, default M/512 MiB.

facts.label: One-off task limits
facts.value: Maximum ten one-offs per app and fifty per account; size configurable; detached jobs start immediately and require the owner to ensure they terminate.

facts.label: HTTP and live connections
facts.value: HTTP/HTTPS, HTTP/2 to the router, WebSockets, server-sent events and long-running streams supported; router-to-container traffic is HTTP/1.1.

facts.label: Public ports and address families
facts.value: Public app ingress uses IPv4 ports 80/443; other public ports are dropped; optional TCP Gateway supports TCP applications. Public IPv6 is not supported.

facts.label: Private app networking
facts.value: Free project-scoped private networks isolate app containers, with private DNS and Scalingo-managed WireGuard encryption; arbitrary private TCP/UDP ports supported.

facts.label: Outbound addresses and TLS defaults
facts.value: Outgoing traffic uses published regional IPv4 pools; IPs may change with at least 30 days' notice. Shared database Force TLS is disabled by default.

facts.label: App files are temporary
facts.value: /app and /tmp writable; files disappear on restart or redeploy. No persistent app volume is provided by this filesystem model.

facts.label: Durable file service dependency
facts.value: Recommended external services include Outscale OOS, S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob and OVH object storage; signed direct uploads suggested for larger files.

facts.label: Managed supporting services
facts.value: Managed Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Caching, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and InfluxDB are listed; caching backup docs now name Valkey.

facts.label: Database editions and isolation
facts.value: Shared Resources: container/shared CPU, application add-on, single AZ. Dedicated Resources: private VM/VPC, dedicated CPU/disk, up to three AZ, currently selected PostgreSQL customers only.

facts.label: HA and certification scope
facts.value: Starter single node; Business hot standby with 99.96% SLA; Enterprise multiple standby with 99.99%. Scalingo states ISO 27001/HDS certification, not yet PaaS SecNumCloud qualification.

facts.label: Custom and generated domains
facts.value: Generated Scalingo domain; maximum twenty attached custom domains per app by default, support can raise; domain registration purchased elsewhere.

facts.label: TLS automation and wildcard exception
facts.value: Managed generated-domain certificate; free automatic Let's Encrypt for custom domains. Wildcards need DNS TXT verification and either manual renewal steps or supported DNS-provider API automation.

facts.label: Certificate/wildcard cadence inconsistency
facts.value: Default-certificate guide says 45-day certificates and renewal starts at day 30, but its wildcard paragraph still says TXT updates every three months.

facts.label: Rolling deployment and health gate
facts.value: Build succeeds, new web/TCP containers start and pass TCP-port readiness; postdeploy hook runs, traffic switches, then old containers get thirty seconds to exit.

facts.label: Review apps and staging safety
facts.value: GitHub/GitLab PR review apps can auto-create/update/delete; copy formation, stack, collaborators, environment and add-on plan settings, excluding DB contents.

facts.label: Rollback method
facts.value: Documented rollback is Git-pushing an earlier commit, causing a rebuild. Direct deployment of an older stored build is described as not publicly available and support-assisted.

facts.label: App, router and database logs
facts.value: Dashboard/CLI access stdout/stderr and add-on logs; router logs opt-in; current hot log archived after 50 MiB; all logs retained one year.

facts.label: Log ingestion and exports
facts.value: Per container live ingestion maximum 16,384 lines/minute and 64 MiB/minute; overflow lines are dropped until next minute. Log drains support third-party services and syslog.

facts.label: Metrics and operational alerts
facts.value: Dashboard CPU/RAM, requests/minute, response/error charts; selectable history windows 3/12/24/48/72 hours. Metric alerts notify selected notifiers after a configured duration.

facts.label: Two-factor and roles
facts.value: Optional TOTP two-factor login with recovery codes; Owner, Collaborator, Limited Collaborator roles; Owner billed and controls app deletion/rename.

facts.label: Secrets and support access
facts.value: App environment variables injected into builds/runtime/one-offs; code should not store credentials in Git. Support data/source access ordinarily requires express prior approval.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed platform; no customer OS/root/hardware/update installation requirements for running its control plane.

facts.label: Hosted data, logs and backups
facts.value: DPA Article 8 places hosted personal data in selected French Outscale region; database/log backup OOS storage also in that region in France.

facts.label: Account/support transfer exceptions
facts.value: DPA Part III names US Intercom support processing, US PayPal and conditional Cloudflare USA/Europe processing, with stated transfer safeguards.

facts.label: Retention and encryption scope
facts.value: DPA: customer-resource processing agreement duration + 30-day return period unless otherwise requested; user/account records can be archived five years, invoices ten years. Platform data is encrypted at rest.

facts.label: Shared Postgres daily backup retention
facts.value: Managed full logical backup enabled daily by default; Starter retains last seven daily plus four weekly; Business seven daily/eight weekly/twelve monthly.

facts.label: Manual backups and after deletion
facts.value: Starter last ten manual backups, Business fifty; kept until rolling limit while DB exists. After DB deletion manual backups use creation-based one-month/one-year limits respectively.

facts.label: Postgres continuous recovery
facts.value: Shared Resources PITR seven days; Dedicated Starter seven, Business fourteen, Enterprise thirty. First base backup may take up to twenty-four hours.

facts.label: Restore and backup export tools
facts.value: Download logical .tar.gz archives via dashboard/CLI, extract and restore with pg_restore; direct pg_dump also documented; Shared PITR restore is dashboard-only.

facts.label: Source and database exit
facts.value: Keep source in own Git; export environment settings via CLI, download Postgres logical backups or pg_dump, restore with standard tools on another service.

facts.label: Runnable image export
facts.value: Optional €50/30-day image-download add-on, osc-fr1 only, last twenty built images per pricing; export starts with /start and requires re-supplying environment variables.

facts.label: Deletion and paid exit assistance
facts.value: Export before deleting: access ceases immediately. Account deletion requires transferring/deleting owned projects/resources and is irreversible; extra recovery assistance can require a separate quote.

facts.label: Product and operator
facts.value: Scalingo; https://scalingo.com/; operated by Scalingo SAS, Strasbourg registration 808 665 483, France.

facts.label: Current offer and signup
facts.value: Active public PaaS/database offer with pricing, trial instructions and new-app creation documentation; no current platform shutdown found.

facts.label: Historical region shutdown
facts.value: agora-fr1 was decommissioned August 31, 2020; customers were directed to osc-fr1.

facts.label: Current resource sunsets
facts.value: New customers lost swap June 1, 2026; new apps of existing customers September 1; all app-container swap ends January 1, 2027. Sandbox databases stopped new provisioning March 2, 2026.

facts.label: Open maintenance notice
facts.value: Public status says all systems online, but emergency infrastructure maintenance has an Update dated October 27, 2026, without a final resolved update.

facts.label: Emergency infrastructure maintenance
facts.value: Status page reports an emergency security update by infrastructure provider Outscale across both regions beginning October 21, 2026. As of the November 5 update, mitigation had ended in osc-secnum-fr1, while some osc-fr1 workloads still awaited provider schedule; brief availability impacts remained possible.

facts.label: Application SLA
facts.value: One container 98.00% monthly availability; two or more containers 99.9%. Beta/non-GA resources excluded.

facts.label: Database SLA and credits
facts.value: Starter/Essential 98%; Business 99.96%; Enterprise 99.99%. Credit is 5% of affected pre-tax service price per hour beyond target, capped at 50% monthly price.

facts.label: Autoscaler SLA wording conflict
facts.value: Autoscaler limitations refer to 99.96% SLA for minimum two app containers; signed-style SLA page says application 99.9% for two or more.

facts.label: Status history and unresolved maintenance
facts.value: Current component view all online; October 31 osc-secnum app-operation incident and October 30 osc-fr1 DB-host incident marked resolved; broader emergency banner remains unclosed.

facts.label: Included support
facts.value: Basic email/live chat during business days, 9 AM–6 PM local time; English/French docs and support; no Basic guaranteed response time listed.

facts.label: Paid priority support
facts.value: Starter: higher of €100/month or 5% usage, three-month commitment, one-hour business-hours response. Business: higher of €500 or 10%, six months, 30 minutes in-hours/one hour out-of-hours.

facts.label: Custom operational support
facts.value: MCO: contact sales, twelve-month commitment, custom 24/7 monitoring/team and response up to fifteen minutes; tailored app/network/third-party monitoring.

facts.label: Published support-hours inconsistency
facts.value: Support-plan page says business days 9 AM–6 PM local time; legal notice lists 9 AM–12 PM and 2 PM–6 PM CET/CEST.

facts.label: Hosted software license and service terms
facts.value: Hosted proprietary platform governed by GTC/GTU; limited non-transferable service-use right, customer retains code/data ownership; no self-hosted platform license offered here.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections

facts.value: Migrations can copy files, database, or both from ServerPilot or SSH-accessible hosting; the migration can be tested and run into an existing or new app.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: App access logs rotate daily and rotated app logs are retained for one week; server-log retention varies by file.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring

facts.value: Each app runs as an isolated system user; its processes cannot read other apps' files unless apps share a system user.

facts.label: Access and secret handling

facts.value: New connection requires a fresh standard Ubuntu LTS image, x64 architecture, and at least 256 MB RAM; root or sudo access is required for installation.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: ServerPilot configures Nginx, Apache, MySQL, PHP, firewall, and daily automatic package/security updates by default; customer owns app code, provider account, and data backups.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms

facts.label: Solo base/seat fees
facts.value: No company plan, seat fee or standard long-term contract; each service/resource is billed separately. Static site fee is US$0; runtime H1 US$5/month, S1 US$10, C1 US$18, S2 US$40.

facts.label: Taxes, currency and billing cycle
facts.value: Prices are USD excluding tax. Usage period runs 1st to 1st, charged by Stripe to the default card after the period; tax follows billing address/tax ID.

facts.label: Cancellation and refunds
facts.value: Current docs stop resource billing on deletion and settle a final company invoice immediately; unused credits are removed. Terms ordinarily make fees non-refundable and describe cancellation at subscription-period end.

facts.label: Subscription-period wording conflict
facts.value: Current billing docs use calendar months, while the binding 2025 SLA defines anniversary-date monthly periods and terms describe general renewing subscription periods.

facts.label: Resource units and local disk
facts.value: Detailed pricing explicitly defines 1 GB as 1,000,000,000 bytes; API memory/storage limits are MB with 1000 MB = 1 GB. Each runtime instance has up to 20 GB ephemeral disk.

facts.label: CPU isolation details
facts.value: Published pod vCPU allocations and throttling behavior are clear, but a complete dedicated-physical-core versus shared-host CPU contract and processor-family matrix was not found.

facts.label: Database entry allocations
facts.value: DB1 0.25 CPU/0.25 GB/1 GB disk US$5; DB2 0.5 CPU/2 GB/5 GB US$34; DB3 1 CPU/4 GB/10 GB US$65 per 730-hour reference month.

facts.label: Larger database specification conflict
facts.value: Marketing prices DB7/8/9 at 16/30/60 CPU and 64/120/240 GB RAM; current detailed docs list 14.5/28.5/58.5 CPU and 58/108.5/229 GB at the same prices.

facts.label: Meters and 730-hour convention
facts.value: Running compute/databases/disks/builds/load balancers are metered by the second; bandwidth by byte; object storage by each hour's peak size. Monthly reference price means 730 hours.

facts.label: Hourly precision inconsistency
facts.value: Pricing says hourly prices are monthly/730 rounded to four decimals, but its worked example calculates from unrounded monthly/730 ratios.

facts.label: Ongoing static allowance
facts.value: US$0 static-site fee; 100 GB bandwidth and 600 build minutes per company per billing period, shared across production and preview sites; 100 sites/company.

facts.label: Free limits and excess behavior
facts.value: Static publish directory maximum 1 GB; default 30-minute build limit. Beyond shared allowances bandwidth costs US$0.10/GB and builds US$0.05/minute.

facts.label: Application transfer charges
facts.value: Application response data via generated/custom domains costs US$0.10/GB, measured at US$0.0000000001/byte. Incoming traffic and internal same-location connections are free.

facts.label: Database, static and bucket traffic
facts.value: Database internal and external traffic is not billed; static has company-pooled 100-GB allowance then US$0.10/GB; object-storage operations/ingress/egress are free, storage paid.

facts.label: Application builds
facts.value: 4 vCPU/8 GB builder, US$0.02/minute billed by second; no included app build-minute allowance. Prebuilt Docker-image deploys skip the build and its fee.

facts.label: Static build allowance/rate
facts.value: Static builder 4 CPUs/8 GB; 600 shared minutes/billing period included, then US$0.05/minute billed by second. Build includes clone through upload.

facts.label: Deployment time and queues
facts.value: App whole deployment defaults to 30 minutes, one deployment/application at a time; per-process rollout timeout 20 minutes. Static production one/site at a time; ten queued/running with parallel branch previews.

facts.label: Persistent disks and optional extras
facts.value: App disks US$0.30/GB/month, minimum 10 GB/US$3; billed by second while attached process runs. Standalone edge load balancer US$40/month plus its response bandwidth; object storage US$0.02/GB/month.

facts.label: Database disk-addon conflict
facts.value: Marketing offers extra disk at US$10/month per 10 GB through support; current database/limits docs say storage cannot be added separately and requires a larger database size.

facts.label: Usage alerts, not caps
facts.value: Company and project alerts email at 1–10 chosen thresholds of a positive USD budget; new alert defaults 80%/100%; alerts never stop/suspend/limit services.

facts.label: Scaling stops and residual bills
facts.value: Manual zero instances/hibernation/suspension stops app compute; suspended databases stop runtime billing. Separate databases, bucket data and other running resources remain independent.

facts.label: Manual/automatic scaling
facts.value: Web/worker instances 0–20 dashboard by default, 0–50 via API; autoscale min ≥1 with CPU/memory targets, configurable max/steps/intervals. Sizes change on deployment.

facts.label: Hibernation behavior
facts.value: Opt-in HTTP-idle hibernation stops web and workers, wakes on next domain HTTP request. Private/TCP connections do not wake it; cron/jobs keep their schedules; hibernation and autoscaling cannot be combined.

facts.label: Idle/suspended billing
facts.value: Processes bill only while instances run; zero/hibernate/suspend stops compute. Disk billing follows attached process running time; suspended database has no runtime charge, but backup buckets remain billed.

facts.label: CPU/RAM and request limits
facts.value: RAM hard cap kills/restarts with exit 137; CPU over allocation throttles. HTTP response wait up to 185 seconds; hibernated-mode headers within 15 seconds; no session affinity across instances.

facts.label: General HTTP payload cap
facts.value: A universal maximum normal request body and a separate fixed WebSocket idle lifetime were not established in current limits/network/infra/terms; hibernation explicitly rejects wake requests over 50 MB or without Content-Length.

facts.label: Static/deploy and variable limits
facts.value: Static output 1 GB/deployment; ten queued/running deploys/site; app default whole deployment 30 minutes/rollout 20 minutes. Environment keys up to 255 chars, values 32,768 chars; no count cap published in limit table.

facts.label: Entry credit and card
facts.value: Public signup guide offers US$20 on adding a valid payment method; current billing docs say once per person on the first company, all usage types covered; card and billing details required before resource use.

facts.label: Trial expiry conflict
facts.value: Signup page says the US$20 credit expires after 30 days; current billing docs say the second day of the second month after company creation, e.g. October 18 → December 2.

facts.label: Payments and buyer eligibility
facts.value: Credit/debit card on Stripe; optional support-arranged prepaid funding from US$5,000 via card/bank transfer still requires card on file. Terms require age 13 or local higher minimum, with guardian responsibility for minors.

facts.label: Sanctions and domain restrictions
facts.value: Terms exclude sanctioned parties and listed embargoed/residency categories, including Iran, Syria, Cuba, North Korea, Russia and specified occupied Ukrainian regions. Custom .ru domains are refused.

facts.label: Commercial use and ownership
facts.value: Terms allow creating/managing customer apps and serving own third-party clients; customer retains app/content ownership. No non-commercial-only restriction found for ordinary static allowance or paid app sizes.

facts.label: Prohibited use and testing
facts.value: Terms prohibit explicit adult content, infringement, phishing/spam/malware, open proxies, IRC and crypto mining. Load testing is prohibited except on dedicated servers; app security tests have advance-notice rules.

facts.label: Managed hosting responsibility
facts.value: Applications and databases run on Kubernetes clusters in one selected OCI or Google Cloud region; Sevalla operates servers/OS/clusters/registry/network. Customers maintain code, dependencies, schemas and configuration.

facts.label: Static, storage and edge modes
facts.value: Static files and S3-compatible object storage use Cloudflare R2; static delivery and optional standalone load balancers run at Cloudflare's edge.

facts.label: Supported app types
facts.value: Arbitrary compatible web/API containers, server-rendered apps, continuous workers, cron jobs and deployment jobs; static files use the dedicated static product.

facts.label: Static-only limitations
facts.value: Static service publishes prebuilt files without a server process; SSR, API routes, per-request code and direct server-side database/session handling need an application.

facts.label: New-company OCI locations
facts.value: 20: Ashburn, Chicago, Montréal, Phoenix, San Jose, Santiago, São Paulo, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, London, Madrid, Stockholm, Zurich, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Tokyo, Sydney and Dubai.

facts.label: Legacy locations and edge scope
facts.value: Unmigrated companies see 25 Google Cloud locations mapped to OCI destinations. Static origin builds are always OCI Ashburn; edge delivery is marketed as 260+ locations; bucket location is a Cloudflare R2 hint.

facts.label: Native build/runtime families
facts.value: Ingot supports Node/Bun/TypeScript, Deno, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust, Java, .NET, Elixir, Gleam, Zig, C/C++, static files and shell applications; Dockerfile/image supports compatible custom stacks.

facts.label: Default runtime versions and configuration
facts.value: Ingot 0.5.0 lists default Node 24, Python 3.14, PHP 8.5, Java 25 and .NET 10, configurable by language variables, ingot.json or repository version files.

facts.label: Container architecture
facts.value: Prebuilt application images must target linux/amd64. Other architectures crash. Build/runtime containers are sandboxed; default Ingot final image runs as UID/GID 1000 rather than root.

facts.label: Static build environment
facts.value: Static builder uses selected Node version and lockfile-based npm/Yarn/pnpm/Bun. Latest LTS maps to Node 26 since October 28, 2026; selectable older majors remain listed.

facts.label: Next.js serving and static export
facts.value: Official guide deploys Next.js with next build/next start, or standalone node server.js; output:export can use static-site hosting.

facts.label: Next.js ISR, middleware and images
facts.value: Migration guide confirms single-instance ISR; multiple instances need a shared cache such as Redis for coordinated revalidation. next/image runs in the app; middleware/edge-runtime routes execute in the selected origin server.

facts.label: Streaming/framework deployment scope
facts.value: Core HTTP supports unbuffered SSE/chunked responses. Framework caching and edge caching still need app-specific configuration, particularly personalized pages.

facts.label: Git providers/private repositories
facts.value: GitHub.com, GitLab.com and Bitbucket Cloud public/private repositories; authorized accounts grant private access. Self-managed GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server and Bitbucket Data Center cannot be directly connected.

facts.label: Docker, CLI/API and source controls
facts.value: Dockerfile in Git or public/private container image, with saved registry credentials, are supported. API/CLI/Terraform/GitHub Actions and deploy hooks automate operations; source root/build path supports monorepos.

facts.label: Workers and deployment jobs
facts.value: Background workers run continuously and restart after exit; jobs run before deployment, after success or after failure. They use independent sized processes and second-metered compute.

facts.label: Cron scheduling and execution
facts.value: Five-field cron, at most once a minute; UTC default or IANA timezone. One instance/run; skip overlap by default or replace; retry failed run once; max duration off by default or configured in seconds.

facts.label: Cron observability
facts.value: Run history retained 30 days, including exit/max-time/replacement reasons, retries and logs; process card shows last 30 runs.

facts.label: HTTP, WebSocket, SSE and gRPC
facts.value: HTTP/HTTPS through Cloudflare; WebSockets on web process, unbuffered SSE/chunked streaming. gRPC is selectable and app must serve cleartext HTTP/2 h2c internally.

facts.label: Private connections and TCP
facts.value: Same-location app/app or app/database internal connections open otherwise isolated namespace paths. Web/worker processes can expose TCP proxies; proxy traffic bypasses Cloudflare protection.

facts.label: Fixed egress and outbound restrictions
facts.value: OCI has one fixed egress IP shared by workloads per region; Google Cloud uses the provider's regional ranges. SMTP 25/465/587 blocked on both, plus 2525 on OCI.

facts.label: Networking limits
facts.value: Web port defaults 8080 and must bind 0.0.0.0; configured 1–65535 excludes platform-reserved ports. TCP proxy assigned ports 20000–29999 or 32768–65000; default dashboard quota three/app.

facts.label: Ephemeral versus durable files
facts.value: Runtime local writes are erased on every restart/deploy; each instance has up to 20 GB. Persistent disk survives both and belongs to exactly one web process or worker.

facts.label: Persistent disk sizes and rollout
facts.value: 10–1000 GB listed sizes, grow-only; attached process is single-instance with no autoscale, and deployment stops old process before starting new, causing downtime.

facts.label: Managed service types and privilege
facts.value: Managed PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Redis and Valkey. Each server exposes one database and one non-superuser account; no extra databases/users on that server.

facts.label: Database cloud/version split
facts.value: New OCI PostgreSQL 18/17/16; Google Cloud 17/16. Other engine/version choices also differ. Existing no-longer-offered versions can keep running; upgrading requires new DB and data migration.

facts.label: Database resizing and connections
facts.value: Size increases restart briefly; memory/storage cannot be downgraded in place. Same-location internal connections are free; external access defaults off, with credentials and optional IP allow/deny restrictions.

facts.label: Domains and certificates
facts.value: Generated sevalla.app for apps, sevalla.page for static sites, sevalla.net for load balancers; custom domains and automatic Cloudflare-issued/renewed TLS are documented.

facts.label: Wildcard and domain rules
facts.value: No custom-domain count limit per service in limits table. Wildcards use a checkbox rather than a literal *. name, with DNS validation; .ru rejected; same hostname may exist on only one service across companies.

facts.label: Readiness/liveness and deployment ordering
facts.value: Health probes off by default. Readiness gates traffic; liveness restarts failures. Defaults: period 10s, timeout 1s, success one, failures three; HTTP 200–399 passes.

facts.label: Rollback and partial failure scope
facts.value: Git rollback reuses a prior successful different-commit image with current process settings/runtime variables; old build-time values stay in image. No database/volume contents are rolled back.

facts.label: Pipelines and previews
facts.value: Free pipeline/stage organization; trunk-based promotion reuses an image without rebuilding. Preview app per PR/branch is a separately billed app, deleted on PR close or configured stale policy.

facts.label: Static preview/revert behavior
facts.value: Static production switches atomically after success and keeps previous live version on failure; branch/commit previews are separate, consume shared quotas and expire 30 days after finishing/latest branch preview.

facts.label: Runtime, request and build logs
facts.value: App runtime stdout/stderr plus Cloudflare access logs; build logs per deployment. Search/filter, live tail and JSON/CSV download are documented.

facts.label: Metrics/history limits
facts.value: Resource, replica and Web HTTP analytics; dashboard custom logs/metrics time range up to 60 days, log arrival up to two minutes.

facts.label: Login, 2FA and SSO
facts.value: Email/password login requires email or authenticator code; supported Git login and company SSO delegate authentication. Trusted-device exception lasts 30 days with same browser/IP/method.

facts.label: Roles and project isolation
facts.value: Company owner/admin/developer/billing, project admin/developer and per-service administrator roles; owner alone can delete company/transfer it.

facts.label: Secret handling
facts.value: Variable values encrypted at rest and masked/revealable; build/runtime/both scopes, default both. Runtime values reach all processes; company globals can be overridden by app-specific keys.

facts.label: API key scope and escalation capability
facts.value: Keys are hashed, shown once, company-scoped with roles/custom resource capabilities; optional expiry and rotation grace. API_KEY:CREATE can create keys with any role, including company admin.

facts.label: AI support access
facts.value: Stella answers from docs by default; optional company AI-support permissions can grant read/action API access, including read-only commands inside processes under Read applications.

facts.label: Published security assurance/advisory
facts.value: Security docs state SOC 2 Type II audited and ISO/IEC 27001:2022/27017/27018 certified, Sevalla in scope. October PHP advisory describes provider redeploy mitigation with exceptions for failed/pinned/suspended apps.

facts.label: Self-host installation and operator work
facts.value: Customer control-plane/server installation not applicable to managed Sevalla. Provider manages OS/Kubernetes/platform; customers handle code/dependencies, data, backup targets and safe resource/network configuration.

facts.label: Runtime/build/storage data locations
facts.value: Apps, disks and database live in their selected region; app builds run there too. Static builds run OCI Ashburn, files/buckets use Cloudflare R2, and edge caching creates worldwide copies.

facts.label: Public DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Kinsta DPA and named subprocessor list cover Sevalla. Analytics/access logs and ClickHouse log storage are listed in the US; support vendors in the US; AI tooling providers in US/Ireland.

facts.label: Privacy and sensitive-data scope
facts.value: Privacy policy covers provider-collected account/business data and excludes customer-app data. DPA permits customer-controlled sensitive data with safeguards and notice of categories/restrictions.

facts.label: Retention after cancellation
facts.value: Privacy retains account data after cancellation for possible reinstatement and legal purposes. DPA requires reasonable deletion/return on proper termination/written direction, with reasonable efforts to delete within 45 days.

facts.label: Google Cloud snapshot backups
facts.value: Automatic daily database snapshots retained seven days, up to five manual snapshots retained 14 days; snapshots not downloadable, restore compatibility is exact engine/version/location.

facts.label: OCI external backup targets
facts.value: New OCI databases dump to up to five configured S3-compatible targets; daily/hourly/weekly schedules, automatic retention 1–365 days (default seven), manual retention 0–365 (default 14).

facts.label: Backup formats and restore
facts.value: OCI PostgreSQL/MySQL/MariaDB dumps are compressed .sql.gz; Redis/Valkey .rdb.gz. Download supported for Sevalla targets; restore same/newer engine version in same company/location; dump restore capped at one hour.

facts.label: Persistent app disk backups
facts.value: App disks are backed up daily, kept seven days; restore through support with app/mount path. Deleting app deletes its disk backups.

facts.label: Legal portability wording conflict
facts.value: DPA Annex II broadly says customers can download backups; current product docs explicitly disallow downloading Google Cloud database snapshots.

facts.label: Source, configuration and image exit
facts.value: Source remains in user's Git/registry; variables can be exported. Git integrations, proprietary pipeline settings/internal DNS, generated domains and service IDs need replacement at another host.

facts.label: Database/file exit
facts.value: PostgreSQL exports with pg_dump custom/plain formats and restores using pg_restore/psql; OCI dumps downloadable; objects use S3 API, disk files can be copied to user-controlled storage.

facts.label: Deletion and failed-payment retention
facts.value: Deleting app/database removes live data and snapshots without recovery; OCI dump files remain in buckets until retention/manual removal. Failed payment retries about 15 days, then suspension; company deleted after 90 suspended days.

facts.label: Identity and operator
facts.value: Sevalla, a Kinsta product; contracting operator Kinsta Inc. Previous Kinsta application/database/static hosting is an alias, not a separate app-hosting company.

facts.label: Brand and dashboard transition
facts.value: Standalone Sevalla brand documented August 12, 2024; from February 2, 2026 app/database/static-site management moved from MyKinsta to Sevalla.

facts.label: Current operation and lifecycle search
facts.value: Active public offer, current pricing, registration path and operational status. No current full-platform shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the official sources searched.

facts.label: Current cloud migration
facts.value: New companies start on OCI; existing Google Cloud companies move in waves. Static builds moved September 1; Wave 1 began October 7; databases/disks/TCP-proxy companies move throughout November 2026.

facts.label: Retired endpoints and builder
facts.value: Legacy TCP/database external connection endpoints were disabled October 15, 2026. Ingot became default for new Git apps October 29; Nixpacks is deprecated but existing Nixpacks apps keep working.

facts.label: Uptime commitment
facts.value: Binding SLA updated September 25, 2025 guarantees 99.9% per monthly period unless order form higher; live apps/databases/static sites covered, provider monitoring decides downtime.

facts.label: Credits and claim deadline
facts.value: Above 43 minutes at 99.9% or four minutes at 99.99%, SLA permits credits; app/DB formula says twenty times affected subscription-value proportion, capped at month's eligible value. Request in chat within 30 days.

facts.label: SLA exclusions and maintenance
facts.value: Daily 02:00–05:00 local data-center maintenance excluded, as are emergency maintenance/scheduled outages, external providers/force majeure, excess workload and customer code/configuration.

facts.label: Current status/history
facts.value: Official status page says All Systems Operational; November 3 dashboard/API/support maintenance completed 09:38 UTC while hosted workloads were intended to keep running.

facts.label: Support channels and access
facts.value: Dashboard Support starts with Stella AI and can hand off to humans. Human support for active paid-service companies, English, Monday–Friday 08:00–17:00 UTC; sign-in trouble email support@sevalla.com.

facts.label: Support scope and response promise
facts.value: Provider supports platform/billing/connections; app development, code review, custom Dockerfile fixes and migration work are out of scope. No numerical guaranteed human first-response/resolution time found.

facts.label: Hosted license/commercial terms
facts.value: Self-host software license not applicable: Kinsta owns/licenses platform; terms grant limited access to operate customer applications, with customer retaining app/content ownership.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, acquisition, or customer-data breach found for Sliplane.

facts.label: Cheapest ongoing app price
facts.value: Germany/Finland Shared Starter: €9/month, 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 20 GB disk; per-server fee, no per-service or collaborator fee.

facts.label: Persistent published files

facts.label: Software license and hosted terms
facts.value: An installable platform license is not applicable to this managed service. Terms identify provider software/content as proprietary and govern hosted use.

facts.label: Git deployment inputs
facts.value: Any reachable repository URL supported by git clone; public/private Git, Git LFS, and monorepo working directories are documented. Private repositories use per-site deploy keys or authenticated HTTPS.

facts.label: Direct upload and CLI

facts.label: Management API maturity

facts.label: Workers and scheduled application jobs
facts.value: Not applicable to standard static hosting.

facts.label: Public network delivery
facts.value: HTTP/HTTPS website delivery with IPv4 and IPv6 across the edge network. HTTPS certificates are automatic.

facts.label: External backend proxy
facts.value: A 200 rewrite can proxy requests to a URL on another service, including external API requests.

facts.label: Long-lived and advanced proxy connections
facts.value: WebSocket upgrades, streamed proxy responses, maximum connection/proxy duration, upstream size limits, and private-origin network access were not established.

facts.label: Published files and replacement

facts.label: Writable application storage

facts.value: Finite build/revision retention, maximum stored versions, whole-site atomic cutover guarantees, and health-gated deployment checks were not established.

facts.label: Build-log retention and export
facts.value: Exact build-log retention and customer log-export facilities were not established.

facts.value: Invocation guide lists 15 regions, while status page lists 18 Functions components, additionally ap-east-1, eu-north-1 and us-east-2.

facts.value: CLI v3 released November 2, 2026; unattended hosted mutations require --yes, database commands default local unless --remote.

facts.value: Outbound SMTP ports 25 and 587 blocked; no static or stable outbound Edge Function IP addresses available.

facts.value: Arbitrary inbound TCP/UDP ports and private VPC connection availability for hosted functions not established in checked runtime, architecture, networking and Enterprise pricing sources.

facts.value: Ephemeral /tmp resets on every invocation. Persistent /s3 bucket mounts use S3-compatible object storage, including separately metered Supabase Storage.

facts.label: Persistent app files

facts.value: Supabase verifies domain DNS and issues the SSL certificate using one of several certificate authorities; no separate certificate issue price stated beyond domain add-on.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring

facts.value: Enterprise log ingest differs by source: detailed docs list 20 GB/month plus $0.50/GB, while headline plan comparison says custom.

facts.value: Supabase Edge Runtime software is MIT licensed; hosted service use is governed by Supabase service terms and AUP.

apps.name: Surge
apps.line: Publish static websites from a command line to Surge's CDN.

free.text: Free, no card; verify email before new surge.sh sites pause at 90 min

cells.regions: US, Canada, Europe, India, Asia-Pacific and Australia

work.math: $0 a month published Free subtotal. 100 MB, 1 million requests and 100 GB of data sent out fit only if the file count and publish timing meet the limits. Commercial permission and fair-use fit are unclear.
Surge does not provide a backend runtime for API execution.
Needs an external API host and separate PostgreSQL/backup service.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or qualifying security incident found.

facts.label: Free entry price and scope
facts.value: Free: $0, account-level, unlimited projects/domains, subject to published size/rate limits.

facts.label: Pro entry price and scope
facts.value: Pro: $30/month per account, covering the account's projects rather than a separate charge per project.

facts.label: Currency and taxes
facts.value: Dollar symbol published; ISO currency, tax inclusion, and country-specific billing treatment not established.

facts.label: Renewal, cancellation, and refunds
facts.value: Paid plans auto-renew; self-serve cancellation is immediate. On request, the latest month's fees are refundable; earlier charges are not.

facts.label: Customer compute allocation
facts.value: Not applicable: no customer app vCPU, RAM, processor architecture, or dedicated-core allocation is sold by this static host.

facts.label: Project storage size
facts.value: Both plans: 450 MB and 10,100 files per project.

facts.label: Metering and usage rates
facts.value: No metered bandwidth or overage charge; bill is the selected plan price.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Yes; recurring Free service without a trial window or project cap, within size/rate rules.

facts.label: New-account serving restriction
facts.value: Newly signed-up accounts' surge.sh domains serve for 90 minutes, then wait in ready state until email verification. Verification resumes serving without republishing.

facts.label: Publishing limit versus fair use
facts.value: Published rate limits pause publishing, not existing delivery. Separately, terms permit terminating projects that impose an unreasonable infrastructure/business burden.

facts.label: Inactivity/deletion clock
facts.value: A fixed inactivity-based sleep or deletion period was not established.

facts.label: Outgoing transfer and request charges
facts.value: Free/Pro delivery is not metered and has no published per-GB/request overage bill. No fixed included GB/month bucket is stated.

facts.label: App/database network traffic
facts.value: No server-side app/database traffic path is supplied by Surge. A browser or externally hosted API uses the other services' network rules.

facts.label: Build location, minutes, and cost
facts.value: Surge does not build source. Build locally or in external CI, then publish the output; no Surge build-minute allocation or machine is included.

facts.label: Publish rate limits
facts.value: Both plans, rolling windows: domain 30/15 minutes and 200/24 hours; account 60/15 minutes and 500/24 hours; IP 240/15 minutes.

facts.label: Deployment failure behavior
facts.value: Upload/propagation complete before atomic cutover; failed or interrupted publishing leaves the live revision in place. Oversized projects are rejected before publishing.

facts.label: Paid feature triggers
facts.value: AUTH rules and ROUTER files require Pro. Free already includes forced HTTPS, CORS, private domains, previews, and rollback.

facts.label: External or optional charges
facts.value: Domain registration, optional external CI, APIs, forms, databases, and third-party monitoring are separate dependencies, if chosen.

facts.label: Surprise-bill protection
facts.value: No bandwidth/overage metering; Free remains a zero-price plan unless upgraded. Publishing limits refuse work until their rolling window clears.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Static delivery is managed across the network; no customer instance count or CPU-idle meter. Pro is an account subscription independent of traffic.

facts.label: Request-time compute limits
facts.value: Application execution duration, function memory, and worker concurrency limits are not applicable because no application runtime is supplied.

facts.label: Additional delivery/upload ceilings
facts.value: Numeric static-response concurrency, maximum single-file size, and publish timeout were not established beyond the total project cap.

facts.label: Trial and payment-card requirements
facts.value: Free is not a temporary trial. Initial documented signup asks for email/password; card entry is introduced when upgrading to Pro.

facts.label: Account eligibility
facts.value: Terms require age 13 or older and a valid reachable email; privacy also excludes people below the applicable age of consent.

facts.label: Buyer geography and payment detail
facts.value: Country eligibility, card-brand matrix, and non-card payment options were not established.

facts.label: Commercial use, Free and Pro
facts.value: Ordinary business-site, advertising, affiliate, and sales permissions are not clearly settled. Terms prohibit commercially exploiting the Website/Services; public docs promote production use and company organizations.

facts.label: Acceptable use
facts.value: Terms restrict illegal/infringing content, harmful material, spam, duplicate-content proliferation, and republishing removed projects. Infrastructure-provider AUPs also apply.

facts.label: Incorporated infrastructure policies
facts.value: DigitalOcean and Akamai AUPs restrict unlawful/harmful use, security abuse, and spam; Akamai also names pornography/obscene content.

facts.label: Incorporated Vultr policy
facts.value: Exact linked Vultr AUP content could not be verified: HTTP 403.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Managed static-file hosting on Surge's own CDN; customer builds output locally or in external CI, then uploads it.

facts.label: Suitable app types and overlap
facts.value: Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript, documentation, asset hosting, and browser apps. No execution of application server code, functions, or databases.

facts.label: Delivery regions
facts.value: Both plans: San Francisco and New York, US; Toronto, Canada; London, UK; Amsterdam, Netherlands; Frankfurt, Germany; Bangalore, India; Singapore; Tokyo, Japan; Sydney, Australia.

facts.label: DNS routing and location choice
facts.value: Surge DNS/CNAME target geo.surge.world selects a nearby edge. An A record pins the hostname to one chosen edge address.

facts.label: Languages, runtime, and containers
facts.value: Host serves built static files; no server-side language/container runtime. Local CLI package requires Node >=18.13.

facts.label: Vite and static generators
facts.value: Vite output dist, static Astro output dist, and Eleventy output _site can be uploaded without a Surge runtime adapter.

facts.label: Client-side routing and missing pages
facts.value: A 200.html shell serves unmatched paths with HTTP 200 for browser routing; 404.html handles actual not-found responses.

facts.label: Cache-description conflict
facts.value: Platform overview says far-future caching; detailed CDN guide specifies Cache-Control public, max-age=0, must-revalidate with ETags.

facts.label: Deployment inputs
facts.value: Directory or single HTML file through CLI; authenticated tarball upload API; JavaScript SDK. CI can use the same output-upload flow.

facts.label: Private repository and CI workflow
facts.value: Source can stay private; CI checks it out/builds before invoking Surge with a scoped secret token. Official GitHub Actions guide supplies PR-preview and production-push steps.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled application jobs
facts.value: Not applicable to static delivery: no hosted long-running worker or scheduled application runtime. Scheduled CI can rebuild/publish output externally.

facts.label: HTTP, HTTPS, and CORS
facts.value: HTTP/HTTPS static delivery; project-wide CORS via a CORS file or platform setting, free on both plans.

facts.label: Application connections and private network
facts.value: Customer WebSocket server, arbitrary TCP/UDP listener, outbound app IP, and VNet-style runtime networking are not applicable to this static-only host.

facts.label: Persistent deployed files
facts.value: Each revision stores an immutable project snapshot; production points to one. Last 100 revisions/domain retained as newer revisions arrive.

facts.label: Runtime writes and attached volumes
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted app process writes to a persistent filesystem or attached volume.

facts.label: Database, cache, queue, and form dependencies
facts.value: No bundled application runtime/database. External APIs handle dynamic work; the migration guide explicitly excludes native function and form-handling execution.

facts.label: Hosted access gates
facts.value: Free private domains admit publishers/collaborators; Pro AUTH can restrict paths by verified identity or HTTP Basic credentials.

facts.label: Custom domains and DNS
facts.value: Free custom apex/subdomains on both plans. Use Surge nameservers, CNAME to geo.surge.world, or an edge A record.

facts.label: Certificates, HTTPS, and wildcard coverage
facts.value: Managed custom-domain certificates issue/renew automatically. Delegated domains get root-plus-subdomain wildcard coverage. New surge.sh names force HTTPS; existing domains may require explicit enforcement.

facts.label: User-supplied certificate entitlement
facts.value: API reference labels PUT /:domain/ssl custom PEM upload Pro only, although plan docs say Pro adds exactly AUTH and ROUTER.

facts.label: Preview and promotion workflow
facts.value: Every revision gets a preview URL; --preview avoids moving production. Cutover promotes the latest or specified revision without rebuild/upload.

facts.label: Rollback and failed release recovery
facts.value: Managed rollback/rollfore/cutover move the production pointer between retained revisions, including their file-based configuration.

facts.label: Analytics and deployment diagnostics
facts.value: CLI stats reports traffic, audience, bandwidth, and per-datacenter load. Debug exposes live manifest, revision/certificate state per edge, and cache purge.

facts.label: Analytics API window
facts.value: Authenticated analytics API returns the past 14 days, cached 15 minutes.

facts.label: Raw-log retention, export, and alerts
facts.value: A fixed raw usage-log retention duration, customer raw-log export, and alert SLA were not established.

facts.label: Account protection
facts.value: Optional passkeys or authenticator-based two-factor sign-in; recovery codes documented. Existing API tokens continue to work after MFA is enabled.

facts.label: CI secrets and token scope
facts.value: Domain-scoped account tokens can publish and run project commands, including revisions/config/stats/teardown. Without a domain scope, an account token has full account access.

facts.label: Team roles and important access scope
facts.value: Org members can publish all org domains and manage ordinary membership; admins protect privileged membership/org removal. Any member can transfer a domain to their own account.

facts.label: Free organization membership conflict
facts.value: Teams guide: 3 people per Free org. Orgs guide: 5 people, up to 3 Free orgs administered/account and 10 tokens/org.

facts.label: Protection files and browser-visible secrets
facts.value: AUTH/ROUTER/CORS control files are not served as ordinary assets. AUTH rules are versioned, and existing identity sessions can last 12 hours after access removal.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed hosting platform. The local client requires a Node/npm environment and network credentials; customer maintains their own build/client dependencies.

facts.label: Data location and processor terms
facts.value: No public service-specific single-country storage promise, DPA, or complete subprocessor/location matrix established.

facts.label: Data carried by deployment client
facts.value: Upload includes project files, credential, domain, file counts/size, parsed arguments, client version/time, and descriptive User-Agent; request source IP is visible.

facts.label: Independent backup scope
facts.value: An automatic daily off-site backup schedule, independent retention, or post-teardown restore promise was not established.

facts.label: Portability and migration path
facts.value: Retain source, build output, control files, and DNS settings; rebuild/upload static output elsewhere. Surge-specific AUTH/ROUTER/config behavior needs replacement.

facts.label: Account closure and remaining data
facts.value: Account deletion removes account, plan, and account tokens after projects and sole-admin org duties are resolved. Privacy permits residual billing/abuse/log/support records and eventual stored-copy removal.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Surge, provided by Chloi Inc.; official CLI repository is sintaxi/surge.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Active, publicly documented signup; first CLI login creates an account if the email is new. Free and Pro are offered.

facts.label: Public status information
facts.value: Network page advertises live per-edge status and machine uptime, refreshed each minute; CLI audit checks project state per edge.

facts.label: Contractual availability
facts.value: No numeric public SLA/service-credit schedule established; terms disclaim uninterrupted or error-free service.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Public docs, support@surge.sh, linked Slack community, and official GitHub issues are available.

facts.label: Support response commitment
facts.value: Free/Pro hours, timezone, guaranteed first response, and incident escalation timetable were not established.

facts.label: Client software license
facts.value: Official README and package manifest identify ISC for the surge CLI. Hosted platform access remains subject to Surge's terms.
