facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Lighthouse runs the customer's server process, so the reviewed docs set no request-count fee, request duration or managed function timeout for HTTP requests.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Default account quota in the use-limit table is per region: up to 5 Razor Speed instances and 20 each for Starter and General. The FAQ separately says 10 instances per region.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: The current use-limit guide permits up to 10 SSH key pairs per region, 20 custom images per region and up to 100 firewall rules per instance.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Resource capacity is the purchased vCPU/RAM/disk/bandwidth package. Maximum HTTP request body, connections, app processes and per-request duration are not specified as managed Lighthouse limits.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: No Lighthouse-specific free trial amount or duration was found on the product, pricing, account-registration or help pages checked.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: International account setup supports email, Google or WeChat registration; account location must match an individual's country/region of residence or a company's country/region of establishment. It cannot be changed later.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Signup documentation ties the selected location to phone area code and identity checks. It lists major card types and says payment choices vary by country; it does not provide a complete, stable list of every country accepted for Lighthouse purchases.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: International terms prohibit users located, resident or organized in comprehensively sanctioned territories and restrict listed persons. Territories named include Iran, Cuba, North Korea, Syria, Crimea/Sevastopol and the so-called Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Tencent's general international terms allow the paid Services subject to applicable terms and law; the Acceptable Use Policy prohibits illegal or harmful content, spam, rights violations and abusive or security-breaching use.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Examples of restricted use include unsolicited spam, fraud, infringement, unauthorized network/security activity and content unlawful under applicable rules; Tencent may suspend or terminate service for violations.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Managed cloud VPS: Tencent provides the virtual machine, system disk, public networking, image catalog and console; the customer administers the guest OS, software, app, updates and app data.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Bundles combine vCPU, memory, SSD system disk, public bandwidth and monthly traffic quota. Application images add preconfigured software; Tencent says the customer manages software installed separately.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Lighthouse simplifies CVM's networking and resource controls. The private VPC is assigned automatically and cannot be chosen by the user; the bundle can be upgraded but not downgraded.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Official scenarios include small business and personal sites, blogs, forums, e-commerce, web apps, storage/image hosting, development/test and learning environments. Arbitrary software can be installed with server administration.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Workload A can be served from the VM with a self-managed web server. Lighthouse does not include a managed static-site build/deploy pipeline or edge delivery plan.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Workloads B and C can run custom server code, subject to selected resources and server administration. The database may be self-managed or an external/managed TencentDB service; it is not bundled with the Lighthouse VM.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Region guide lists Hong Kong, Singapore, Tokyo, Jakarta, Seoul, Bangkok, Silicon Valley, Frankfurt, Virginia, São Paulo and Johor Bahru. Region is selected at creation and cannot later be changed.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: USD base-plan prices are grouped for Singapore, Tokyo, Silicon Valley, Frankfurt, Jakarta, Seoul, Virginia, São Paulo and Johor Bahru. Hong Kong (China) has its own price table. Razor Speed bundles are unavailable in Johor Bahru.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Region count is conflicting: global product page says nine worldwide regions; current region guide lists 11; current pricing page lists Hong Kong plus nine outside-China regions and omits Bangkok and Toronto.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Official FAQ lists CentOS, Ubuntu and Windows Server, with application images including LAMP, WordPress, ASP.NET, Node.js and BT-Panel. User can install additional software.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Docker CE is available as an application image; Linux and Windows can be administered through SSH and RDP respectively. Container workloads use VM resources.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Current supported version matrix for language runtimes and CPU architecture were not stated in the product FAQ, images guide, overview or pricing table checked.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Windows application images use Windows Server/ASP.NET; those bundles have their own higher USD price schedule.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Lighthouse does not publish a managed framework adapter matrix for Next.js, Django, Rails, Laravel or other frameworks. Frameworks run as software the customer installs on the VM.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Product docs name LAMP, Node.js, WordPress and ASP.NET images, but do not promise framework/version-specific support or managed updates.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Create an instance through the Tencent Cloud console/API, select an OS or app image, then move code with SSH/SCP or install/build from source on the VM.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Docker image option is supplied as a VM application image; Docker Compose and other deployment tools can be installed and run by the customer.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Private Git repository deployment permissions, automatic pull-on-push and build hooks are not documented Lighthouse features.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Background processes and worker services can be run as OS-managed processes or containers on the VM; the customer handles supervision, updates and restarts.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: OS schedulers such as cron can be installed for recurring jobs; Lighthouse publishes no managed cron service or separate schedule quota.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: A maximum worker duration or Lighthouse-specific process count limit was not found in the use-limits, FAQ, billing or image docs checked.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Public IP networking is included with the VM. Inbound and outbound public connections can use ports allowed by the instance firewall and provider network policy.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Same-region Lighthouse instances in the same account communicate privately by default; cross-region Lighthouse communication requires CCN, and other Tencent products are not generally privately linked by default.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Lighthouse instances do not support IPv6. Public or private IP cannot be changed after creation and an Elastic IP cannot be bound later.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: TCP port 25 is blocked by default and cannot be unblocked for Lighthouse. The FAQ also warns that ISPs can block other risky ports.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: The instance firewall supports user-managed ingress/egress rules; current use-limit table allows up to 100 firewall rules per instance.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Network connection timeout, maximum concurrent sockets and WebSocket-specific provider caps were not published in the FAQ, region guide, pricing or use-limit pages checked.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: The OS and application use the bundle's persistent SSD system disk; additional data disks can be attached as separately billed CBS.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Stopping and restarting an instance keeps the disk; expiration and release follow the documented suspension/retention process.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: No shared multi-instance persistent filesystem is included in the Lighthouse bundle. CFS is a distinct Tencent service and private connectivity to it is not enabled by default.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Lighthouse does not include a managed PostgreSQL database. LighthouseDB is a separate service; Lighthouse-to-LighthouseDB private connectivity is supported in the documented cases.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Self-managed PostgreSQL, Redis, queue or auth software can be installed where compatible with the VM. Tencent's image catalog also has preconfigured open-source applications; the builder manages the installed stack.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: COS, Cloud Monitor, SSL Certificates, CBS, CCN and managed database products are distinct Tencent products or add-ons, not Lighthouse bundle entitlements.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Custom domains can point to the public IP; the overview says customers register a domain and configure DNS. Domain registration is separate.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Tencent documents an online free certificate flow for eligible non-mainland Lighthouse regions and selected application images, including WordPress, WooCommerce, Cloudreve, Typecho, Matomo and LAMP; custom certificates are also supported.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: DNS records, custom-domain binding and web-server HTTPS setup are customer configuration. No wildcard certificate inclusion or automatic issuance/renewal guarantee for every arbitrary workload was established.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: App traffic can use HTTPS when the customer configures a certificate and web server; this is not a managed edge TLS termination service included with every VM.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Lighthouse creates and manages the VM, but does not provide pull-request preview environments, application release health checks or managed rolling deployments in the reviewed guides.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Users can create a new instance or image and manually switch DNS or configuration for a release; no platform-managed one-click app rollback was documented.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Snapshots can restore the system disk. Restore replaces the disk state and may not preserve application memory/cache; it is not a database transaction rollback.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Console charts include CPU, memory, private/public network bandwidth and system/data disk use. Cloud Monitor can alert through WeChat, email, SMS or phone.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: OS/app/build logs are generated and managed inside the VM by the customer. No Lighthouse application-log retention, export or ingestion allowance is stated in the reviewed Lighthouse monitoring docs.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Tencent CloudAudit can show Lighthouse control-plane operations. It is distinct from application request logs and customer OS logs.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Tencent Cloud accounts support login/operation protection; Cloud Access Management (CAM) provides resource-level authorization for Lighthouse actions.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Linux servers are accessed using SSH; Windows servers use RDP. The customer controls OS-level users, SSH keys, application credentials and guest security configuration.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Up to 10 SSH key pairs per region are listed in the current usage limits; instance firewall supports up to 100 rules.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Account-level role/secret storage limits and a Lighthouse-native application secret manager were not found in the account, Lighthouse or CAM pages checked.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Not applicable: Lighthouse is a provider-hosted VM service, not a self-hosted control panel or deployment tool. Customer still manages the guest OS and app stack.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The region guide says regions are isolated and lets the user choose a compute region, but the reviewed privacy/DPA pages do not promise that all app data, support records, logs, backups or account metadata stay in that region.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The Lighthouse privacy module lists configuration, account identifiers, usage/diagnostic data, monitoring and access/error logs; some diagnostics may be kept for months and account/network records follow separate retention periods.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: Lighthouse has a product-specific data processing/security module. It applies to the service; it does not by itself provide a blanket local-residency guarantee for all VM contents.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Manual system-disk snapshots are available. Current snapshot guide says free quota is two times the number of created instances per region, capped at 20; pending-repossession instances and storage-optimized packages are excluded from that count.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Older use-limits page says free snapshots can be up to ten times the number of instances with a cap of ten, conflicting with the newer snapshot guide's two-times/cap-twenty rule.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Snapshots are manual; snapshot retention/deletion is customer-managed. Restoring replaces the system disk and snapshot coverage is not a guaranteed application-consistent database backup.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Lighthouse-specific price for snapshot storage above the free snapshot allowance was not found. Generic CBS snapshot-storage rates exist, but the pages checked do not settle the exact Lighthouse billing method and size accounting.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: The server is a standard Linux or Windows VM; customers can copy source files, database dumps and uploads out using OS tools, then repoint DNS to another provider.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Lighthouse offers image export/custom images and disk snapshots, but no universal one-click export of a running VM into another cloud's native image format was established.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Domain registration is external to Lighthouse, so the owner can leave the VM provider while keeping the domain and changing DNS records.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: After expiry, service suspension occurs around 48 hours later; data is retained for 15 days in the pending-repossession state, then released and cleared if not renewed.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Tencent Cloud Lighthouse; official offer https://www.tencentcloud.com/products/lighthouse; owned and operated as a Tencent Cloud product. No former product name found in the current official pages checked.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: The international terms assign the contracting entity by buyer region: Tencent Cloud Europe B.V. for EEA/UK/Switzerland; Tencent Cloud LLC for North America; Tencent Korea Yuhan Hoesa for South Korea; Tencent Cloud International Pte. Ltd. for other listed locations.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Public international product and current USD bundle schedule are available. Individual and enterprise account registration are documented; no signup or regional purchase flow was completed.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: No whole-product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice was found in the official Tencent newsroom, Tencent Cloud Techpedia/blog item checked, product notices and product documentation.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Tencent stopped selling the old General and Enterprise instance bundles on 2024-03-29. Existing bundles could be renewed at original price; current omitted bundles are no longer purchasable.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: The official status page is https://status.tencentcloud.com/ . No Lighthouse-specific public uptime SLA, service-credit rule or eligibility class was found in the service agreement, general SLA index and Lighthouse agreement pages checked.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: The current official status page provides incident/status information; historical uptime was not calculated for Lighthouse in this record.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: General SLA documentation was checked, but it does not establish an explicit Lighthouse uptime percentage or credit rule in the Lighthouse pages reviewed.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Documentation, ticket submission and Tencent Cloud support plans are published. The Basic support level is free and lists 24/7 ticket support for general questions with a response target under 16 hours.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Customers can submit support tickets and use the contact channels listed for their region; paid support plans may provide faster response targets.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: The reviewed general terms do not require Tencent to provide technical support unless a support service is purchased.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: Lighthouse is a proprietary hosted service. No separate Lighthouse server-software license or customer-paid license for Linux bundles was listed in the Lighthouse pricing page.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: Windows bundles use Windows Server images and carry higher published bundle prices; the Lighthouse rate table does not break out a separate Windows license fee.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Pay-as-you-go usage settles hourly. If a cycle's charge is below USD 0.01, no hourly bill/deduction is generated; the charge carries into a monthly bill adjustment.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Service fees exclude applicable taxes. General terms provide no general refund entitlement except where an applicable agreement or law provides one.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Packages are prepaid and scoped to a selected region or namespace. Excess usage falls through to pay-as-you-go; refunds and in-term changes use the package's stated proportional rules.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: CPU allocation follows configured memory. Published examples: 256 MB → 0.2 core; 1024 MB → 0.8 core; 1280 MB → 1 core of accounting power; 3072 MB → 2 cores.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Default runtime quota: 64–3072 MB memory; increments of 128 MB from 128 MB. Temporary /tmp storage: 512 MB. Compute-power guide separately permits up to 122880 MB (120 GB); allocations at least 6 GB require a large-specification application.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: CPU functions, international USD table, including Singapore: resource usage USD 0.0000167/GB-second; event or HTTP invocations USD 0.002/10000; idle provisioned concurrency USD 0.00000847/GB-second.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Resource usage = configured memory in MB / 1024 × actual execution milliseconds / 1000. Execution duration is metered in milliseconds and aggregated hourly; failed executions that run code can be charged.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: The billing overview quotes mainland outbound at USD 0.12/GB; the detailed regional table says USD 0.1203/GB. It introduces the basic package as USD 1.86/month but later specifies USD 0.06/day with a 31-day May example.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: No ongoing free execution tier after the first three activation months: the basic package is paid. Its monthly quotas are 100000 GB-seconds, 500000 event invocations, 500000 HTTP invocations and 2 GB public outbound.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: The product page still describes a monthly free tier, while the specific purchase guide limits it to the first three calendar months and explicitly says there is no free tier afterward.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Public outbound and HTTP response outbound: Singapore, Jakarta, Seoul, Tokyo, Frankfurt and mainland China excluding Hong Kong/Macao/Taiwan USD 0.1203/GB; Hong Kong USD 0.1504/GB; Bangkok, Silicon Valley and Virginia USD 0.0752/GB.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: HTTP response traffic is excluded from both the trial/basic public-outbound allowance. Public outbound initiated by the function and response outbound are separate billing categories.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Inbound transfer received by the function is not charged as public outbound. Same-VPC access to a database does not generate SCF public-network outbound usage.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Builder supplies deployable code or image. The Next.js guide requires building locally before deployment; it documents template, folder and repository paths. No included SCF-hosted build-minute pool is established.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: Code plus bound layers: at most 500 MB uncompressed per function version. Image guide: image below 1 GiB, same-region private TCR repository; supported Docker/OCI formats and x86 architecture.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: CFS, COS and CLS are billed separately under their own pricing. HTTP through a standard API Gateway can add gateway request/response charges; native Function URL provides a direct HTTP(S) path.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: CLS feature-based prices for Singapore, USD: log write 0.032/GB; standard index 0.066/GB; standard log and index storage each 0.00243/GB/day; requests 0.028/million. Other CLS operations have separate meters.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Billing budgets support cost thresholds and notifications. They are alerts; an enforceable account-wide dollar cap or guaranteed automatic stop at the chosen budget was not established.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Per-function reserved concurrency can impose an upper bound; zero prevents invocation. Limits are expressed as concurrent configured memory and shared across versions.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: On arrears, the payment-overdue guide describes a 24-hour grace period, then suspended function execution, reclaimed provisioned concurrency and stopped timer triggers. Payment can resume service.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: On-demand instances start for invocations and are reused/reclaimed by the platform; no provisioned instance minimum is selected in the examples. Provisioned concurrency keeps instances ready and has a separate idle GB-second charge.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Regional default concurrency is measured in aggregate configured MB, not as a fixed number of requests. Function reservations and purchased packages change capacity; over-limit requests can be rejected.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Default limits: execution timeout 1–900 seconds, synchronous event request 6 MB and response 6 MB, asynchronous event 128 KB; 1024 file descriptors and 1024 processes/threads.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: Per region: 100 GB function code and five namespaces; per namespace: 50 functions; per function: 1000 versions, ten triggers of the same type, 4 KB environment variables and five bound layer versions.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Trial allowance in each of the first three calendar months, including activation month: 1000000 GB-seconds, 1000000 event calls plus 1000000 HTTP calls and 2 GB public outbound. Resets monthly, no accumulation.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: International signup guide requires binding a supported credit/debit/prepaid card after registration; lists Visa, Mastercard, American Express, UnionPay, JCB, Discover and Diners Club with brand-specific acceptance. USD 1 authorization is cancelled in 1–5 business days.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: SCF's web-function guide requires completed identity verification. Individual verification accepts specified government documents issued by the account's country; Chinese Resident Identity Card-only users are directed to the mainland service.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: International account limits: one root account/email, up to five accounts/phone, up to three verified individual accounts per identity and ten enterprise accounts per organization. Mainland-registered companies are directed to the mainland site.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Terms section 12 excludes restricted persons and entities operating, organized or resident in comprehensively sanctioned territories listed in the terms: Iran, Cuba, North Korea, Syria, Crimea/Sevastopol and the so-called Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics. It also addresses aggregate ownership/control of at least 50% by restricted persons.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Ordinary business applications are within the service terms; integrated applications may be offered to customers, subject to restrictions on resale of the services themselves. No separate hobby/noncommercial-only SCF plan is stated.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: AUP prohibits illegal/harmful content, fraud, unsolicited abusive messaging, malware and unauthorized security attacks; general terms also restrict high-risk uses and applicable trade-law violations.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: For a Service Region that includes the United States, the terms prohibit processing/storing data subject to ITAR or HIPAA under the stated service agreement.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Fully hosted function-as-a-service: Tencent manages execution infrastructure and scaling; the builder supplies code, dependencies, permissions, triggers and configuration. Event functions and HTTP/Web functions are distinct invocation models.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Suitable for event handlers, API endpoints, scheduled tasks and HTTP applications. Native Function URLs can invoke event and Web functions directly.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Static files can be served by an application HTTP server, but SCF is not an included CDN/static-object delivery plan. Image functions must start an HTTP server listening on port 9000.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: SCF API region list includes Guangzhou, Shanghai, Nanjing, Beijing, Chengdu, Chongqing, Hong Kong, Singapore, Jakarta, Bangkok, Seoul, Tokyo, Virginia, Silicon Valley, São Paulo and Frankfurt; finance endpoints are separate.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Examples select Singapore, region code ap-singapore. Function URLs and custom-domain mappings are regional; a CDN is not automatically added to a direct function endpoint.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Node.js runtime guide lists 20.19, 18.15, 16.13, 14.18, 12.16, 10.15, 8.9 and 6.10; Python guide lists 3.10, 3.9, 3.7, 3.6 and 2.7. Older listed versions are not proof of upstream support.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: Go development uses compiled binaries; additional languages/frameworks can use container images. Image functions run on x86; ARM-built images are not supported by the checked image guide.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Official Next.js guide deploys a local SSR project as an HTTP-triggered function. Template and existing-project paths are documented; server starts via the supplied bootstrap configuration.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: Feature-level Next.js version/adapter compatibility, streaming and ISR/cache invalidation guarantees were not established in the checked Next.js, Web function and image guides.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Console supports templates, new code, code packages and TCR images; Function URL can be configured through console or SCF API/CLI. Direct function deployment is distinct from the Application Console.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Timer triggers asynchronously invoke a function on a cron schedule, including second-level fields in the recommended seven-field expression. Execution is subject to the function's configured timeout.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: After the entry function returns or throws, that invocation ends. Work that must outlive the HTTP response should use a separate invocation/queue workflow within documented runtime limits.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Job Image functions execute a configured command without an HTTP server or exposed port, receive event input through an environment variable, and release the instance after the process exits. Currently event functions only; invocation responds asynchronously.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Function URL supports HTTP(S), public or private endpoint forms, and WSS when WebSocket support is enabled in the function configuration.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Public-only, VPC-only, public plus VPC and fixed-public-egress configurations are documented. Private networking supports access to databases and Redis.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: The standard /tmp directory is temporary, 512 MB. Image writable layer is also limited to 512 MB; local instance files are not a durable upload store.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: CFS can be mounted for shared persistent files with the required same-region/VPC configuration. CFS is separately billed; COS is another separate object-storage dependency.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Managed supporting products include TencentDB for PostgreSQL, with separately selected instance/storage/backup billing. Function VPC configuration supports private database access.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: COS, CFS, CLS and event-source integrations are supporting products with independent charges and policies; queues/event streams are integrations rather than an included SCF database or auth allowance.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Native Function URL supplies a stable HTTPS endpoint per enabled version/alias, disabled by default. Custom domains map paths to functions in the same region; wildcard domains are not supported.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: For custom-domain HTTPS, select a matching certificate in Tencent Cloud SSL service; the guide permits uploading an existing certificate or purchasing one. Forced HTTPS uses a 301 redirect.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Lowest current plan: Starter 1 CPU core, 1 GB memory, 10 GB Standard storage, 250 Mbit/s listed bandwidth, and one public IPv4 for €3/month global price, EUR, before local taxes.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Starter and Premium are charged hourly from the start of each billed hour, capped at 672 hours (28 days) per calendar month. The monthly cap makes the monthly plan total stable across month lengths.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Current EUR Global-price examples: Starter 1 CPU/4 GB/30 GB is €10/month; Premium 1 CPU/1 GB/25 GB is €5/month; Cloud Native 1 CPU/4 GB is €12/month before tax. Cloud Native storage and IP are extra.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: The November 16, 2026 schedule lists a previous General Purpose 1 CPU/1 GB/25 GB configuration at $7.10/month Global and $9.80/month Helsinki, USD, before applicable tax. It applies to the discontinued plan family, not a new Starter server.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Prices exclude VAT and other applicable local taxes. UpCloud lists EUR and USD prices on the public pricing page and accepts EUR, USD, GBP, and SGD payments; non-EUR payments are converted to EUR using the day’s exchange rate.

facts.label: Entry cost and billing terms
facts.value: Payment timing is unclear for a new account: the current Terms describe post-pay as the default for new customers after launch, while current billing and account-balance help pages describe hourly charges deducted from prepaid account balance.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Current Starter plans range from 1 to 4 CPU cores, 1 to 16 GB RAM, and 10 to 50 GB Standard block storage. The smallest plan includes 10 GB.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Premium plans range from 1 to 80 CPU cores, 1 to 512 GB RAM, and 25 to 500 GB MaxIOPS storage. Current published plans include Balanced, High CPU, and High Memory variants.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: Cloud Native plans range from 1 to 80 CPU cores and 4 to 512 GB RAM. They do not bundle block storage or a public IPv4; the customer adds those separately.

facts.label: Included compute and storage
facts.value: The current price page names AMD CPU generations for the current plan families, but the plan specifications do not establish a per-plan shared versus dedicated CPU allocation guarantee.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Cloud Servers are metered by the hour, with a 672-hour monthly cap for the current plans. There is no separate per-request or CPU-time charge for a normal always-on VM.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Starter and Premium server plan charges continue while a server is shut down. Cloud Native compute charges apply only while the server is powered on.

facts.label: Usage billing units and rates
facts.value: Starter 1 CPU/1 GB includes 0.5 TB of monthly public egress under the Fair Transfer Limit. Ingress and private-network traffic are included. At the limit, UpCloud warns the customer and may throttle bandwidth to 100 Mbit/s; it does not charge an excess-GB fee under this policy.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: No ongoing free Cloud Server plan is published. UpCloud offers a temporary 7-day trial; the Essentials complimentary tier covers selected other services/features, not free Cloud Server compute.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Public ingress and private transfer are included. Public egress is included within a plan-specific global fair-transfer quota; Starter 1 CPU/1 GB is 0.5 TB, Starter 1 CPU/4 GB is 1 TB.

facts.label: Data transfer and network costs
facts.value: Exceeding the Fair Transfer Limit triggers a warning and may reduce Cloud Server bandwidth to 100 Mbit/s for the remainder of the month. No excess-GB fee is listed under the standard fair-transfer model. An optional paid transfer model is described for unlimited transfer without bandwidth restriction.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: No managed build minutes, Git deployment pipeline, or preview-build allowance is documented for Cloud Servers. Source builds can be run by the customer on the VM or on separately billed CI/build infrastructure.

facts.label: Build and deployment costs/limits
facts.value: For a build run on the VM, the server continues to incur its normal plan charge while it is running; build minutes do not create a second Cloud Server usage meter.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Starter and Premium include one public IPv4 and IPv6; Cloud Native requires public IP and storage add-ons as needed. Additional public IPv4 and Floating IP are each listed at €3.47/month global price, EUR, before local tax.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Global EUR block-storage prices are MaxIOPS €0.220/GB/month, Standard €0.085/GB/month, and Archive €0.056/GB/month. Helsinki Archive storage is €0.100/GB/month; the other two listed Helsinki rates are €0.220 and €0.085/GB/month. Prices exclude tax.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Simple Backup on an included server disk costs +10% of plan price for one daily backup, +20% for seven daily backups, +40% for four weekly plus seven daily backups, or +60% for year retention, global EUR percentage pricing before tax.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: Windows Server licenses are billed per CPU core. Current listed prices are €12.00/month per core for Standard and €29.02/month per core for Datacenter, global EUR, before tax. The November 16 notice publishes replacement USD pricing for older licenses.

facts.label: Other unavoidable or easy-to-miss charges
facts.value: UpCloud firewall, SDN private networks, and IPv6 are included at no additional charge. Managed databases, external domain registration, and third-party application services are separate.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: Documentation describes a prepaid balance, low-balance email notices, optional automated top-ups, and server shutdown when credits run out. Storage, IPs, and backups can keep charging while a server is shut down, and balances may go negative.

facts.label: Protection against a surprise bill
facts.value: The new-customer post-pay rule in the Terms conflicts with help/pricing pages describing prepaid credits. The documentation does not establish a firm spend cap for an account on the post-pay model.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Cloud Servers do not auto-sleep as an app host. Starter/Premium keep billing while powered off; Cloud Native stops compute billing when powered off.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: CPU and RAM can be scaled up without downtime on compatible servers. Scaling down requires a shutdown; storage does not automatically shrink.

facts.label: Scaling, sleeping, and idle billing
facts.value: Horizontal scaling requires customer configuration or a separate orchestration service; the separate Managed Kubernetes service offers node autoscaling.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: The smallest current Starter plan permits up to five concurrent deployments per customer. The general product does not set a managed HTTP request duration or concurrency cap; request capacity depends on server and application resources.

facts.label: Runtime and request limits
facts.value: A Cloud Server can attach up to 16 concurrent storage devices, for a maximum total of 64 TB. The public price page says a volume can be up to 4 TB.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: New users can start a 7-day free trial after account creation and identity verification. It includes up to 2 CPU cores and 4 GB RAM for Cloud Servers, up to 180 GB total across the listed storage tiers, and excludes Windows servers.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: Starting the trial requires name, email, phone, billing address, and a credit card. A temporary 0 or 1 EUR/USD card authorization may be used for verification; the card is not charged for the trial.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The trial must be activated within 365 days of account creation. At expiration, trial resources are deleted unless the user upgrades by making a one-time deposit of at least 10 in the chosen currency. First payment has a 30-day money-back guarantee up to €500/$500.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The exact promotional free-credit amount is not published as a stable public value; UpCloud says the offer changes and directs visitors to the signup page for the current offer.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: UpCloud says it will not provide service to sanctioned-listed people or entities, people or entities in sanctioned regions, or payments from financial institutions in sanctioned regions. The account help page names Russia, Belarus, Crimea, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, and Syria, and says the list is not exhaustive.

facts.label: Trial and buyer requirements
facts.value: The Terms say the service is for business and professional use by entities, organisations, and private entrepreneurs; it is not intended for consumers or private persons using it personally.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: The Terms allow customers to use Cloud Servers to provide their own services to end customers, with the customer responsible for those users and their content.

facts.label: Commercial and acceptable use
facts.value: Prohibited or restricted use includes illegal/harmful content, misuse of others’ rights, spam, unlicensed software, sustained excessive load, unsafe configuration, and cryptocurrency mining without prior written approval. Bulk email requires prior approval.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Infrastructure as a service: UpCloud operates the physical cloud infrastructure; the customer deploys a VM and manages its operating system, application, updates, application security, and data. UpCloud says it does not manage customer software.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Linux and Windows servers can be reached using SSH, VNC/web console, or Remote Desktop, depending on the selected operating system. Linux users can add SSH public keys during deployment.

facts.label: Hosting and management model
facts.value: Managed Databases, Managed Kubernetes, Load Balancer, File Storage, Object Storage, and Simple Backup are separate UpCloud products or features with their own service scope and charges.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: A customer can install and run static websites, web apps, APIs, databases, long-lived processes, and containers on a supported OS, subject to its server resources and the AUP.

facts.label: Suitable app types and directory overlap
facts.value: Related directory categories include virtual servers, container tooling installed on a server, managed databases, object/file storage, DNS/domain providers, and managed load balancing.

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: UpCloud lists 15 server locations: Amsterdam (NL-AMS1), Copenhagen (DK-CPH1), Frankfurt (DE-FRA1), Helsinki (FI-HEL1 and FI-HEL2), London (UK-LON1), Madrid (ES-MAD1), Stavanger (NO-SVG1), Stockholm (SE-STO1), Warsaw (PL-WAW1), Chicago (US-CHI1), New York (US-NYC1), San Jose (US-SJO1), Singapore (SG-SIN1), and Sydney (AU-SYD1).

facts.label: App server and delivery regions
facts.value: Cloud Servers do not provide an app edge-delivery network as part of the VM plan. The separate CDN product and its pricing/location model are not included in the Cloud Server examples.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: UpCloud provides Linux distribution and Windows Server templates; custom installation media and custom server images are supported. A user can install language runtimes or a container engine within the VM.

facts.label: Languages, runtimes, and architecture
facts.value: A complete current CPU architecture matrix (including any ARM availability by plan and region) was not found in the plan specifications.

facts.label: Framework behavior
facts.value: No managed framework adapter, automatic server-rendering path, or framework-specific cache/revalidation guarantee is documented for Cloud Servers. Framework behavior depends on the OS and software installed by the customer.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: Deployment inputs include a public OS template, user-created image, custom installation media, first-boot initialization script, or API-created server.

facts.label: Deployment inputs and tools
facts.value: UpCloud offers a web control panel, REST API, upctl CLI, and infrastructure-as-code tooling including Terraform and Pulumi. No managed Git provider-to-app deployment connection is listed.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Long-running background workers and cron jobs can be installed and managed by the customer inside a VM. There is no Cloud Server plan-level managed worker or scheduled-job add-on documented.

facts.label: Workers and scheduled jobs
facts.value: Cloud Server workloads can continue running while the server is powered on; plan billing is not tied to an HTTP request duration.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Public IPv4 and IPv6 are included in Starter/Premium plans; private networking is available. Cloud Server firewall supports configurable inbound/outbound rules and supports both IPv4 and IPv6 on public/utility networks.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Trial firewalls are locked to a limited port set. Outbound SMTP port 25 is blocked on all new accounts by default; paid customers can request an unblock after identity/payment checks and a use-case review.

facts.label: Network and connection support
facts.value: Additional public IPv4 addresses and floating IPs are billed separately; UpCloud lists up to five concurrent IPv4 addresses per Cloud Server.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Cloud Server plan disks use persistent block storage. Starter includes Standard storage; Premium includes MaxIOPS; Cloud Native requires a separately selected disk.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Cloud Server data is permanently deleted when the server and associated resources are deleted. A stopped VM is not an application backup.

facts.label: Persistent app files
facts.value: Storage devices can be enlarged, but cannot be automatically shrunk. A smaller plan may leave a disk billed as extra until the customer copies data to a new smaller disk and deletes the old one.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Customers can self-manage databases on their VM. UpCloud also sells separate Managed Databases for MySQL/PostgreSQL and other database engines; those plans and bills are outside Cloud Servers.

facts.label: Databases and supporting services
facts.value: Load balancers, gateways, File Storage, Object Storage, managed database services, and CDN are separate products, not resources included in the bare VM price.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: Cloud Servers provide a network endpoint; custom domain DNS, web-server routing, and HTTPS certificate installation are customer-managed. No managed domain attachment or certificate renewal is listed as part of the Cloud Server plan.

facts.label: Domains and encrypted connections
facts.value: The Cloud Server price does not specify a count of managed custom domains, automatic TLS issuance, or wildcard certificate handling for applications.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: No managed preview environment, app deployment health check, or application rollback feature is documented for Cloud Servers. Customers provide CI/CD and release controls.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Server images can be used to create similar new servers. Backups can restore a whole storage device or be cloned to a new disk for file recovery.

facts.label: Preview, release, and recovery workflow
facts.value: Infrastructure image or disk rollback does not restore an external or separately managed database to a matching point in time unless that database is part of the backed-up storage.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Cloud Server CPU/disk statistics are available through the API, and network-transfer statistics are visible in the control panel. Transfer statistics are retained for one year.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Account audit logs provide the latest 180 days in the control panel at no extra cost; UpCloud says longer access up to five years is available through Sales.

facts.label: Logs and basic monitoring
facts.value: Application and build logs live in the customer’s VM or their chosen logging system. UpCloud does not document a Cloud Server managed app-log store or a retention period.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: Linux servers can use SSH keys; Windows uses a generated Administrator password. UpCloud supports subaccounts with resource-level permissions and separate API tokens.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: API tokens can expire, be restricted to IP ranges, and be revoked. UpCloud recommends separate tokens for integrations and supports two-factor authentication with API token workflows.

facts.label: Access and secret handling
facts.value: A managed application-secret store for processes inside Cloud Servers is not documented as a Cloud Server feature.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: Not applicable as a customer-hosted UpCloud control plane: UpCloud manages the infrastructure service. Inside the VM, the customer operates the OS, software, firewall rules, updates, app monitoring, and backups.

facts.label: Self-host requirements and ongoing work
facts.value: No separate customer control-plane machine or minimum local hardware requirement is needed to use the hosted service; API, CLI, and Terraform/Pulumi tools run in the customer’s environment.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: The Terms say the customer selects the data center for Customer Data and UpCloud will not transfer Customer Data away from it without the customer’s explicit request. Backups are stored in the same data center as their source server.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: Current DPA lists UpCloud Oy as operating the EU data centers and identifies wholly owned subsidiaries involved for Singapore, UK, US, and Australia deployments.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: A complete location guarantee for account metadata, support communications, platform telemetry, and all logs was not established.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Simple Backup supports daily for one day (+10%), daily for seven days (+20%), weekly for four weeks plus daily for seven days (+40%), or monthly for twelve months plus weekly and daily copies (+60%). For an included VM disk, pricing is a percentage of the server plan price.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Backup schedules are per server; Simple, Flexible, and manual on-demand backups are supported. Backups are stored in the source server’s data center; offsite copy requires the customer to clone or export them.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: If a Simple Backup plan is disabled or the server is deleted, existing backups convert to on-demand backups and remain until the user deletes them; they can continue to bill.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: A full restore overwrites the disk and requires the server to be shut down. Alternatively, clone a backup to new storage to recover files; there is no automatic single-file restore.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Customer retains ownership of Customer Data; Terms say UpCloud deletes data within a reasonable time after termination or when service use ends, except where law requires retention. Customers are responsible for backups.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Custom images, API, SSH, and storage-copy workflows support customer-led moves. A complete one-click cross-provider export for account settings, networks, servers, data, and backups is not documented.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Current product name: UpCloud Cloud Servers, a public cloud virtual server product. No product-level former name or rename found.

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Contracting operator is UpCloud Oy, a Finnish limited liability company based in Helsinki, Finland. UpCloud Oy is identified as the parent of its operating affiliates.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Cloud Servers are active and offered to new customers through current Starter, Premium and Cloud Native plans. The current pricing page lists these plans and a signup path.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: Developer, General Purpose and Flexible plan families are discontinued for new deployments. The Developer plan documentation says API deployments of those old Developer plans remain possible.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: UpCloud’s official Announcements blog and Media Center were checked. No acquisition or Cloud Servers shutdown announcement was found. The blog’s PwnEscape notice says UpCloud mitigated the Linux kernel vulnerability on October 21, 2026.

facts.label: Operating and signup status
facts.value: UpCloud’s pricing page announces changes to discontinued Cloud Server plans, Standard and Archive Block Storage, and Windows Server licenses effective November 16, 2026. The notice is separate from the current Starter/Premium/Cloud Native offer.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Current plan promises: Starter 99.99% SLA; Premium and Cloud Native 99.999% SLA. The written SLA excludes free trials, website, API, and control panel.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: For an unscheduled interruption longer than five minutes, the SLA provides credits equal to 50 times fees for the affected service-item interruption, capped per event and in total; claim within 15 days after correction. Credits are not cash.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: The official status page showed all systems operational at check time. It also listed upcoming maintenance, including NL-AMS1 network work on November 11, 2026, with brief latency expected.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: UpCloud provides English-language 24/7/365 live chat and email support. The help page says support assists with infrastructure but does not manage or install customer software.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Paid support tiers list response targets for service requests of under 4 hours (Essentials), under 1 hour (Advanced), and under 10 minutes (Enterprise); incident targets are under 2 hours, 30 minutes, and 5 minutes respectively.

facts.label: Support channels and terms
facts.value: Included support-plan price and guaranteed first response for every new Cloud Server account were not established from public plan pages.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: Not applicable as a self-hostable software license: Cloud Servers are a proprietary hosted infrastructure service. The customer must supply compliant licenses for installed third-party software.

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
facts.value: Windows Server licenses must be purchased through UpCloud for use on its servers, except that listed Microsoft License Mobility products may use the customer’s existing eligible license under the relevant agreement.

facts.value: Separate public DPA, contractual region residency and exact locations for code, database, objects, builds, logs and backups not found.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Non-static channels nightly DB/files snapshots: Starter/Basic 24 hours; all paid plans 7 days. Newest nightly retained regardless of age.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Snapshots may lack aligned file checkpoint; a database restore alone changes data, not code or necessarily matching objects.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: DB restore asynchronous: read-only default, maintenance 503 alternative or live mode discarding intervening writes at switch; up to an hour documented.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Exact backup region, comprehensive app/config recovery guarantee, numeric file-export thresholds and contractual recovery objective not published.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Source clone/download and channel/app export archives with database dump and Docker Compose/restore scripts; separate blob archive or generated sync script where too large.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Requested export archives retained 24 hours; API download token scoped to export. Export can omit files and require sync-blobs.sh.

facts.label: Exit and portability
facts.value: Closing account cancels subscription, deletes apps and revokes access at once; account/history/billing remain until erasure request; backup copies outlive deletion.

facts.label: Exit and portability

facts.label: Product identity and ownership
facts.value: Named legal operator/company, parent ownership, incorporation country and former names not published in checked product, terms, privacy and blog pages.

facts.label: Operating and signup status

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Availability, performance and data durability explicitly best effort, service as-is without warranty.

facts.label: Availability promise and status history
facts.value: Public dedicated status URL, timestamped incident history, uptime percentage and service-credit schedule not found.

facts.label: Support channels and terms

facts.label: Software license and commercial terms
