facts.label: Still-published subscription prices
facts.value: Free US$0/month; Dev US$5/month; Pro US$19/month; Team US$79/month with three seats plus US$24/month per extra seat; Enterprise custom.

facts.label: Seat and own-server allowances
facts.value: Personal Free/Dev/Pro can manage one/three/ten own servers respectively; Team has unlimited bound own servers and three included Pro-level seats.

facts.label: Renewal and cancellation
facts.value: Terms ordinarily renew at the current non-promotional rate; cancellation leaves current-term features until cycle end with no prorated subscription refund. Subscription docs say downgrading suspends containerized services.

facts.label: Currency and invoicing
facts.value: Card subscriptions/charges are USD; Alipay can fund credits in CNY. Invoice docs distinguish ordinary receipts from statutory invoices/fapiao, available on Team and above.

facts.label: Tax display treatment
facts.value: Invoices include taxes according to local regulation, but whether every displayed subscription/server price includes or excludes applicable tax was not established.

facts.label: Wind-down refunds
facts.value: Account-balance refund requests and incident compensation are separately accepted through Zeabur Support. Ordinary docs instead describe non-refundable prepaid credits and prorated eligible-server refunds as Zeabur Credits.

facts.label: Runtime resources on a server
facts.value: CPU, memory, local storage and network belong to the selected/owned server; the shared-cluster model used shared hardware. A subscription CI specification is not runtime capacity.

facts.label: Minimum bound-server hardware
facts.value: Registering an own server requires at least one CPU core and 2 GB memory, a reachable public address and privileged SSH access.

facts.label: Build resources by plan
facts.value: Free and Dev CI machines: 2 vCPU/4 GB; Pro and Team: 4 vCPU/8 GB. Builds run on separate shared CI infrastructure and the builder is released after image upload.

facts.label: Runtime storage and processor matrix
facts.value: Persistent volumes use the selected server/storage environment; a complete numerical per-plan runtime disk/CPU-architecture/exclusive-core matrix was not found in current pricing and deployment/server specs.

facts.label: Server and subscription meters
facts.value: Servers were billed at a fixed monthly plan price, independent of individual service resource consumption; subscriptions are separate monthly fees. Existing shared users continue usage billing.

facts.label: Legacy shared usage rates
facts.value: Shared-cluster docs identify CPU/memory/network usage meters, but a complete current numeric tariff and rounding/minimum policy were not established on the checked pricing, usage, subscription and terms pages.

facts.label: Existing-server renewal behavior
facts.value: Old purchase docs describe monthly automatic renewal, balance checks about every eight hours and provider-dependent expiry grace periods; the shutdown notice disables renewals from December 1.

facts.label: Free plan scope
facts.value: Free plan has no subscription charge, no credit-card requirement, one manageable own server, 2C4G CI and 48-hour log retention in the price table.

facts.label: Free idle policy
facts.value: Free-plan guide says idle services sleep and wake on the next request; it does not give the inactivity threshold or explain this policy separately for every dedicated/BYOH mode.

facts.label: Free operational exclusions
facts.value: Free guide excludes SLA, Zeabur Email and automatic database backup/import. Automated backup is documented from Dev upward; log-forwarding tier descriptions are inconsistent.

facts.label: Transfer billing by infrastructure
facts.value: Dedicated-server allowance/overage is part of its provider/server specification; own-server transfer remains with the outside host. Legacy shared model includes traffic usage billing.

facts.label: Private database connectivity
facts.value: Same-project services use a stable internal hostname such as postgresql.zeabur.internal and the injected database port.

facts.label: Exact transfer tariff and exemptions
facts.value: No universal current inbound/outbound allowance, overage rate or explicit price for the examples' 100-GB public/10-GB database traffic was established across managed servers and legacy shared clusters.

facts.label: Build pipeline and inputs
facts.value: Source builds use zbpack or a supplied Dockerfile on shared CI, then push an image to Zeabur's registry. CLI upload, Git and image-related deployment paths are documented.

facts.label: Build charges and quotas
facts.value: CI machine sizes are published, but a separate current build-minute rate, included minutes, concurrency/deployment-count cap and maximum build duration were not established.

facts.label: Image-registry shutdown dependency
facts.value: Zeabur build registries stop being available; image pulls can fail and a service that works now may fail only when restarted later.

facts.label: Charges beyond subscription
facts.value: Rented or external server, provider transfer, added disk, team seats, external logging and replacement/migration infrastructure can add costs beyond the dashboard plan.

facts.label: Documented backup inclusion
facts.value: Dev and above include off-site backups in Zeabur's S3 storage with no additional storage charge stated in the backup guide.

facts.label: Project budget stop
facts.value: Project budget is opt-in, minimum $10; notification at 80%, services in that project suspend at 100%; changes take effect immediately.

facts.label: Budget residual charges and timing
facts.value: Stop delay, measured overshoot, retained-data charges and interaction with prepaid dedicated-server/subscription renewal are not fully specified by the budget/pricing/server/terms pages.

facts.label: Vertical and horizontal scaling
facts.value: Service CPU/memory limits can be adjusted and apply on the next deployment. HA guide says automatic horizontal scaling is not supported; users manually duplicate services and configure balancing.

facts.label: Sleep and suspend charging scope
facts.value: Free guide describes inactivity sleep; manual suspension preserves config/volumes and stops the service process. Suspend docs broadly say charges stop, while rented-server docs use fixed monthly billing.

facts.label: Closure versus ordinary idle behavior
facts.value: From December 1, forced shared-cluster suspension is for wind-down/backup and is distinct from request-triggered Free sleep. Server shutdown follows expiry rather than an inactivity timer.

facts.label: File-management upload limits
facts.value: Single-file dashboard upload: Free 50 MB, Dev 250 MB, Pro/Team 1 GiB.

facts.label: Runtime/account ceilings
facts.value: A current complete matrix of app count, aggregate CPU/RAM, maximum request size/lifetime/concurrency and generic persistent-disk caps was not found across the checked pricing/server/build/network docs and terms.

facts.label: Trial and auto-billing
facts.value: One 14-day trial per user, choosing Dev or Pro with that plan's features/quotas; Team has no trial. Trial renews into the selected paid plan unless cancelled; ending early starts the paid cycle immediately.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Stripe-supported cards include Visa, Mastercard, Amex, JCB and UnionPay; Alipay funds Zeabur Credits and PayPal is explicitly unsupported.

facts.label: Buyer and identity restrictions
facts.value: Terms require accurate account information and lawful use/legal capacity; privacy policy says service is not intended for children under 13. No exhaustive accepted-country or documentary identity-check matrix found.

facts.label: Commercial-use conflict
facts.value: Fair-use policy permits commercial use on Developer/Team and restricts old Serverless plans to non-commercial use. Pro guide markets SaaS/e-commerce production use, while terms section 4 says service use is personal/internal/non-commercial.

facts.label: Acceptable-use restrictions
facts.value: Fair-use rules forbid VPN/proxy services, crypto mining, scraping/crawling, illegal activity, torrent aggregators and automated bots/scripts. Terms add intellectual-property, abuse, privacy and infrastructure restrictions.

facts.label: Server compliance inspections
facts.value: Terms allow necessary inspections of usage/configuration on dedicated servers purchased/hosted on a user's behalf and actions for prohibited usage, including suspension or reclamation.

facts.label: Hosting model — shared and rented servers
facts.value: Legacy shared Kubernetes clusters ran multiple users' workloads; dedicated Zeabur-supplied servers use fixed-monthly infrastructure with managed ZeaburOS/K3s deployment components.

facts.label: Hosting model — customer-owned hardware
facts.value: Users can bind their own machine for dashboard deployment, logs, variables, storage and networking; their server infrastructure remains independently owned/billed.

facts.label: Standard VPS versus ZeaburOS
facts.value: ZeaburOS is the renamed K3s-based managed deployment-node OS; a standard Ubuntu 24.04 LTS installation is self-managed and has no Zeabur project/observability interface.

facts.label: Suitable applications and overlap
facts.value: Static frontends, arbitrary compatible container web apps/APIs, continuous processes, databases and other templates; private connections allow frontend/backend/data services in a project.

facts.label: Static deployment model
facts.value: Node guide supports static output_dir deployment through a Caddy web server; custom Docker images also run serving processes.

facts.label: Server and cluster origins
facts.value: Historical managed-server docs list AWS, GCP, Hetzner, Linode, DigitalOcean, Aliyun, Tencent and Volcengine across Asia, Europe, the Americas and Oceania; own-server location follows the user's host.

facts.label: Legacy shared regions and delivery
facts.value: Status page lists shared-region entries for Taipei, Jakarta, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Frankfurt, California and Shanghai. These reflect existing components, not new shared deployment availability.

facts.label: Language/runtime routes
facts.value: Build docs list Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go, Java, .NET, Rust and Elixir; custom Dockerfiles/images permit additional compatible stacks.

facts.label: Node.js and PHP configuration
facts.value: Node guide defaults to latest LTS and supports engines-based selection and npm/Yarn/pnpm/Bun. PHP guide defaults to PHP 8 with NGINX/php-fpm and permits composer/zbpack version selection.

facts.label: Processor and OS compatibility
facts.value: The hosted architecture matrix is not fully established; ZeaburOS is K3s-based, standard VPS docs name Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. Separate OSS installer explicitly supports Linux amd64/arm64.

facts.label: Framework and static behavior
facts.value: Node guide lists Next.js, Remix, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro static/SSR and other frameworks; output_dir chooses Caddy static serving. Next.js guide describes importing the GitHub project.

facts.label: Advanced framework features
facts.value: A complete versioned guarantee for Next.js streaming/ISR, shared regeneration cache, edge middleware and other adapter-specific behavior was not found in framework, build, network, pricing or terms pages.

facts.label: Git and private-source deployment
facts.value: Authorize the Zeabur GitHub App for personal/organization repositories; pushes trigger CI/CD. Custom root directory and monorepo app_dir select the source subproject.

facts.label: Containers and direct uploads
facts.value: Custom Dockerfile or Docker/OCI image deployments, CLI-uploaded source, templates/deploy buttons and IDE/browser extensions are documented.

facts.label: Export and automation tools
facts.value: Project deployment configuration exports to YAML with image/source/variable/volume configuration; CLI can import a template. Export explicitly does not include actual persistent data.

facts.label: Continuous workers
facts.value: PHP guide explicitly documents separate queue/cron-worker services and custom startup commands for continuously running background tasks.

facts.label: Scheduled-job model
facts.value: Hosted PHP guide runs Laravel's scheduler as a service process. A universal hosted managed-cron frequency/duration/retry contract was not found in hosted deployment, framework, billing and terms docs.

facts.label: HTTP and non-HTTP public access
facts.value: Public HTTP uses generated/custom domains; non-HTTP services can use assigned hostname/port forwarding. Git-source services allow one exposed port, defined by Dockerfile or the injected PORT/default.

facts.label: Private service network
facts.value: Same-project services resolve internal hostnames and use injected service/database variables. Service-name changes do not change the documented private hostname.

facts.label: Firewall and fixed-address scope
facts.value: Server firewall guide allows inbound TCP/UDP/source rules where available; its scope is inbound, with outbound unrestricted by that firewall. Server IP/port infrastructure comes from the chosen host.

facts.label: WebSockets, streaming and request limits
facts.value: The WebSocket developer guide describes platform log/GraphQL subscriptions, not a universal customer-app proxy guarantee. Exact app WebSocket/SSE/gRPC behavior, body-size cap and connection lifetime were not established.

facts.label: Temporary versus persistent files
facts.value: Service-local data normally resets on restart; a mounted volume preserves its directory across restarts. Volumes are scoped to a single service and cannot be shared between services.

facts.label: Persistent volume deployment limit
facts.value: Services with volumes use Recreate: old container stops before replacement starts, causing downtime rather than the ordinary stateless rolling-switch behavior.

facts.label: Server storage and host ownership
facts.value: Existing dedicated-server volumes live on the host/K3s storage environment; an additional disk can be mounted at the documented storage path. Rented host/disk is deleted after expiry; user-owned hardware remains.

facts.label: Databases and support services
facts.value: Templates/container services include PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis and other app-supporting software; variables connect them to app services.

facts.label: PostgreSQL backup compatibility
facts.value: Existing Dev+ database service can use online PostgreSQL backup with pg_dumpall, encompassing all databases; daily backup time is configurable in UTC and files are SQL dumps.

facts.label: Production data capacity
facts.value: App and database share the selected host's finite CPU/RAM/disk; registering a minimum host is not a promise it fits B plus a separate 1-GiB PostgreSQL process and platform overhead.

facts.label: Domains and managed TLS
facts.value: Generated zeabur.app addresses and custom domains are documented; dedicated-server migration reference identifies Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 issuance by Zeabur's ingress component.

facts.label: Generated-domain and DNS exit
facts.value: Generated zeabur.app domains and Zeabur-managed server DNS stop working after shutdown. Custom-domain DNS, replacement ingress/TLS and dependent webhook/OAuth URLs must be moved.

facts.label: Purchased-domain transfers
facts.value: New domain purchases are stopped; self-service transfer-out for existing domains is available from the Dashboard.

facts.label: Health and deployment switch
facts.value: Default TCP probe interval 10 seconds, timeout 5 seconds, three failures; custom HTTP health path expects 2xx. Failed new deployment leaves the old serving version for ordinary stateless deployments.

facts.label: Rollback scope
facts.value: Rollback creates a new deployment using a previous successful image; image services can select an old tag. It does not revert variables, volume contents or database migrations.

facts.label: Staging and previews
facts.value: Projects support isolated environments and staging. The migration reference describes PR preview environments as deprecated and identifies the hosted capability as disappearing on closure.

facts.label: Log retention conflict
facts.value: Pricing/plan table states Free 48 hours, Dev seven days, Pro 30 days, Team 90 days. Logging guide instead says previous-instance logs disappear after restart and no long-term storage is provided.

facts.label: Metrics and basic troubleshooting
facts.value: Real-time CPU, memory and inbound/outbound network charts, plus build/runtime log views and application stdout/stderr streaming.

facts.label: Log forwarding edition
facts.value: Pro guide and main pricing associate log forwarding/search with Pro and higher; Free guide broadly says advanced features including forwarding start at Dev.

facts.label: Account authentication and MFA
facts.value: Hosted FAQ describes third-party login; GitHub guide also supports linking an account registered by email. Security policy's enforced two-factor statement refers to employees, not a published customer-MFA contract.

facts.label: Team roles and billing isolation
facts.value: Team has Viewer/Admin roles; Editor is labelled coming soon. Team workspace subscription, payments, invoices and resources are independent of personal workspaces.

facts.label: Variables and access tokens
facts.value: Service variables can be edited and shared/referenced within a project; public API keys can be generated/revoked. Migration guide warns hosted access tokens have whole-account access.

facts.label: October incident and scope
facts.value: Preliminary report says attackers accessed shared clusters, some GCP dedicated servers and the platform database, including stored service variables, account and project information.

facts.label: Incident credential guidance
facts.value: Provider instructs replacing passwords/keys stored on Zeabur even if rotated after August; GCP users are told to check root/SSH access and unrecognized keys. Exposed secrets can still be misused.

facts.label: Security-policy qualifications
facts.value: Security guide says SOC 2 Type II is being pursued, not completed certification, and describes TLS/encryption/network controls; the incident report documents actual control failures and remediation.

facts.label: August customer-data security incident
facts.value: On 2026-08-27 an attacker exploited a user-deployed service, reached Zeabur systems and read part of the production database, including account information and project environment-variable names and values containing API keys, passwords and other credentials.

facts.label: Bound-host requirements
facts.value: Hosted server registration requires one CPU core/2 GB RAM, reachable public IP, SSH and root or passwordless-sudo capability; documented ports include 22/80/443/4222/6443 and 30000–32767.

facts.label: Maintenance and uninstall work
facts.value: Zeabur managed purchased-server maintenance; bound own hosts require owner operation/storage capacity. Removing the old K3s/Zeabur stack can destroy service/volume state, and replacement networking/certificates/build/backup duties need an owner.

facts.label: Separate OSS installation scope
facts.value: OSS team installer requires Linux/systemd on amd64 or arm64, root, at least 4 GiB RAM and 10 GiB free under /var/lib/rancher; smaller personal mode is separately documented.

facts.label: Data and build locations
facts.value: App runtime/volumes follow the selected server, while builds are on separate shared CI and off-site backups are in Zeabur's S3 storage.

facts.label: Privacy scope and named services
facts.value: Privacy policy covers account/usage information, Stripe payments and third-party service disclosures; security docs describe provider infrastructure and platform data stored in MongoDB Atlas.

facts.label: Public DPA and full residency terms
facts.value: A standalone public DPA, complete named subprocessor schedule and all-data residency contract were not found in the checked legal/privacy/security/server/backup pages and official-domain searches.

facts.label: Retention scope conflict
facts.value: Security guide says customer data is kept seven days after account termination before deletion; privacy policy uses necessity/legal retention, and shutdown notice says final shutdown data/export deadlines remain undecided.

facts.label: Backup scope and price
facts.value: Dev+ off-site S3 backups add no backup storage fee under the guide; offline backups cover mounted volume contents only, and online database backups are supported for named engines.

facts.label: Daily retention and export
facts.value: Automatic daily backups run at a selected UTC time and are retained seven days; older files are deleted. Users can download/API-retrieve backups, but direct own-S3 destination is not supported.

facts.label: Restore formats and responsibilities
facts.value: PostgreSQL SQL dumps restore with database tooling; other supported engines use their native formats. File backups restore by uploading/decompressing into the target persistent volume.

facts.label: Backups during shutdown
facts.value: Migration guide says hosted backups disappear too; export them and establish independent backups before server expiry. Rented-server disk data is not kept after deletion.

facts.label: Configuration exit
facts.value: Project exports produce YAML containing deployment/image/source/variable/volume configuration but no database/volume contents; schema is Zeabur-specific.

facts.label: Images, networking and operations exit
facts.value: Mirror or rebuild images; replace push-deploy, registry, internal DNS, generated domains, ingress/certificates, logging/metrics and backup operations before Zeabur dependencies stop.

facts.label: Machine ownership and deletion
facts.value: Zeabur-rented hosts are in Zeabur's cloud account and are deleted after expiry; bound own hosts remain but require replacing hosted components. Dedicated host access differs from shared-cluster CLI/dashboard-only access.

facts.label: Routine deletion and final deadlines
facts.value: Suspend docs offer a two-hour support-recovery grace after deleting a service, then permanent volume/data removal. Shutdown-specific final data-export/deletion/support dates remain unannounced.

facts.label: Identity and ownership
facts.value: Zeabur hosted deployment platform; operator Zeabur Inc., incorporated in Delaware on 14 January 2025, with the published Newark, Delaware registered address.

facts.label: Separate open-source software
facts.value: A separate official Zeabur OSS site advertises version 0.1.0 and an Apache-2.0 Kubernetes interface running on user infrastructure.

facts.label: Current operating and signup status
facts.value: Winding down. Official 17 October 2026 announcement stops new dedicated-server and domain purchases immediately and sets final dedicated/shared infrastructure shutdown for 31 December 2026.

facts.label: Shutdown schedule
facts.value: From 1 December, dedicated-server renewals are disabled and each server stops on its own expiry date; shared-cluster services pause and can be manually resumed for backup. All rented dedicated servers/shared clusters stop by 31 December.

facts.label: Shared-cluster access already restricted
facts.value: Shared clusters stopped accepting new projects in March 2026 and new services in existing projects on 1 April 2026.

facts.label: Data/export/support deadlines
facts.value: The shutdown announcement says final data-deletion, export-deadline and Zeabur Support closing dates have not been finalized.

facts.label: Discovery-row correction
facts.value: apps.md says Active and describes AI Hub closure as separate; the official October notice winds down the hosting platform itself.

facts.label: Official status and incident history
facts.value: Public status page currently says operational; the October security incident is marked Resolved on 20 October, with the update still stating investigation continues and exposed data can be misused.

facts.label: SLA by edition
facts.value: Free guide explicitly excludes SLA. Enterprise descriptions offer custom SLAs/support; the checked public terms disclaim uninterrupted/error-free service.

facts.label: Full SLA remedies
facts.value: Public credit brackets, outage measurement, claim deadline and complete plan-specific exclusions were not found in pricing/Enterprise descriptions, terms, server or support pages.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Zeabur Support portal and contact@zeabur.com are documented; support handles migration, refund and incident-compensation requests during wind-down.

facts.label: Published first-response targets
facts.value: Price table: standard target four working days; Dev/Pro/Team receive two/five/ten Express passes/month for a guaranteed 36-hour first response during working hours, with a pass returned if missed.

facts.label: Hosted platform license
facts.value: Hosted Zeabur access is governed by proprietary service terms; visibility of zbpack/CLI source is not an open-source license for the hosted control plane or an availability promise.

facts.label: Separate OSS license
facts.value: The separate Zeabur OSS repository has Apache License 2.0, permitting licensed use/modification/distribution subject to notice/license conditions; the site presents self-operated Kubernetes software.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no new sale, full-platform shutdown, rebrand, or qualifying security incident found during this sweep.

facts.label: Core base prices
facts.value: Lightweight US$0/month per project; Serious US$10/month per project. App/database/storage resources are added separately; no feature-tier or seat fee.

facts.label: Billing period and commitment
facts.value: Resources are metered by the minute and charged from credit hourly. Core and dedicated IPv4 renew for calendar-month-length periods starting at activation, paid one month in advance.

facts.label: Tax and upfront cash
facts.value: Prices exclude taxes/fees under terms; minimum manual top-up is US$10 excluding VAT. Applicable VAT is added according to regulation.

facts.label: Refunds and cancellation
facts.value: Core upgrade/deletion refunds unused subscription time pro rata as promo credit. Dedicated IPv4 fee is never refunded; unused paid period can be reused until expiry. Remaining account credit is non-refundable on contract termination.

facts.label: Shared and dedicated CPU
facts.value: Shared CPU costs US$0.60/core/30 days; a physical core is shared with up to ten tenants with variable available power. Dedicated CPU costs US$6/core/30 days and reserves full core capacity.

facts.label: Runtime allocation ranges
facts.value: Current price/scaling references show 1–8 CPU cores, 0.125–48 GB RAM and 1–250 GB disk per runtime container; RAM scaling step is 0.125 GB, disk step 0.5 GB.

facts.label: RAM/disk tariffs
facts.value: RAM US$0.75 per 0.25 GB/30 days, equivalent by our arithmetic to US$3/GB/30 days; disk US$0.05 per 0.5 GB/30 days, equivalent to US$0.10/GB/30 days.

facts.label: Hardware and architecture scope
facts.value: Homepage names AMD EPYC, NVMe storage and ECC RAM; native runtime OS choices are Alpine and Ubuntu, with Docker isolated in VMs.

facts.label: Usage meters
facts.value: CPU, RAM, disk, egress/build/backup overages and object storage are separately metered; core and dedicated IPv4 are subscriptions. Each service's containers add resource costs.

facts.label: Precision and debit timing
facts.value: Usage is calculated down to the minute and deducted hourly. Promo credit is spent first; recurring subscription renewals can take the balance below zero.

facts.label: Ongoing free component
facts.value: Lightweight core repeats with 15 build hours/month, 100 GB egress/month and 5 GB backup storage. App CPU/RAM/disk remain chargeable.

facts.label: Free and promo retention restrictions
facts.value: Terms permit discretionary suspension of promo-only users and automatic data deletion on the 14th calendar day after suspension; account access may also be blocked after over six months' inactivity.

facts.label: At included quota limits
facts.value: Extra egress/build/backup usage is billable at the published overage rates. Daily-spend notification is not automatic project shutdown.

facts.label: Egress included and excess
facts.value: Lightweight includes 100 GB/project/month; Serious 3 TB/project/month. Excess transfer out of the project costs US$0.02/GB.

facts.label: Private and cross-project network
facts.value: Same-project services communicate by hostname on an isolated VXLAN network; different projects require public access rather than shared private networking.

facts.label: Transfer edge cases
facts.value: Explicit inbound, same-project database and CDN allowance/exemption accounting beyond the generic project-egress definition was not located.

facts.label: Build allowance and overage
facts.value: Lightweight: 15 build hours/month; Serious: 150 hours/month. Extra build time US$0.50 per 15 hours. Build container CPU/RAM/disk are not separately charged.

facts.label: Build machine and duration
facts.value: Temporary build container: CPU 1–5 cores, 8 GB RAM, disk 1–100 GB; entire pipeline has a one-hour time limit including debug pauses.

facts.label: Build/deployment concurrency
facts.value: A current numerical per-account/per-project parallel-build limit or deployment-count quota was not found in pipeline, pricing, import or terms.

facts.label: IP addresses and gateway charges
facts.value: Dedicated IPv4 is US$3/project/month; dedicated IPv6 and shared IPv4 are free. Custom-domain TLS and the documented L7 balancer are included.

facts.label: Storage and observability extras
facts.value: Object storage US$0.02/GB/30 days; backup overage US$0.50/5 GB; extra self-hosted ELK/Prometheus/Grafana components consume normal resources.

facts.label: Daily project budget
facts.value: A configured daily spending limit sends an email warning when reached; project services keep running. Threshold resets at midnight UTC.

facts.label: Automatic payment controls
facts.value: Optional auto top-up uses a chosen balance threshold, US$10–US$10,000 payment amount and UTC-calendar-month automatic-payment limit; the last payment is reduced to meet that limit.

facts.label: Insufficient balance and residual costs
facts.value: Billing docs say Zerops may stop exhausted-credit projects, releasing dedicated IPv4 while core remains billable; terms preserve disk charges even when restricted and allow negative balance.

facts.label: Runtime vertical/horizontal scaling
facts.value: Native runtime CPU/RAM/disk can scale within user bounds; containers scale from 1 to 10. Setting matching minimum/maximum pins resources/count. Disk grows but does not shrink in the current scaling guide.

facts.label: Docker scaling conflict
facts.value: Docker guide and early scaling table describe horizontal scaling; later scaling text says VM count changes restart the VM, and current scaling guide explicitly says manual only/no automatic autoscaling.

facts.label: Idle and stopped costs
facts.value: A running runtime has a one-container minimum; no automatic idle sleep/scale-to-zero policy was established. PostgreSQL stop consumes only disk; a stopped project retains core subscription charges.

facts.label: Restart after top-up conflict
facts.value: Terms say service restores after sufficient credit; current billing guide explicitly says a stopped project stays stopped and must be manually started, with IPv4 separately reactivated.

facts.label: Runtime resource/container limit conflict
facts.value: Current marketing says up to 50 runtime containers, while service-specific Node and current scaling/import references state a maximum of ten per service.

facts.label: HTTP payload and connection settings
facts.value: Shared zerops.app subdomain upload cap 50 MB. Custom L7 client_max_body_size defaults 512m, configurable 1k–2048m; connections/worker default 4000, range 1024–65535.

facts.label: Timeout settings and unlisted execution ceiling
facts.value: L7 header/body timeouts default 10s and can range 1s–300s; response send timeout defaults 2s, range 1s–300s. A universal app execution-time/body/concurrency ceiling beyond documented proxy settings was not found.

facts.label: Service counts and identifiers
facts.value: Infrastructure docs say a project can contain unlimited services. Runtime/database hostname is fixed on creation, maximum 25 lowercase ASCII letters/numbers and unique within a project.

facts.label: Signup promotion and card requirement
facts.value: Homepage advertises up to US$65 signup credits; FAQ says starting requires no credit card. Promotional credit is discretionary, not cash or transferable.

facts.label: Promotion expiry and verification
facts.value: A current universal promo expiry, exact staged verification conditions and complete buyer-country/identity-check list were not found in the checked offer, billing, FAQ and terms.

facts.label: Paid funding requirements
facts.value: Terms permit credit-card payments; auto top-ups need a prior manual top-up, saved payment method and billing details. Billing details are required except EU non-VAT users' transactions under US$350.

facts.label: Commercial use by core
facts.value: Terms contract with natural persons, businesses and legal entities and permit serving third parties; Lightweight targets smaller production workloads, Serious production/high availability.

facts.label: Restricted workloads and content
facts.value: Terms prohibit crypto mining, network scanning/attacks, phishing, spam/mass unsolicited email, illegal/infringing content and attempts to bypass resource/network controls.

facts.label: Sensitive personal data restriction
facts.value: DPA inside terms prohibits storing special-category personal data under GDPR Article 9(1).

facts.label: High-consequence operations
facts.value: Terms say the service is not intended for operations where major or serious damage may occur and disclaim responsibility for activity results.

facts.label: Managed system containers
facts.value: Provider operates bare-metal infrastructure and Incus-based full Linux system containers, networking and middleware. Runtime apps remain the builder's responsibility; supported database/storage services are fully managed.

facts.label: Docker hosting mode
facts.value: Docker runs inside dedicated VMs rather than native Incus runtime containers; Docker Compose and prebuilt images are supported with host networking configuration.

facts.label: Lightweight versus Serious core
facts.value: Lightweight puts project controller/routing/firewall/logger/statistics in one container with limited redundancy. Serious separates infrastructure components for high availability.

facts.label: Suitable workloads and overlap
facts.value: Static websites, SSR web apps/APIs, continuous background processes, Docker applications and managed databases/search/brokers/storage are documented.

facts.label: Static hosting behavior
facts.value: Static service serves framework output through preconfigured Nginx with SPA fallback, redirects, headers and CORS. Advanced section also allows a complete custom Nginx file when run.routing is absent.

facts.label: Compute locations
facts.value: Operational status lists EU Central prg1 (Prague), US East ny1 (New York) and US West sea1. Homepage lists the same three plus sgp1 as future/ETA.

facts.label: Delivery network locations
facts.value: CDN docs list Prague (CZ), Falkenstein (DE), London (UK), Sydney (AU), Singapore (SG) and Beauharnois (CA); object/static modes are documented.

facts.label: Native runtime families
facts.value: Node.js, PHP, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, Java, Deno, Bun, Elixir and Gleam have published build/runtime bases; catalog also lists Ruby.

facts.label: Published runtime versions
facts.value: Base list names Node 24/22/20/18, Python 3.14 Ubuntu-only/3.12/3.11, PHP 8.5/8.4/8.3/8.1, .NET 10/9/8/7/6 and Java 21/17.

facts.label: OS/base selection
facts.value: Alpine and Ubuntu bases support system package customization. Current guide names Ubuntu 26.04, 24.04 and 22.04; Deno needs Ubuntu. Explicit OS prefixes avoid differing legacy defaults.

facts.label: Pinned OS versions and aliases
facts.value: Base table lists ubuntu@26.04 and ubuntu@24.04, while ubuntu@latest is explicitly an alias for 22.04. The current selection guide also describes Ubuntu 26.04.

facts.label: Framework and SSR deployment
facts.value: Static output uses Nginx; SSR/API apps run continuous runtime processes. Production guide gives Laravel, Symfony, Django, Node, Spring and Phoenix settings.

facts.label: Advanced Next.js/adapter matrix
facts.value: No complete current Next.js version/ISR/shared-cache/edge-middleware/streaming compatibility matrix found in official runtime, pipeline, framework-related production and networking references.

facts.label: Git deployments and source access
facts.value: Native GitHub and GitLab integrations authorize repository access, install webhooks and trigger on branch push or tags/regex; organization access can be authorized.

facts.label: CLI, artifacts, API and configuration
facts.value: CLI can upload source/build or deploy prebuilt artifacts; GUI can trigger pipelines. Import/export YAML provisions services; zerops.yaml describes build/run. API/integration tokens enable custom automation.

facts.label: Docker input
facts.value: Prebuilt container images and Docker Compose run in the Docker VM service; image tags should be pinned because cached prepare steps do not automatically pull a changed latest tag.

facts.label: Long-running workers
facts.value: Runtime services can use custom continuous startup processes; the catalog and production patterns support separate app/API/worker roles without requiring a public HTTP endpoint.

facts.label: Scheduled commands
facts.value: run.crontab uses five-field cron timing, with once-per-minute example; jobs run in one container by default or all containers when allContainers is true.

facts.label: Job execution ceilings
facts.value: A universal cron execution timeout, retry policy and guaranteed exactly-once dispatch were not published in cron, pipeline, scaling, pricing or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Public HTTP, ports and private access
facts.value: Custom-domain HTTP/HTTPS, private project networking, VPN/SSH and direct public TCP/UDP are documented. Direct ports 10–65435, with 80/443 reserved, apply to runtime and PostgreSQL access.

facts.label: WebSockets and streaming controls
facts.value: Release note explicitly exposes WebSocket support; L7 config permits connection/timeouts and disabling response buffering for real-time APIs.

facts.label: Outgoing firewall
facts.value: UDP has no listed restrictions; outbound TCP 1–1024 allows only 22, 53, 80, 123, 443 and 587; TCP 1025–65535 is unrestricted in the firewall guide.

facts.label: Address persistence and exit
facts.value: Project has one dedicated IPv6; optional one dedicated IPv4 costs US$3/month and can change after release/reactivation. Exhausted-credit stop releases IPv4.

facts.label: Ordinary runtime files
facts.value: Runtime disk survives restart/reload/stop-start, but deploys and container replacement discard writes; replicas have independent filesystems.

facts.label: Local persistent storage
facts.value: Local Storage is a separately managed persistent volume, mounted into same-project runtime services/containers on the same physical host with local POSIX locking/mmap semantics.

facts.label: Storage choices and restrictions
facts.value: Object Storage is S3-compatible; SeaweedFS is an HA-capable network filesystem with caveats, unsuitable for databases needing local locking. A runtime can mount at most one Local Storage volume.

facts.label: Managed supporting services
facts.value: PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Valkey/KeyDB, search engines, vector search, NATS/Kafka, ClickHouse and storage are listed managed service types.

facts.label: PostgreSQL versions and deployment modes
facts.value: Current PostgreSQL docs list 18.1, 17.7, 16.11 and 14.20. Single mode has one node; HA uses three nodes on separate machines and automatic failover. Mode is immutable after creation.

facts.label: PostgreSQL resource/connection controls
facts.value: Resource limits/profile can be changed; memory-step transitions can trigger restarts. Internal primary port 5432 is plaintext, replica 5433 HA-only; pooled 6432 requires TLS.

facts.label: Custom domains and HTTPS
facts.value: Custom-domain routing and automatic free Let's Encrypt certificate issuance/renewal are documented; IPv6 is included, IPv4 can be shared or paid dedicated.

facts.label: Wildcard domain and CDN scope
facts.value: Custom wildcard domains and automatic certificates are supported using an _acme-challenge CNAME to Zerops' zone. Static CDN explicitly cannot be enabled for wildcard domains.

facts.label: Release and readiness controls
facts.value: New native containers start and pass configured readiness before replacing old ones by default; temporaryShutdown true stops old containers first and causes downtime.

facts.label: Readiness timing disagreement
facts.value: Pipeline reference describes five-second retries and five-minute failure; dedicated health guide says no fixed schema default and requires explicit failureTimeout/retryPeriod duration strings.

facts.label: Rollback scope
facts.value: Ten recent application versions are retained; artifacts can be downloaded and old versions reactivated. Environment variables restore to the selected version's last-active state.

facts.label: Preview environments
facts.value: Separate projects support dev/stage/prod. Official GitHub lifecycle reference automates branch/PR projects and cleanup, but is a user-owned workflow rather than a Zerops-managed preview service.

facts.label: Logs and exports
facts.value: Project logger collects build, runtime-prepare, runtime and database logs. CLI/GUI views and syslog forwarding to external vendors or own ELK are documented.

facts.label: Current logging architecture
facts.value: May 2026 article describes per-project VictoriaLogs, Vector, syslog-ng and a compatibility proxy, replacing an older custom SQLite logger.

facts.label: Monitoring and retained history
facts.value: Resource/container scaling history is visible; optional Prometheus/Grafana/ELK/tracing setups are documented. A fixed current default runtime/build-log and metric-history retention duration was not found.

facts.label: Account protection
facts.value: March 2026 release note documents FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys, hardware-key/biometric support, TOTP two-factor authentication and reauthentication for sensitive settings.

facts.label: Roles and tokens
facts.value: Owner/Admin/Developer/Guest roles and per-project Full/Read-only overrides; integration tokens are constrained by creator permissions and can be scoped per project.

facts.label: Secrets and environment isolation
facts.value: Service secret variables, build/runtime variables and project variables are distinct. Default service isolation limits automatic cross-service visibility; explicit references and sharing rules can grant access.

facts.label: Sensitive-variable feature wording
facts.value: RBAC table describes redacted sensitive variables for read-only users, but the same page labels marking variables sensitive/encrypted as Coming Soon.

facts.label: Published kernel security advisory
facts.value: May 1, 2026 Copy Fail advisory says shared-kernel Zerops was affected by CVE-2026-31431, all regions were patched, and no action was required for Zerops customers.

facts.label: Self-host installation requirement
facts.value: No customer control-plane installation is required for the managed Platform mode. Provider manages infrastructure; users manage code, data/configuration and application dependencies.

facts.label: Control-plane outage behavior
facts.value: March release note says project L3/L7/network infrastructure is independent of Zerops' control plane and keeps working when parts of that plane fail.

facts.label: Public data-processing agreement
facts.value: Terms Article 13 is a DPA: user is controller, Zerops processor; documented instructions, confidentiality, subprocessor flow-down and assistance/audits are described.

facts.label: Privacy retention and international transfers
facts.value: Privacy policy keeps business-partner data for cooperation plus ten years, IP/web traffic up to two years unless incidents require longer. Transfers outside EU/EEA require recognized GDPR safeguards.

facts.label: All-data residency scope
facts.value: A complete named subprocessor list and contractual per-data-type location matrix for apps, builds, logs, backups and support were not found in terms, privacy, regional, storage and backup docs.

facts.label: Backup schedule and supported data
facts.value: Daily automatic backups default to 00:00–01:00 UTC; custom daily/weekly/monthly/cron schedules and manual backups are available for supported databases and storage.

facts.label: Retention and quotas
facts.value: Defaults keep at least seven daily, four weekly and three monthly backups; configurable total maximum defaults to 50/service. Project technical backup limit is 1 TiB; oversized new backup is not stored.

facts.label: Backup cost and encryption
facts.value: Lightweight includes 5 GB, Serious 25 GB; excess is US$0.50/5 GB. Backups use a per-project X25519 key and separate storage; source says raw backups are inaccessible to staff.

facts.label: Download and restore
facts.value: Download backups and use service-specific tools. PostgreSQL backup ZIP contains per-schema pg_dump custom-format dumps, restored with pg_restore rather than plain psql.

facts.label: Backup versus legal responsibility
facts.value: Docs describe automatic supported-service backups; terms say backups/data-loss responsibility is not assumed unless otherwise agreed and recommend users keep their own backups.

facts.label: Deletion recovery window
facts.value: Backup guide keeps deleted-service/project backups seven days; project encryption key is permanently destroyed after seven days, making remaining backup data unrecoverable.

facts.label: Source/configuration/artifact exit
facts.value: Keep source in own Git; project/service configuration exports as Zerops YAML. Ten recent application artifacts can be downloaded.

facts.label: Data and domain exit
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports SQL/custom-format export/import; backups are downloadable. S3-compatible data uses its API; custom-domain DNS can be repointed to another host.

facts.label: Termination and data removal
facts.value: Contract is indefinite with 30-day notice termination; provider may delete stored data on termination. Insufficient credit not replenished causes automatic live-data deletion on the 14th day after restriction.

facts.label: Product and operator
facts.value: Zerops Platform, operated by Zerops s.r.o., Czech Republic, ID 21275602; registered office Varšavská 715/36, Prague–Vinohrady.

facts.label: Earlier shutdown and ownership change
facts.value: Original vshosting/Contabo-group project stopped at the end of 2022. Original developers acquired the IP and relaunched independently in 2024; About specifies June 2024.

facts.label: Current operating and signup status
facts.value: Active public managed-platform offer with registration, paid resource pricing and three operational compute regions; no current full-platform shutdown/sunset notice found in the official sources searched.

facts.label: Component deprecation
facts.value: Shared Storage is deprecated; existing services were converted in place to SeaweedFS. The old automatic mount path is best-effort and will be removed in a later release, with no date stated.

facts.label: Other product editions
facts.value: Homepage presents Platform, Mate and Box; Mate/Box are labelled Soon there, while Box service docs describe an available beta without an SLA.

facts.label: Current status and history
facts.value: Official status reports all services online, including API/dashboard and prg1/ny1/sea1 compute/storage. October 27 billing maintenance is shown in recent history.

facts.label: Public SLA details
facts.value: No current general plan-specific numeric uptime commitment, service-credit brackets and full claims schedule located in current pricing, infrastructure/support docs or Zerops' own terms.

facts.label: Availability exclusions and claims
facts.value: Terms describe planned maintenance averaging two hours/month with unused time carryover, third-party/network/power/DoS exclusions and written failure complaint within 24 hours.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Official docs recommend Discord; email support@zerops.io, issue reporting and social contact are published. Security/abuse contacts are separately listed.

facts.label: Response guarantee and enterprise support
facts.value: Pricing offers enterprise premium support by sales contact, but public standard support hours/timezone, guaranteed response/resolution time and premium prices were not found.

facts.label: Hosted platform license
facts.value: Self-host platform software licensing is not applicable to this managed service record; access/use is governed by Zerops terms.
